replies.author: Francisco  (he/him/his)
replies.text: The difference is how you play. Outside of haste, buffs have a VERY small impact on dps. Players give them an outsized amount of attention. Compare what spells he is using, what upgrade level, how fast he casts them. Many people cast slow. Any time not spent casting is wasted dps. If you take 1 extra second between each spell, that end up being many casts over a fight you miss

replies.author: Sarion
replies.text: This might help you. I play Mage, instead of Necro - but its really the Ranger/Shaman buff stacking that's an issue. Most of your Necro buffs you can use along with the others - except the Shielding line which you're better off ignoring and using Ranger/Shaman alternatives.

replies.author: Sarion
replies.text: Upgrading buffs only extends their duration, it does not increase their potency. They might be using some alchemy potions along with the buffs, but most of the Dex probably comes from focusing almost entirely on Dex/Wis gear and upgrading it all to +10. How much the extra Dex would increase your damage likely depends on how much you currently have. It definitely helps, but it takes a lot of Dex to get big increase in DPS. What are your DoT's leveled to? Getting those to Rank VIII - X is going to be more substantial than your Dex. Same with your bow and arrow - get those to +10.

Did a few tests while at work between jobs. 

Two with NO gear besides bow, arrow and quiver
Both 104 DEX & 318 ATK
31:02 & 20:36 duration
186 & 173 DPS
15% & 14% crit
77% & 75% accuracy
35-2.1K damage range
4 & 5 Double Attack %

replies.author: PsychoDad

replies.author: PsychoDad
replies.text: The AVG hits for the controls were 787 & 755, missed that .

replies.author: PsychoDad
replies.text: Normal gear, only change was a DEX potion. 207 DEX 478 ATK 22:50 duration 296 DPS 19% crit 77% accuracy 35-2.1K damage range 861 AVG hit 4 Double Attack % .

replies.author: PsychoDad
replies.text: Normal gear, Boon of the Garou only. 282 DEX 508 ATK 21:56 duration 292 DPS 20% crit 72% accuracy 145-2.1K damage range 935 AVG 2 Double Attack % .

replies.author: PsychoDad
replies.text: One of the things that stands out to me is the DEX potion alone didn’t increase the minimum hit but Boon did. I don’t think that’s tied to ATK because naked vs geared the min was still 35. Also the AVG seemed to go up with the only addition being DEX. The accuracy being lower on the Boon test is odd. The crit going up was also odd cause it went up on both buffed tests but not naked to geared. So a read of just these is screaming there’s breakpoints to me rather than linear increases with stats.

replies.author: Exzeph
replies.text: Can you test to see if STR has any effect at all on Bow hits?

replies.author: PsychoDad
replies.text: I didn’t do a STR only buff but buffing STR also buffs ATK so I’d say yes, STR buffs bow damage.

replies.author: Exzeph
replies.text: are you sure tho haha because on the statistic sheet you can only ever see the ATK stat for your primary weapon in other words currently there is no way to see the ATK stat of a weapon in the Range slot

replies.author: PsychoDad
replies.text: ATK is ATK. it is the stat used for every attack that goes against AC as I understand. It applies to both melee and ranged. Now, melee and ranged both have additional modifiers besides of course. But my bet would be any way you can raise your ATK on your sheet will benefit your damage.

replies.author: Krayte
replies.text: When I tested str back near launch I found no parseable difference. Used the buff values of shm strength + bards lvl 45 haste to get near 510, without it was around 400 str, made 0 difference whereas changes in dex did make a difference. Bow accuracy and atk isn't tied to character sheet accuracy and attack, (eagle eye buff on ranger shows no change to character sheet acc but does show a parseable increase in accuracy) but having said that a lots changed since and this week's patch may have affected it

replies.author: Exzeph
replies.text: What I am trying to tell you is that it is currently not possible to see the sheet damage of your Ranged slot and the ATK stat you see on your sheet is actually just the Primary weapon atk

replies.author: Sarion
replies.text: Adding +100 STR with no change in Dex boosted the ATK shown on the inventory UI and resulted in absolutely no change in bow damage. Also, I am pretty sure the ATK shown in the inventory is based on level, weapon skill for your main hand weapon, and strength plus raw ATK bonuses from buffs and AAs. It would be weird if my bow damage was based on whether I am any good with the 1h blunt weapon in my main hand. And likewise, my skill with archery has no effect on that number. I don't think there's good reason to assume that ATK number means anything for your off hand or ranged weapons at all.

replies.author: Cyanide Bunnyslayer
replies.text: Focuses do not benefit the pet. They still benefit from most stats (except for STA, WIS and INT) If a pet can equip a weapon, they will benefit from the stats and any procs. However the auto attack damage won't go up unless the weapon is a better damage/delay ratio than the pet's native damage/delay. For a max level warder at +10 rank, that magic ratio is > 31/28 right now

replies.text: Because of what Cyanide pointed out, you might still be better off with the earthshaker for now. However, the earthshaker would have a delay of 1.06, which isn't as good as your pets. Therefore, it will use the damage of the weapon, since it is so much higher than the pets, and not the delay which will give you a significantly higher ratio than with the fiery defender. replies.author: Sarion
replies.text: The problem is the UI. The ATK listed in the UI is exclusively your main hand ATK. Nowhere in the game shows your off hand or ranged melee attack. However, spells and AAs that increase pure ATK are applied to all 3. So they absolutely help off-hand and Ranged hits. Strength increases Main and Off hand ATK (specifically offense, not accuracy - your hits land in the higher end of damage distribution with higher strength vs enemy mitigation AC). Dexterity does the same thing for ranged attacks that Strength does for melee attacks. There's just no way to see that number in game.

replies.author: Sarion

1550121960447414302.title: I am addicted to Evasive Stance... alternatives?
1550121960447414302.report:
I pair my ENC/CLR (my must-have classes) with a MNK. Most of my DPS comes from a hasted+buffed charmed pet using Allure +10, Swift Like The Wind, Garou, proc'ing weapons, etc.

I have created a macro so, when charm breaks, I automatically re-target the former pet, go into Evasive Stance, go into OverChannel Invocation, and re-cast Allure. Evasive buys me the time to re-cast Allure under OverChannel (slow casting) instead of Inversion (fast casting), which in return helps charm last much longer. Charming under OverChannel makes a big difference in my experience.

Here is the conundrum: I want to switch MNK for a tankier class, such as SHD or WAR, but neither of them have Evasive. I have tried re-casting Allure under OverChannel without Evasive, and when a D4 mob + a hasted charmed pet are beating on you, interrupts do happen despite having all the necessary channeling and anti-stun AAs.

I have tried the ENC's Trickster AA, but it doesnt work very well I have also tried switching the MNK for a BRD (since BRD also have Evasive), but I dont have enough spell gems for ENC, CLR and BRD.

In short: I am stuck with MNK due to Evasive.

Any suggestion? Thank you!

replies.author: Boisterous
replies.text: As far as songs go I would drop psalm of warmth and run elemental rhythms. Make sure you have a drum exalt equipped. This will help with his big DD spells. Put largos melodic in your SA - the slow is 35 percent which is almost double Selos chain. You should put some motes in it to make sure it doesn't get resisted all the time. Mine is at 9, but you can probably get it to about 4 and be ok. You should probably toss a HoT on yourself and then only use drain soul as your main source of healing. If you mote it up it will lifetap for around 700hp. Even at level 5 it will be a significant improvement and nearly unresistable. So basically debuff, using over channel put your dots up, switch to inversion and lifetap the hell out of him. As the poster above says, some runs of the planes for gear will make a huge difference. As you get more AC, you take less damage, which means evasive stance uses less endurance, which means you don't run out as quickly, which means you don't have to spam heals or sit in channeler stance.

replies.author: Boisterous
replies.text: As far as SA songs, you get marginal gains by running all three regens vs cantata. (I think it's plus 2 mana/endurance to run all three) Id recommend you run cantata for Regen, largos melodic bunding, elemental rhythms, guardian rythms, Jonathan's war song (lvl 45 I think). It should cap your haste, slow Innoruk, buff your resistances, and still give you decent regen. If it turns out you're running out of endurance or mana specifically, swapping that specific regen song might be worth it. The alternate path is full turtle, where you just keep yourself alive and put up all your aoe dots and your single target chants, switching from channeler to evasive and just trying to dot him up, keep the per charmed, and outlast him. I can give more specifics if that's the route you go, but I think you'll get it with a charmed pet and some motes into drain soul, tbh

BRD/SHD/DRU may be a stronger option. But if you really want to do BRD/NEC/DRU, I would "personally" recommend trying: -Keep your pet (upgraded to at least rank 8, so it is level 49... but if you get it to rank 10 it will be better than lvl 50 charmed pet if utilizing heavy hitting WAR weapons, as the pet ignores weapon delays at rank 10 and treats every weapon as if it has a base delay of 30 (if you use savage spirit's 70% haste, with a +10 earthshaker that's a 74/18 weapon on a rank 10 pet). Charmed pet is nice, but if you're struggling to survive already, 1 charm break/resist at the wrong time is likely match over, and it will likely take more than 2-4 charms to defeat him. (Savage spirit is better than augment death at this level too). -Balance your endurance regen between evasive and balanced stance (and divine invocation) when you have to heal... -Balance your mana regen between Recovery and Divine Invocation based on if your are missing HP or not will make your taps much more mana efficient. (Neither of these would be an issue with SHD just sitting in defensive and spell blade stance). -Use upgraded Largo's Melodic Binding in your SA (over Consonant Chain or even Cessation). -If solo, use Jon's Provocation over Melody of Ervaj in your SA. -Level up vamp embrace (this is literally 214% stronger on the SHD (with bloodmoon), but still very nice as a BRD/NEC)

1547982037644746762.title: Calling all Druid experts
1547982037644746762.report:
I had a discussion in theory crafting about end game Druid and its power ability. It seemed the general consensus was that Druid was not sleeper in any way shape or form and underperforming. 

But I believe these guys haven’t spent the hours on Druid that you may have. So those that have put in the hours, gear and aa, and have also played other specs like wizard shaman and necro etc. is it true there’s no hidden value or class combo people are sleeping on, no unique abilities like the lightning aoe line, no game mechanics that can make Druid feel strong relative to the other classes? Let me know your thoughts!

replies.author: Auronnj Jay
replies.text: When Im leveling other classes I pretty much always use druid for the DS and the heals. So it's one of my most used classes from 1-46, then I swap to bard

replies.author: Retired8404
replies.text: For the most part, that flower heal thing is dope af. Very underrated. DS..also underrated and underused. If a mob is gonna smack you and they will, make them pay for it.

replies.author: Mug_O_Tea
replies.text: DS feels bad because ranking does nothing. But druid is exceptional for PoS for example. Harmony is great. You can charm bees and destroy as well as an enchanter. Your charmed bee gets the most powerful pet buff as far as I'm aware (not that it matters cos you can gear your pet) Hot lines are strong. I'm actually working on an aoe concept right now that is going to use Druid because of the lightning blast. Not sure how well it'll work but will drop feedback. Starfire is fairly ok a nuke. Dots are actually pretty when compared to a shaman. Like I'm pretty sure a puma on shaman and pet is WAY more damage overall than all 3 druid dots combined Like. The only thing druid really has as a "boon" is harmony and a very slightly higher damage nuke. But when you compare said nuke to wizard and wizard crit. It's meh and when you compare the AOE to bard it's cheap..... But next to useless. Half the targets. Long cast time. Short recharge but... Offset by a 6s cast. Considerably less damage.

replies.author: Labradorian77
replies.text: The Druid magic dot gets very few resists even before moteing. Back classic eq I leveled a Druid solo root rotting and quad kiting. While not an over powered class, they have some useful tools that makes a good addition for leveling if not endgame.

replies.author: Sparks
replies.text: I think the thing that made Druid so powerful in regular classic is what makes it weaker in EQL. It can do a lot of different things pretty well, but not as well as more specialized classes (can nuke, but not as well as a Wiz or Mage, can heal but not as well as a Cleric, can DoT and buff, but not as well as a Shaman, etc). Since we can be three classes at once, there's less value in a jack-of-all trades once you hit end game. I agree with others though that it's a great leveling class, and of course ports are dope.

replies.author: Katlie
replies.text: It’s the range of tools as much as the depth. When AAs are also considered, you have instant inviz, instant Evac, +spell crit chance (free AAs). Harmony of Nature does not need upgrading (already works on mobs up to 65). Also doesn’t fall off randomly like Pacify, unless I’ve just been very lucky with it. Wolf Form adds +ATK, runspeed and Ultravision and you can click off the illusion (unlike Boon of the Garou - I thought my enchanter was going to be a human female, how wrong I was! Rawwwr! Rawwrrr!) Decent +STR buffs. Joint best pet buff with BST. Charm for situational use (Vox, Sky, PoF) if needed. Tracking is the thing I probably miss the most when I don’t have DRU. It’s minor, but it’s also nice to be able to port quickly from a spell since the menu is better organised than the Rituals tab. Better than SHM? Of course not. More flexible? For sure. More fun? Definitely. What other class debuffs FR by nuking!

replies.author: Mug_O_Tea
replies.text: You love Ice lol

replies.author: Katlie

replies.author: JustinGayme.TTV
replies.text: While I appreciate the discussion, ultimately I think in this type of game it’s worth repeating that there really shouldn’t be any thought of a sleeper trio etc. By all means if we are discussing min maxing, game on! But when it comes to playing, play as you wish. I have Druid in my lineup simply for their versatile aa’s (crit). Cleric actually played way smoother instead of Druid in my trio (I play wizard/enchanter/) but I stilll keep Druid just for the crit aa. So yea I’m probably slowing my min max rate but I like that juicy crit Now onto your question: I do think Druidgenerally underperforms from a min max perspective. In a trio they don’t really offer anything that other classes dont (and on its own every class can do what they do but better. They offer damage shields sure but again since discussing maxing, the damage shields are negligible at the rate stuff dies. The only hard reasons I can think of why to slot Druid (from min max perspective) is if you’re a heavy wisdom trio, and trying to keep 3 wisdom classes for certain invocations. They do have a few noteworthy unique buffs. Great wolf form can be mass cast to a raid, and indoors. It’s faster than other speed buffs (except mount) and you can even click off the visual of the wolf and keep the speed buff if ya wanted.) TLDR; in min maxing Druid does seem to underperform, but they hav a few things worth slotting them for if it suits your playstyle or fun.

1547304603140366346.title: Sharing pet equipment with a loadout
1547304603140366346.report:
I have my air pet using my Indicolite armor. When I swap to a different non-mage loadout with my warrior, it loads the armor. When I swap back to mage, instead of the equipment going back into the pet inventory, it's dumped into my Equipment or inventory storage.

Any ideas how to fix this? Or is this a known issue?

replies.author: Anachrony
replies.text: Yes, I have problems with this too. It doesn't seem to save pet equipment as part of a loadout, but it really should. Pets can use equipment that matches the class of the character, and have different classes of their own depending on what type of pet they are. So that alone is plenty of reason that the equipment is totally different between layouts. But also you may want to emphasize different stats based on whether they're a tank pet, DPS pet, or charmed. It's annoying to have to manually fix the pet equipment every time you change loadouts. It becomes doubly chaotic to manage if the pet from one loadout uses the same equipment as the character in another loadout.

replies.author: Anachrony
replies.text: Similarly, there are problems managing exaltation slots between loadouts. Certain exaltations might impose extra class requirements or compete with other exaltations that are better for some classes than others. So it's often necessary to swap out exaltations based on loadout. Or sometimes you want the same exaltation in the same slot, but the loadout has a different item in that slot. It seems like any time you move around exaltations it doesn't save and restore them properly, so you have to manually adjust it every time you swap loadouts. It's very annoying to manage since it takes a lot of time to figure out the best exaltations for each slot and go through every slot and try to remember what belongs there.

replies.author: Nalthien
replies.text: Two really important things to know about the EQLegends tools "BiS finder" tool. I want to say first that it's a very valuable tool; but, the defaults are...wonky. First, it tries to optimize for the stats you select. It attempts to have default stat weights (how much it values each stat) but they aren't great. Second, it *seems* to optimize piece by piece at times which means that weird things happen such as: choosing to only value STR and then your STR goes down when it selects pieces when you hit the auto button. The most important thing is that it will give you a good starting point.

replies.text: Honestly this game is so easy that optimizing the perfect setup isn't neccessary. I prefer to upgrade gear useable by multiple trios to +8, then drop 2 VTM into it and be done, at least at this point in the expansion. Class specific weapons and strong items like SK sky shield being the exception. As for general gearing, I tend to value resists as it allows you to ignore some annoyances and offers magic mitigation, so for example I use double rainbow hues shield in ANY slot, and it's not like you have to gimp your ac/hp/mana. For the neck, Kerran necklace is fine if you like it and fine if you don't; I don't use it for bossing or mote farming, but I do for levelling a new class. Doesn't matter either way. As sk/wiz/enc you will have to OOC regen occasionally, so I don't mind spending some extra tics regenning mana. Now if you are doing a DDD build, then gearing and BiS lists suddenly becomes very important. Pump up that mana as high as you can and stack resists. It allows bigger pulls and can be the difference between finishing a pull or clicking the release button.

1545361491287613480.title: Slow: ENC vs SHM
1545361491287613480.report:
In theory, at the highest level of their respective Slow lines, the ENC version is supposed to be only 5% less than the SHM version. However, when I play my lvl 50 SHM mobs seem to swing visibly less often than when I play my lvl 50 ENC. I havent done any parsing, so I cannot validate it.

Can anyone confirm that the difference is only 5% please?

replies.author: Janus (Tashan - Neriak Server)
replies.text: It's is 5%. Amerzel spell data shows this as well and was the case back in the day. Keep in mind other factors like haste ojn mobs, some have it, some dont and differential attack speeds based on difficulty of zones. It's the same in Kunark with Enchanter hitting 70% slow and Shaman hitting 75%. There's a reason for this and it was that Enchanters are ment to fill the gap in debuffing in other ways. They share the Incapacitate lines but only Enchanter has the Weakness and Gasping Embrace line. They were meant to be stacked. Weakness and Gasping Embrace ends up netting a 3-6% dmg reduction on mob output depending.

replies.author: branar
replies.text: As Janus says it's 5%. It is worth noting that the way the calculation is done means 5% can create a difference detectable to the "naked eye" even without parsing. The calculation is new attack delay = base attack delay / (1 - slow percentage) As an example, with 2.0 seconds between attacks, shiftless deeds@level 50 and 55% power puts mobs attacking once every ~4.44 seconds. togors@level 50 and 60% power puts mobs attacking once every 5.0 seconds. You can absolutely feel a half-second difference if you're paying attention -- and while I can't remember the attack speed of classic mobs, I think their base attack delay might actually even be 3 seconds, not 2? That means almost a full second of difference in final attack delay between the two slows.

replies.author: Janus (Tashan - Neriak Server)
replies.text: Yup, 0.84 second difference if 3

replies.author: Janus (Tashan - Neriak Server)
replies.text: 3.2 second difference from Bard Slow to use another reference

replies.author: PorkSocks
replies.text: When you have a calculation like this, every extra percent is more effective than the last percent. If one class had a 98% slow and another had 99, the 99 would take half as many remaining attacks. If you got to 100 obviously you would never be attacked at all. Single percents matter. 5% matters quite a bit. This effect becomes even more pronounced with the higher level versions of slow to come.

replies.author: Koh Phi Phi
replies.text: I dont follow: how does going from 98% to 98% halve down the number of attacks?

replies.author: Jurian
replies.text: Think about it this way. Let’s say a mob throws 100 attacks normally. When 98% slowed, only 2 attacks would happen in the same timeframe. When 99% slowed… it’s now just 1 attack. Thats a 50% reduction. Think of it like… diminishing returns, in reverse.

replies.author: PorkSocks
replies.text: Also I said 99 to 98. Not 98 to 98, which is obviously no difference.

replies.author: Sinbbus
replies.text: Another thing to take note of, is SHM gets the better slow, enc gets the better haste. Both have pros and cons.

replies.author: Monte
replies.text: Comparing the difference of 98% vs 99% are not relevant to the game because we are not working with those numbers. Look at numbers in a fight. Using the numbers here: 2.0 sec delay means in 1min (60sec) fight the mob attacks 15 times with a ench slow (50%) vs 13.5 times with Shaman slow. To answer the the original question: if the mob have a low delay atk like 1 or 2 sec then it could be visible. At 3 sec in 60 sec fight the difference is one attack 9 vs 10 swings. Is my math correct ? Btw the difference between swings holds later at 70% vs 75% because again the variation is 5%

replies.author: Janus (Tashan - Neriak Server)
replies.text: "...with ench slow (50%)..." Ench slow is 55%, 60% for Shaman. He was using the extreme example to demonstrate how slows are calculated. Slow is a function of how Haste is applied but the inverse. This is why when Enchanter gets 70% slow in Kunark and Shaman has 75%, you're going to see something magical. Bard increases from 30% to 35% and Beastlord from 40% to 50%.

replies.author: Janus (Tashan - Neriak Server)
replies.text: This is in particular why I write off anything below 50%. Generally the fall off is 58%.

replies.author: PorkSocks

1545278224139948052.title: RNG/X/X - Ranged DPS, Solo Capable, Not Hot Garbage - Complimentary Classes?
1545278224139948052.report:
Hey all! Stuck in a loop of analysis paralysis...help!

I read through most of the posts here before posting but wanted the opinion of some experts. I am planning to start a ranged DPS focused RNG and I am having a hell of a time deciding which 2x other classes to pick and would GREATLY appreciate any and all advice/experiences.

I was considering RNG/NEC/CLR possibly? Plate/heals from CLR obviously, dots/pet/FD/lifetaps from necro, weave in bow shots between dot casts? Maybe the CLR is overkill given I have NEC lifetaps?

Or possibly RNG/MAG/X - I have been reading the MAG pet can be quite good for a ranged DPS ranger possibly? Does it bring much else? Not familiar with the cloth/caster classes in EQ.

Or maybe something with RNG/ENCH? Sounds like ENCH would let me charm some great pets, drop aggro to ensure pet keeps aggro so I can ranged attack, has clarity/mana regen, other CC obviously?

Also hearing RNG/BER can be good due to BER stance increasing ranged attack frequency...but would also lose ability to use ranged stance/range attack in melee, so not sure about this one.

Seriously, any advice would be INCREDIBLY appreciated. Thanks in advance!

replies.author: Starch
replies.text: hello. i think your first decision path needs to be whether or not you want to play "ranged DPS" or play "DPS at range", which may not necessarily be the same thing. playing "ranged DPS" absolutely involves using the ranged stance, because you can't fire a bow from melee range otherwise. that eliminates BER from contention for solo play. also, because you will be using ranged stance as your primary stance, it means you need to be tanky enough and have enough sustain to take the hits while in this stance. you'll need access to a slow, and enough mitigation to survive without using evasive/defensive/channeler/etc. for the most part. ENC and SHM are the notable supports here, as is SHD or NEC for sustain options. playing "DPS at range" absolutely involves the use of a pet to tank the boss while you stand away from the boss and shoot, since there's no other way to fight high level enemies without being summoned/tanking/etc. this narrows your choices of class pairings. the best tanking pets are MAG, BST, NEC, and of course charm pets. in both scenarios, i suggest RNG/NEC/SHM as a starting point. you have a reliable, albeit sometimes squishy skeleton pet to tank if you need to step away and fire, and a consistent feign death option to manage aggro. you have access to the best synergy class in the game (SHM) which gives you slow, heals, the best dots in the game, and puma for your pet (and you, if you decide to use melee weapons). you have lifetap for sustain and lich and canni for mana. note that in this loadout, your bow is sort of the cake-topper rather than the cake. most of your damage will come from dots and taps. that said, bow shots between casts is still a respectable addition to dps, and for some bosses, once they are below threshold, you can still get some impressive finishing blow crits (yes, finishing blow works with archery).

replies.author: Exzeph
replies.text: You'll want slow, if a true solo master is your goal. Of the choices you're considering Ber and Mag will both be terrible. Ber brings nothing to the table, yes Berserker stance will marginally overperform ranged stance but that's literally it, that isn't enough to burn one whole class in your trio. Mag is not it either, because pets are in a bad place, sure they're being worked on but it's not enough to take a half promise of a maybe they will be good to fill some important needs in your trio. ENC is decent, it will bring haste and slow and CC -- its meta precisely because it is an enabler. BRD can do some of what ENC does just a bit differently and to differing degrees

replies.author: Adrastia
replies.text: Shaman/Mage could be interesting. All of the buffs, slows and healing from Shaman cannot be understated how good it is. An earth mage pet does make for a solid tank if heavily invested; It won't be as strong as a player tank, but its your best bet right now if you're really going for a ranged playstyle. Keep in mind that both ranged and pet stuff aren't in the best of places right now.. but it should still be functional. Shaman in particular has enough utility to let just about anything work. In theory both ranged and pets are on the radar for buffs eventually, so theres a good chance it'll get better in short order too

replies.author: Sarion
replies.text: Personally, I like RNG/MAG/SHM. Upgraded mage pets are solid tanks, even more solid with Shaman slows. And you've got Shaman heals to keep them up. Toss Mage and Shaman DoTs in between bow shots to conserve mana for healing. Every minute or so, toss a Frenzied Burnout + Puma on your pet. And if you have to, step in to tank with Evasive+Slow while you heal. Also, Mage + Ranger has a fun synergy for tackling challenging dungeons. Rangers get Harmony of Nature at 39 which is a powerful lull spell and you can cast it through walls and other things that break line of sight. Mages get Eye of Zomm, which summons a nonagro eye that you control and see through. Summon the eye, send it into a room full of enemies and safely lull them all from the otherside of the wall and just pull one at a time. Or in Plane of Hate I will use it to pull named mobs I want without their guards, and skip all the trash I don't care about.

replies.author: Aafror

Full suite of dots obviously totals more than ranged but I have been pretty pleased. I still think accuracy is in a tough place but it sort of works with enough gear and AAs I guess. Edit to add using +10 sky bow so other than maxing out a few gear pieces I'm about maxed out.

replies.author: carthorn
replies.text: I second this, you could also do RNG/NEC/SHM, which is also solid, pet is not as good as Earth or Air pet as a tank but can still do the job. You also get more DoT synergy and Taps and FD (though you can also use the Shaman FD ring). replies.author: Riddish
replies.text: Yeah ranger buff stacking is absolute horrible and stupid. I have to do the same nature's precision trick people use for wolf form to use boon of the garou. This is like early beta issues, not paying for 2 months issues.

replies.author: Sarion
replies.text: Are they issues, or intentional though? The "tricks" are actual an exploit to get around the stacking rules. I'm all for being able to stack all my buffs but until the devs say otherwise, I think its safe to assume some of these buffs not stacking is very much intentional, not a bug.

replies.author: Draeth
replies.text: Force of Nature is in the buff line with Firefist and Nature's Precision. The first two both stack normally with the Wolf Form buff line. It's only Force of Nature that requires this stupid workaround. Why exactly would it be an exploit for two buff lines to all stack normally with the exception of one buff from one line?

replies.author: Sarion
replies.text: I don't think it technically is the same spell line. Force of Nature is kind of its own thing. The next spell after Nature's Precision is Call of Predator, I'm pretty sure. But that's all pedantic anyways and not my point. As far as I can tell most, if not all, of the buffs are consistent with how they were in original EQ - apart from some tweaks with Endurance since its so much more important in EQL. Since the developers set Force of Nature to have its Attack bonus in buff slot 3, the same as Wolf Form and Greater Wolf Form (and Garou), back in 2003 - it was probably always the intention for them to not stack. So them still not stacking in 2026 is probably not "broken", and anything that lets you get around it is technically an exploit. If anything the bug should be that Nature's Precision and Force of Nature don't stack. Nature's Precision provides Slot 1 Attack Bonus, and Force of Nature provides a slot 3 Attack bonus - and yet the game blocks them even though they have no overlapping buff slots. Its like if Spikecoat and Skin like Steel didn't stack. None of this is to say they couldn't choose to change it for EQL, and I hope they do - but I'm also doubtful that the devs would even view this as a bug in the first place, so expecting a "fix" is probably the wrong way to approach it.

1544052857534418964.title: Mistwalker PPM Testing
1544052857534418964.report:
Did some tests with fast/slow weapons comparing proc rates for dual mistwalker procs and dual fluxbladed axe procs to see what it looked like. 

TLDR: mistwalker is a better proc on a test dummy with a higher proc rate and higher overall damage, and more importantly cannot be resisted. It's not going to change your life, though. 

One thing this shows is that the PPM model is less consistent than you would expect. There are some pretty wild variances in the same loadout across different parses, but puma procs like crazy pretty reliably. Another thing is that at least in these tests I was seeing better proc performance with the faster weapons vs the slower, especially for mistwalker. 
All tests were done in ~5m segments as RNG/BRD/SHM, with 3 parses per variant, and were using either dual mistwalker or dual fluxbladed with no mix/match. 

### Fast Weapon Testing ###
Target: "Test Fifty" (lvl 50 arena dummy)
MH Weapon: Arydryidriyorn (21del)
OH Weapon: Revultant Whip (14del)
Relevant stats: 515dex, 683atk, 175% haste
Stances: Offensive/spellblade (shock of venom)

Averages:
- Mistwalker PPM: 3.17
- Mistwalker DPS: 19.67
- Fluxbladed PPM: 2.78
- Fluxbladed DPS: 10.33
- Puma PPM: 16.78
- Spellblade PPM: 4.51


### Slow Weapon Testing ###
Target: "Test Fifty" (lvl 50 arena dummy)
MH Weapon: Crystalline Spear (30del)
OH Weapon: Gnoll Slayer (40del)
Relevant stats: 506dex, 675atk, 175% haste
Stances: Offensive/spellblade (shock of venom)
Averages:
- Mistwalker PPM: 2.39
- Mistwalker DPS: 15.33
- Fluxbladed PPM: 2.28
- Fluxbladed DPS: 7.33
- Puma PPM: 15.67
- Spellblade PPM: 3.80


I can give some more detailed info if anyones interested but cant include it all here due to message limits.

1543512442418499614.title: Re-charming Macro
1543512442418499614.report:
I want to create a macro to quickly re-charm the same mob when charm breaks. The problem is that, when charm breaks, the former pet (which is buffed up) gets placed in the last slot of the X-target list, and I cannot find any specific command to target the last slot. Apparently, you need to define the slot, such as "/xtarget 3", but there is not such a thing as "/xtarget last". I have tried "/xtarget 9", but if there is no mob in slot #9, nothing gets targeted.

Any suggestion to create this macro?

replies.author: Seabass
replies.text: You can lock that mob into slot 9 when you first engage it by right clicking on its name in the xtarget window

replies.author: Whunkthefunk
replies.text: Here is the combo I use for recharm. Macro One: This is setting your pet to xtar 1, you can make it whatever you want. /xtarget set 1 currenttarget /pet ghold Macro Two: This is the recharm macro. Sets current target, and recharms your pet. /xtarget set 2 currenttarget /xtarget target 1, /pause 80 /doability Over Channel, /pause 30 /cast 14 /xtarget target 2 I shamelessly stole this from a google docs at the start.

replies.author: Varsadi
replies.text: These macros work well. I use the one from this thread which is pretty much the same and it works amazingly.

replies.author: Varsadi
replies.text: If your ping is a bit slower you may not need the delays/pauses.

replies.author: Koh Phi Phi

replies.author: pry
replies.text: For Wizard spells you'll want to max Conflag, Frost Storm, and Rend. Nothing else really matters. You could do Ice Comet instead of Rend. I prefer Rend though, you'll land it a bit easier having Tash, it also gives you 1 Fire, 1 Frost, and 1 Magic based attack. You'll also want Drain Spirit maxed from SK. Vampiric Embrace is good too, but it's lower priority compared to most of your stuff. From Enchanter you'll want motes invested in Allure, Mesmerization, and Shiftless Deeds. You don't need to max them, but you do need some points in them. How many is up to you. Shiftless for landing slow easier. I only put 5 in AE Mez, but a lot people like to max it out, nothing wrong with that. I've never found myself dying wishing I had mez a few ranks higher though. Allure might be the one you want the most in. Higher level means you can charm higher level mobs and maybe even more important the -mr reduction on cast goes a long way in charm lasting longer. Rotation is a simple priority system as long as the target isn't highly resistant to a specific element. Frost Storm > Conflag > Rend. ABC - Always be casting. You should be spamming your next up as your previous cast ends. Your actual cast sequence will look something like Frost Storm -> Conflag -> Rend -> Conflag -> Rend -> Frost Storm

replies.author: pry
replies.text: 1h and 2h should proc the same amount if just auto-attacking unless there's something funky happening. But in actuality we'll proc more with a 2h whenever weaving any casts. The weaving effectively increases your weapon delay to that of the cast time of your spell but without adjusting the proc chance per swing to that effective delay. It's still procs based on how much it should be swinging not how much it's actually swinging. To illustrate, suppose we have 3PPM and 142 haste. Our Bloodmoon at 28 delay swings every 1.157s or 51.86 times a minute. That comes out to 5.79% proc chance per swing. Our 2h Sky sword at 43 delay swings every 1.777s with the same haste. That's 33.76 swings/minute for an actual proc chance per swing of 8.89%. Both should proc roughly 3 times per minute on average. But on an individual swing basis the 2h has a 53% higher chance to proc. This is normally compensated by the Bloodmoon swinging 53% more times. Now let's suppose we're chain casting 2.0s spell+gcd with every attack queued to fire off immediately when the cast finishes. Both weapons effectively become 30 attacks/min as their swings are delayed to happen only every 2s. The proc chance doesn't become 10% to proc per swing to maintain 3 ppm. The game should still see it as 5.79% for the Bloodmoon and 8.89% for the 2h. So our actual results would be 30 x 0.0579 = 1.74 PPM for the Bloodmoon and 30 x 0.0889 = 2.67 PPM for the 2h. This may not explain why in auto attack tests someone is seeing more procs with a 2h. But for those of us chain casting spells it is why we'll proc more with a 2h.

I haven't exactly seen anyone singing the praises of that particular trio but it does work well despite the overlap. In anycase, Paladin, berserker, shaman works well for a froglok or a barbarian following mithaniel marr. Paladin, druid, shaman would work well for someone nature focused and the sort of military arm of someone like Tunare. Paladin, warrior/ranger, bard for a human/half elf Marr follower might work well. Maybe you could do Paladin, beastlord, druid/cleric for a sort of houndsman kind of theme that is ultra dedicated to Marr. The undead killing potential would be great with the cleric atleast.

replies.text: Ranger sockets perfectly into paladin thematically. Pal is innately war + clr, so you already can just use war or clr to skip a slot thematically, or emphasize a char aspect. Pal rng bst would be perfect for a knight of the grove / knight of nature. Pal rog x can symbolize who your pally was before turning to the good life. Pal sk and pal nec can both symbolize balance of good and evil, or life and death. Pal wiz for solusek ro devotee. Pal mag for elemental god or solusek ro devotee. Pal brd is great for mith marr - you sing tales of your valor, or give your paladin hero music that just mystically plays mear them when dramatic. Pal enc eludes me. Enc is antithetical to pal, and my main trio uses enc. I've been using aoe mez as a "compelled duel" spell. "YOU WISH TO BATTLE ME ALL AT ONCE? NAY! DUEL ME - BEST ME HONORABLY, AND CLAIM VICTORY! OR LIVE WITH THY COWARDACE!" Mem wipe is antithetical to paladin. Illusions could be themed as the paladin dramatically seeming to be an important figure in someone's life, bestowed a divine unconscious task to convey a message to someone. Suffocate dot line can be a holy lasso that you constrict a foe with. Slow can be divine glowy shackles. Disempower can be a weakness instilled by your imposing confidence and presence. Pal mnk also eludes me.

replies.text: The various buffs can all just be various blessings if you want to forcefully rewrite another class into more paladin stuff. On a journey, I had backstab be a masked distance snap-thrust, and gave my paladin a rapier.

replies.author: Lukeios
replies.text: I run BRD/PAL/NEC, I'm able to beat CT on D4 but just barely: - The fight is an absolute slog. CT had WIZ so first part of fight was using superior heal X (not Spirit Tap) to stay alive while he dropped his entire mana bar on me - I used Smite in this fight, LoH'd early on (around 80% of my mana reserves) so I'd have it up later in the fight. - From there it was using Envenomed Bolt with Overchannel and then back switching back into Recovery Invocation. I had chants loaded but mostly didn't use them, focusing more on staying alive. - Pet was smacking him the whole time with 70% haste. I'm haste capped using Aldryn +8 and Serpents Tooth +4 - Symphonic Aura line up was Largo's, Verses of Victory, Chant of Battle, Shield of Songs, Cantana of Soothing. Largo's didn't stick. - I did have to switch to Balance stance a few times from Defensive. Be prepared to heal more aggressively during this time. (EN regen is 112 in balanced, for the record) - For reference: I have 6k HP, 526AC (510 Evasion), 4750 mana and 4125 endurance. My resists were nothing special. My gear is good but also has room for improvement. My advice to you: AC cap is not the end, you should be pushing well past it with both AA's and gear choices. Shields in the Any slot are great here. (Shield of the Stalwart Seas and Shield of the Immaculate are what i'm using). Max out Superior heal, Envenomed Bolt and engage in attrition style combat against the big hitters. For this particular fight: I feel like having a Tash proc (from orb of Tishan) and maxed Largo's would help to land slow. I was taking the full extent of his damage through the whole fight. (Just for the record, i'm picking CT on D4 to illustrate the viability of this combo in endgame)

1542538785198309497.title: Managing Bard Charm
1542538785198309497.report:
So how are y'all handling bard charm? I know it's not ENC quality, but I have trouble micro-managing it, my charm always breaks pretty quick, I get swarmed, etc. 
Any mechanical/game tips would be welcome, because it's not working for me.

replies.author: Mirakk Stormhammer
replies.text: Level it. It's one of the few songs worth leveling. Overchannel every time. It checks the resists at the landing stage. CHA doesn't appear to do anything. -MR pet gear doesn't seem to have much of any effect. If you really want to push it up, get Jam Fest maxed out if you haven't already. Higher casting level ensures it lands

replies.author: Sheltim
replies.text: Even if you do everything right, it'll still occasionally break early and it still doesn't last as long as every fight. Set up an audio cue for it breaking, keep a small bank of Endurance so you can swap into Evasive while you recharm.

replies.author: Sheltim
replies.text: "-MR pet gear doesn't seem to have much of any effect" - that's news to me, the recommendations I saw were to use something like the -MR ring or shoulders. Can you say more?

replies.author: Mirakk Stormhammer
replies.text: The pet only wears the gear when it is charmed. So when you are landing the spell, the minus isn't there yet. Once the spell has landed, it seems to snapshot the original resist mod and use it the whole time. Overchannel, and leveling the spell will provide the greatest -MR modifiers at the moment of casting. In my testing, charm breaks rapidly when not Overchanneled and wearing - resist gear on the pet. When using no resist gear but Over Channeling, Max duration happens almost every time.

1542199286362546287.title: Symphonic Aura Twisting: How to Play 14 Group Songs at Once
1542199286362546287.report:
While messing around with my DDD build, I couldn't help noticing that Amplification has a particularly long duration of 30+ seconds, and it's extended by Spell Casting Reinforcement and the Extended Enhancement focus effect.

So I thought, "why can't I just periodically turn off SA and cast amp? Then I can put an extra song in my SA."

And this totally works. It works great! I use the following macro:
/alt act 152
/cast 9 (or /melody or /queuemelody, more on this later)
/pause x (however long your amp cast time is. Spell Haste FE and spell rank matter here. For me it's currently 22)
/stopsong
/alt act 152

I do this once every minute or so, as that's how long my Amp lasts. Max rank Amp along with EE focus effect & max Spell Casting Reinforcement should be above 90 seconds, which is pretty easy to maintain.

But would I be a proper Bard if I didn't push this idea to the extreme?

Turns out, you can actually fit a bunch of songs into a /melody and twist them all between enabling your SA. I've managed to do 10 easily with almost no investment of motes into most of my songs. I suspect with some mote investment you could maintain a full 14 songs 100% of the time with ease.

Here's an example macro for a full 5-melody inside your SA disablement:
/alt act 152
/melody 9 8 7 6 5
/pause x (x = sum of song cast times. I usually round up, so if cast time is 2.04, just add 21 for that song)
/stopsong
/alt act 152

At low mote levels and if you're pushing the number of songs you want to fit in here, it helps to know a bit how SA works. Whenever mana regen ticks, your SA simultaneously fires off all 5 songs. So if you want to maximize the number of songs to fit between SA 'ticks', then you should click the macro *right* after a mana regen tick. If you've set up everything properly, SA should turn back on right before the last song drops off.

replies.author: Kethigar
replies.text: Also of note, even outside of motes, depending on your FEs and AAs, your baseline bard buff songs could last anywhere from 12s to 30s. That's a huge difference, so you may have to mess around with this to find exactly how many songs you can (and want to) fit in comfortably. And if anyone has an recommendations for the macro, feel free to share! I am absolutely not an EQ macro expert so I'm sure there are much better ways to do this

1541891996506128455.title: Inconsistencies with Tracking
1541891996506128455.report:
I've spent the last few days in South Karana tracking rares. My current Ranger combo is 30 (RNG/SK/SHM) so not max track, but high enough to cover a large portion of the zone. During this time i've notice alot of inconsistencies with tracking and/or with mob behavior in general.

 - Enemies will often warp around when tracking both with the radar and using directional tracking. Enemies that i have tracking directly in front of my may swing around wildly in a different direction. Often this seems like the enemy is teleporting, but it could just be incosistent updates of tracking information on my client. Even so, these "teleports" often appear to be inconsistent with an movement/direction the enemy could have been moving in.
 - Enemies sometimes appear very briefly on my tracking list/radar. Usually I can find that enemy somewhere else in the map later, but the behavior is wierd. This could be a subset of the behavior above, but I've seen this occur with enemies that should be very close to me and haveing them move out of range in the short time i see them on track seems unlikely.
 - This usually happens when i first start to track a mob....a little while after I "lock in" on them, they begin to behave/path more more predictably.

I've played alot of EQ., both old school and more recently, but i've never taken a tracking class to a high level until EQL. As a result, I dont know if this is normal EQ jank, or something new to EQL.

replies.text: I noticed some of this too. I've also noticed that when sometimes when I click on a mob in my track window, forces them to appear on the map. I've also had mobs not show up on the map *at all* until I was closer in proximity to them.

replies.author: Caroc

1541782421899321394.title: Enchanter CHA and Charm  explained
1541782421899321394.report:
There are many questions about the effect of CHA on Enchanter's Charm. Since we have access to the code of EQ emulator, which is based on live parsing and is very similar to EQL, I looked into it:

CHA only matters at two moments: 
the initial resist check when you first cast the charm, and each individual tick-save roll where the mob gets a chance to break free. It does not extend the base duration of the spell.

The "sweet spot" starts at 75 CHA. Below that, your Charisma is actually working against you: for every 10 CHA under 75, you get a flat +6 penalty to the mob's resist chance. So a low CHA build makes charm noticeably harder to land and hold.

Above 75 CHA, you get a bonus. Every 10 CHA above 75 gives you "−1" to the mob's resist modifier. 255 CHA would give "−18". It's a real but fairly modest benefit.

Before any of that even triggers, there's a break-check gate. Every buff tick (6 seconds), there's roughly a 75% chance nothing happens at all (no resist roll is even attempted that tick). Only on the remaining ~25% of ticks does the game actually roll a resist check, and that's where your CHA modifier comes into play.

Casting Charm while in Overcharge Stance results in a noticeably longer duration for Charm. This benefit persists even if you subsequently exit Overcharge Stance. At the moment of casting, the game sets a break modifier that is multiplied by the probability of a Charm break. Presumably, the Overcharge modifier is around 0.5, meaning the probability that Charm breaks is reduced by another 50% after all other calculations have been applied.

replies.author: _.chob._
replies.text: Leech touch is the biggest one. The highest levels of HT get a dot component that also leeches. When Im fighting a raid boss, thats enough to keep me standing for a while. And on easier bosses or minis I can even switch to offensive while it ticks. I keep reave on auto so I get my HT back more often.

replies.text: HT w/ Leech Touch turns it into a full heal in the early stages of the fight. Focus effects don't apply to 'combat abilities', but crit AAs will modify it. Dot crit AAs will affect the dot portion, and all of that affects the healing provided. Try to switch to Empower before popping HT, it snapshots for the dot portion

1540698075129970708.title: Gear Stat Paralysis
1540698075129970708.report:
Hey all! Looking for a little advice here. 

Back in the day, when only playing ONE class, it was pretty obvious what stats and gear to prioritize. Now when you’re playing something like a wisdom tank, a melee DPS, and an INT caster, you basically need every stat there is. 

So how do you decide what to focus on? Do you just do a “jack of all trades” thing where you’re above average at everything, but not great at anything? Stack your defense to stay alive? Focus on your DPS stats (depending on your class choices) to kill faster? 

It just almost feels like the freedom has given me too many options, haha. 

(Side note: I’m intentionally not naming specific classes because I’m asking a more generic question)

replies.author: Bandana Belmont
replies.text: I'd say all builds value resists highly, with ac slightly behind that. The game does a pretty good job of supplying those naturally though with decent itemization once you start farming raid targets and planar gear. So much so that you really don't need to think about gearing if you have a plate wearer in your loadout. Just throw on the highest ac piece for that slot and you'll be alright. The only situations that come to mind where you may need to put a little thought into gearing is if one plays a pure direct damage build, in which case they need to stack as much int or wis as possible while sacrificing some ac and resists.

replies.author: Dastion
replies.text: We all know exactly what “Wis Tank, Melee DPS, Int Caster” means :p There is something called EQL tools that had a BIS section that, while not perfect, will help you get an idea what items are good for each slot for your trio. With a tank you’ll want AC so your plate set pieces from the planes are solid options at least for the bigger pieces. You’ll want a good shield with high AC for bash (use it from any slot with the improved bash AA). Haste is a priority so get one of your haste belts from Sky. I think it needs to be +7 to max your haste with just Enchanter’s Augmentation buff. Use your jewelry to fill in stat gaps that weren’t available on your better AC pieces. Odds are you’ll want things like the earring Ivander’s Hoop, the face mask from vox (I think) with a ton of int/wis. etc. When in doubt Dex is also a great stat as it affects your proc rates.

replies.author: Stakka
replies.text: AC > resists > hp/mana

replies.author: Francisco  (he/him/his)
replies.text: There is no metric - if you only do ac, your gonna get charmed, stunned, and feared constantly. If you put mana last your never gonna have any mana. You need a real balance

replies.author: FatedEmperor
replies.text: I run Clr, Enc, and Druid as my main. Typically, I focus on stamina, wis, and int as my primary stats. I have all the combat-focused AAs minus direct spell damage. For me survivability comes down to leveraging my cleric buffs and my mana pool into sustained healing. My damage comes from charm, damage shield, dots, and reducing the enemies' armor. The only boss I have really had an issue on is CT and trying to face tank him, but I have cleared him on D2. All the other bosses I have done on D4 solo. In general, I would suggest prioritizing whichever stat is going to serve multiple classes the best, choosing a min-maxing approach and gimping yourself in one area, and/or using armor that cover multiple stats. It's hard to give advice without knowing specific classes and play style does also factor in somewhat. For a general breakdown for the harder content your going to want some conceptual form of tanking, healing/mitgation, and some form of reliable dps. How you achieve this can come down to class choices or playstyle. Then you are going to want to try to balance those factors, which in some cases may require trial and error.

replies.author: theBruce
replies.text: i run mnk/enc/shm and i balance my stats but i've found with the regen i have for mana, i really do not need to prioritize it at all, the only time i even come close to running out is if i just keep getting endless adds in fear, and even then the massive regen enc/shm affords is more than enough. instead i focus on ac/resists and melee stats for the monk. granted i have all of the AA's that make everything efficient, so this is end-end game gearing.

replies.text: From what I could tell the air pet does not need to worry about weight reduction, but I could be wrong. But nothing in my pet window or taking items off of pet points to this being true (for me). With regarding pet weapons, think of it this way. You would ALWAYS want weapons on your pet, with procs, as even if they ignore the weapon dmg, or ratio, it will use the procs. Easy way to remember how pets look at weapons: 1) Does the weapon have a better ratio than pet native dmg/delay ratio? A) Yes, then use the weapon dmg AND delay, AND procs. B) NO, consider below: B.1) Does the weapon with a worse ratio than native pet dmg/delay have a higher dmg than native pet dmg? If Yes, then use that weapon dmg AND weapon procs BUT use the native pet delay. B.2) If the ratio, AND the dmg is worse than pet native ratio, and DMG, then use ONLY procs. For my air pet, I use Garduk with Barbarian Spiritist Hammer exalt for proc in mainhand on pet (I'm SK/Sham/Mage) and Dagas with Bloodfire exaltation DoT proc in Offhand. Also keep in mind that pets do not proc AoEs currently. So things like Earthshaker proc exalt is worthless for them as of now.

SHM dots + puma are excellent supplementary damage regardless of stance selection - more than monk was contributing. The big misses are evasive during charm breaks and FD (outside the Shaman Sky ring). I've been considering trying SHD (get FD back, plus HT DOT damage to synergize with SHM) or RNG (Charm pet tanking, with ranged attacks) in place of Pal but I need to get leveling them still. I'd imagine ENC/MNK/CLR is enough healing that you can just sit in an offensive stance full time if that's what you want to do. Safer but probably lower damage potential than shaman. 1539919395126771832.title: Most passive class(es) to go with Paladin?
1539919395126771832.report:
I have issues with my hands/fingers, which means my APM is extremely low during combat.
As a result am theory crafting what the best classes are to get high output with minimal button presses.

Have done Paladin/Shaman/Monk and Paladin/Shaman/Ranger to 50, and some thoughts so far:

Monk - Hit auto attack and Mend as needed. It's biggest benefits are passive (haste cap, weapon caps, extra attacks)
Paladin - Use LOH when needed, heal when needed, the odd stun/heal here are there, but pretty low APM so far. (also my locked-in primary)
SK (?) - Havent played this one yet, but Vampiric Embrace is passive, but unsure if I have to spend fights spamming life-taps or not
Bard - Havent played this one yet either, but 5 songs playing via Symphonic Aura, plate wearer - dual wield, does well with either knight.
Shaman - A little annoying having to refresh haste every 10 minutes and also casting slow + dots *every single fight* in addition to healing.

All that said, I am looking at Paladin, Bard, Monk. Any glaring holes in that trio in terms of APM and covering all the basics?
Not looking for the leet-est of the leet, just able to do D0 and D1 basic Hate grinding with Yael, Vox and Naggy right now with minimal button presses.

replies.author: Zelanther
replies.text: Yeah i play my pal/rog/enc in offensive due to striker being a drain

replies.author: jeditobe1
replies.text: From memory, berserker eats endurance at 0.5x damage dealt, and offensive drains it at 100% of *bonus* damage dealt, which is half the damage dealt. Strategy reductions are a bit of a black box and I think dont impact them equally, but they are in theory about the same. Effectively its "you do X damage and you are out of endurance" which correlates to "you get X kills before you run out" before factoring in refill from endurance regeneration. Endgame weapons "drain faster" because they do more damage (still same total damage on the same endurance bar, in theory, but it outstrips your regeneration so you bottom out faster).

replies.author: khantrol
replies.text: Reposting the final findings: Spirit of Kashek X Warder Base Damage = 31 Warder Bonus Damage = 14 Warder Delay = 26 Bonus let x = 126 # Earthshaker max hit when ratio < natural ratio let y = 56 # Earthshaker dmg use in test Bonus Damage = x - (y * 2) Bonus Damage: 14 Base Damage let x = 76 # Max hit unarmed let y = 14 # Bonus damage determined above Base Damage = (x - y) / 2 Base Damage = 31 Delay We can make a chart of possible delays and bracket possible ratios based on parses 31/25 = 1.240 Barrier <--> Cudgel of the Fool +4 1.212 ratio used <--> Barrier 31/26 = 1.192 Barrier <--> Cudgel of the Fool +3 1.173 ratio unused <--> Barrier 31/27 = 1.148 31/28 = 1.107

replies.author: khantrol
replies.text: As for one handers there is a small set of them which have better ratios than unarmed (31/26 = 1.192): Thelvorn, Blade of Light +6 Aldryn, Blade of the Ocean +6 Wu's Fist of Mastery +7 Bloodmoon +9 Thornstinger +10 Theurgist's Star +10 Wu's being the only offhand variant that beats unarmed.

replies.author: khantrol
replies.text: Two handers are a bit of a different story since we have to make up for the loss of offhand dps. Which in my testing isn't possible using the regular weapon ratios. For instance when I parsed bare fist + shield I was getting ~21.3 dps and when I parsed Skycleaver+10 (1.714 ratio) I'm seeing 26 dps. My offhand was dealing about 15 dps in the current set up. That leaves what I'll call the earthshaker trick which is: If a weapons ratio is less than that of the natural ratio (31/26 = 1.192) the pet will use it's natural delay but boost it's max/avg damage based on the given weapon. So using my current set up I'd want to see higher than ~35 dps on the 2 hander to make up for. In my small tests Cudgel of the Fool +3 which has a damage of 61 parsed 34.9 which would be about the break even point. 61/26 = 2.345 ratio. My Earthshaker +5 with 56 damage parsed 32.9 which is a dps loss from bare hands. 56/26 = 2.153 ratio. So probably an earthshaker +7 and higher would be a dps increase over no weapons. I don't have one yet but I'll test once I get it.

replies.author: khantrol
replies.text: There is also the possibility to "earthshaker trick" with 1 handers. But there are only a limited number of 1 handers weapons that would work. Garduk +5 or higher Blade of Abrogation +6 or higher Bloodmoon +8 only Sporali Defender's Blade +9 or higher Darkmetal Holy Water Sprinkler + 10

replies.author: khantrol
replies.text: One final parse to test the garduk earthshaker trick Weapon: Garduk +5 (dmg: 34, delay: 40, bonus: 20, ratio: 0.85) Reason: Do we get a damage bump while ignoring delay? Findings: Yes, so you can get a boost to your mainhand using garduk or blade of abrogation while keeping the offhand dps. This may outpace earthshakers.

So did a little work on druid dots not actually tested it in game but mathed it off the wiki details. 
I use immolate (afaik the most efficient dot) the last swarm dot at 40 and vengeance. 
But I noticed that vengeance seems to have possible the worst chance tomland of all 3. I've got I immo and vengeance to r6. I think immo is sitting at -90 FR and vengeance at -120. So you would think vengeance would land better? 
I see they are two diffener types conjuration and evocation. 

Is evocation a little more reliable? 
Or is it just a really odd RNG for me and vengeance? It's irritating as that's the least efficient dot as far as I can tell. 

Anyone had any similar experience?

replies.author: Dastion
replies.text: The Swarm DoT has a high chance to land because it has a pretty hefty -resistance bonus baked into it. The other two DoT lines target Fire and don't have as much of a bonus unless you upgrade them. Immolate targets Fire at -0 Swarm targets Magic at -100 Vengeance targets Fire at -30 TBH I only ever use the Swarm DoT, I don't have room for much else on my bars with all of the other Druid and Enchanter stuff in my main trio.

replies.text: I actually utilize the fire dot (vengeance of the wild) with fixation of ro and ro's fiery sundering to reduce fire resists and AC in combination with fire arrow line and call of flame to help prevent partials and full resist. Is it good? is it worth it? IDK but I enjoy thinking it does. The reality is if these spells are not good enough the alternative is changing to a shaman, and I just can't stand the idea that the fix to druid problems is switch to shaman atm. I'm happier suffering.

replies.text: Yea I wish the Druid DoTs other than Swarm were more worthwhile. Druid’s ability to do a bit of everything is great but some of that isn’t really worth doing when there is an opportunity cost of what you’d give up doing with your other classes in your trio.

replies.author: Razel the Rogue
replies.text: I have been trying to understand where the devs believe the rogue fits into the melee mix. _Appoligies some of this is a rehash of what we have stated prior._ General Class Mechanics: * Primarily melee - offense skill, dual wield, double and triple attack. * Backstab * Poisons - limited utility * Fast weapons, applies dmg bonus Counter to each Mechanic: * Low base attack compared to other melee such as Monk and Ranger, results in lower DPS from melee. * Monk has high offensive skill which gives higher attack * Ranger gets AAs for higher attack. * Monks and Rogues should share offensive skill caps. Where Monks have highest 1hb skill cap, Rog should be highest 1HPiercing. * Backstab scale decent until later levels. -- devs say scaling is coming. * cleave, reave, smite, monk strikes/kicks should not be competing with Backstab. * exception there is an argument that monk kicks and strike in combination should compete. * Poisons are just nice to haves. They add flavor, but may not be hugely impactful. * Person opinion is that procs in general do not meaningfully compete with melee or spells. * Dmg bonus is very low for fast weapons and those fast weapons have low dmg. I think zerkers are in the same boat, but they have a stance that makes them more desirable. Unless you want stealth. Rogue does fit a niche, stealthy mage or as a 3rd slot for a complete 2 class build.

You're pretty much just comparing Warrior+Shaman to Monk at that point. The big problem is melee classes just don't stack together offensively. It's mostly just... weapon access. AAs and special attacks (for most) add surprisingly little. So stacking multiple melee classes together is largely a waste. What you do gain is defensive ability. Pal+Monk combines higher ac cap and defensive stance with block and evasion. That defensive utility is great, but the damage is just not impressive for 2 classes. Compared to War+Sham, for example, Shaman doesn't just add puma. It also has crazy strong dots. Even the weak ass Shaman pet alone adds more damage to Warrior than Paladin does as an entire class to Monk.

I leveled up Ranger up and it just doesn't compare. I don't get it lol. Yeah, the pal/sk gets smite/reave, but war also gets cleave. Warrior both tanks better and does more damage than Pal/SK/Rng. You're right about it freeing up the healer slot though. But if you're adding Monk to be able to do any Melee damage you're still down a class, just as the War has to spend a class slot on heals. I'm not going to go as far as saying War+Sham is better than Monk+Pal. They just bring different things. War+Sham should do more damage while taking less damage. More direct power. And then the Pal+Monk comes with the better utility of pacify, feign death, and those emergency heals with LoH and mend.

replies.author: EddieRidge
replies.text: Warriors aren't just tanks, they are dps tanks. They have their own class identity just as paladins are righteous warriors with excellent self and group sustain, and SKs are evil with excellent solo capabilities. In live a warrior will put out extremely respectable dps numbers from white damage, specially when tanking. You might say, "but this is classic" and yeah you're right but also other classes have their class identity and their constraints completely removed. e.g. a wizard, that is no longer burst dps but is very effective sustained dps as mana is practically infinite, enchanters had all the constraints that made charm dps possible in classic possible, shamans got overpowered out of era spells (puma), bards got enough mana to spam DDD and become the best aoe dps. Warriors even had their defensive disc, evasive disc, charge disc, and more stripped out and given to everyone as stances and white damage had a resource constraint applied to it (endurance) so I don't think it's much to ask that they do can put up better numbers than support classes, priests and hybrids

replies.text: Yeah this is what is concerning about warrior going forward into Kunark. They’ve already homogenized defensive discipline and given it to knights. Knights also get mage hunter stance while warrior gets 5% bonus DR, not nothing, but not enough. Warrior’s niche was defensive discipline and better threat management. But threat/taunts are really not as much of a factor in EQL and a total nothing burger for solo. They’ll have to make some changes or re-tune things, or knights will get further ahead in future content, as their spells and abilities do continue to excel greatly. With stats going to the moon and strength not really scaling due to the weird d20 formulas they used for EQ, melee won’t catch up unless changes are made. Warrior is still good, and able to tank all the content no problem, its just less flexible and more rigid. So I’m going all in on SK for now with the variety of powerful builds they compliment. Being the one tank that can be in caster/nuker builds that synergize with AM3 builds, is actually kinda broken. Both knights are overpowered as expected, but not everyone caught onto SK because people were so focused on paladins (perceived by many as the only tank that could raid D4 without a healer but that’s been proven wrong with how good upgraded taps are) and harm touch being underwhelming (which was giga buffed and now as good or better than LoH). It seems like SK’s have a higher endgame power ceiling due to their obvious synergy with int casters.

Every combat round the War will do more melee damage via more crits/crips, higher damage crits, and better special attacks while taking less damage. And if you're casting spells for damage it's going to be EBolt, Odium, Plague, and Shock of Venom... not mid SK spells. It isn't a complete runaway though. The occasional HT is nice. Lifetaps are great for lazy damage+healing. But it is less sustained dps. How is Paladin adding more damage though? Suppose you swapped Monk with Rogue. Now War adds kick and block and is significantly better. But if you swapped Sham out for... Bard or Wiz, the knights become significantly better because of their healing kit. 1539147353519296622.title: Wizard is an example of EQL success
1539147353519296622.report:
But other classes dont get to share that success because of design decisions (many of which are almost 30 years old). Other class' design basis should take note of the synergies that wizard is well positioned to take advantage of and add elements that also add to synergies they have (or could have):

Wizard AAs work in synergy to grow the power of the wizard play style:
- destructive fury
- fury of magic
- Quick damage
- that one that decreases spell cost
- wizard unbound crit chance
- mana regen

Spell focii give real power to direct damage (and dots) unlike majority of gear to other damage types (strength and atk giving modest boost to white dps which impacts melee, pets, and archery)
- damage focus
- spell cost reduction
- spell haste

Spell mote system
- decreases cost
- decreases cast time
- increases damage

And the crown jewel is arcane mastery 3 of course. Further decreasing cast time and cast cost.

If you have a cleric friend you can also get the cleric spell haste buff but I dont have a cleric friend so idk about that.

Feels like white damage builds have barely any AAs that effect damage in a meaningful way, stats barely effect damage in a meaningful way, obviously the mote system is working well for white damage. The stances, while on the face seem to be good, make choices more difficult and costly for white damage. Loving wizard though

replies.author: Nixilus
replies.text: Just to add maybe a summary, every system to be interacted with lowers cast time, decreases cost, and raises damage for wizard player power: gear (through focii but not stats which is dumb but I guess inherent to eq), AAs, motes, and invocation/stance. The slow accumulation of each is a nice progression. White damage gets their ambidexterity (2h get wrecked), and combat fury (which is just ability crit chance), a decent couple swords and try to stay in offensive stance as much as possible and end of story besides get levels. Maybe needs some more wizardlike spice.

replies.author: tallcupofcoffee
replies.text: Wiz is in a great spot (funny how they flew under the meta radar in both betas). White DMG and melee abilities are in a challenging game design space. They're all basically single channel. It's great that specials can fire independently, but stacking RNG and Mnk in a trio doesn't bring the same damage scaling that stacking wiz and NEC, for instance. Put another way, *all melee classes share the white DMG tick*. Adding a MNK to a RNG doesn't compound the DPS in the same way as adding a NEC to a wiz.

I'm discounting the utility brought in the combos; obviously, that exists and it's what keeps my combo enjoyable to play, but there is almost no DPS synergy, and it ends up making every fight feel like a slog.

1539034416830087318.title: Triple Bow Shot working?
1539034416830087318.report: Level 50 Rog/Rng/Mnk - 100/100 Triple Attack skill. I have logs for the last bit (2.5 hours in Range stance) and I don't see a single Triple Bow Attack. Is that normal? There are plenty of the Double Attack variety.

replies.author: Orbos
replies.text: Triple Bow Shot working?

replies.author: Diogenes
replies.text: Ranged double/triple shot often do not appear in the same second due to the mechanics in EQ. How many time do you have 'shoots' 1 second apart? Do you think your bow has a 1s delay?

replies.author: MVE - Mutevoice Quietstrings
replies.text: I don't think I have seen one "Triple shot" reported for over 10 hours of game play ‍

replies.author: Diogenes
replies.text: That is because double and triple attack don't get reported. You simply attack 2 or 3 times in a row and each attack is its own line in the combat log. Melee happens in the same second but ranged attacks don't necessarily. For what it's worth...double and triple attack work perfectly fine with Ranged Stance and Archery.

replies.author: djcan
replies.text: Double bow shots and critical double bow shots get reported in the critical combat filter in chat, I see myself get them all the time.

replies.author: djcan
replies.text: I haven’t played with the bow at 46+ to be able to triple attack, just wanted to point out that the log does clearly register them as doubles, it’s not like regular double attack.

replies.author: Diogenes
replies.text: What you are talking about is Innate Called Shot that reports as (Double Bow Shot) in the combat log. This is not the same thing as Double Attack and Triple Attack.

replies.author: Orbos
replies.text: Ah yeah maybes it's just a log thing then, because I do see the Double Bow Shot all the time.

replies.author: nirafelos
replies.text: the (double bow shot) text, as diogenes says, is calling out that the target is stationary and thus the damage was doubled, not that you performed a double attack via the double attack skill. you can test this by resetting to 10 on any x/x/rng comp and noting that you see this signifier and that you won't have access to the Double Attack skill for another 10 levels. At level 50 with the current skillcaps, double-attacking classes only successfully Double Attack 75% of the time (monks are higher), and can only Triple Attack on a successful Double Attack and a successful roll to "upgrade" that to a Triple Attack. This occurs somewhere around 15-20% of the time. That math is fuzzier because we have triple attack 10 levels early here and the math looks different than normal for it.

replies.author: Orbos
replies.text: Thanks for the clarification. That was confusing for sure! I'll just try to look for a bunch of arrows being launched real fast!

replies.author: Orbos
replies.text: So, do you think this was a triple bow shot? Ah crap, can't add pictures...

replies.author: Orbos
replies.text: But it was three "Double Bow Shots" really quick in a row in the combat log.

replies.author: Diogenes
replies.text: Turn on timestamps to make it clearer to yourself. The way melee works it all happens instantly but with ranged attacks there is a delay in processing the attacks and they can be on the same second or consecutive seconds.

1538578274949791846.title: At 50, which heal are we using?
1538578274949791846.report:
Healing Water
0.75 casting time for 425 hitpoints at 150 mana


Superior healing
3.50 casting time for 600 hitpoints at 185 mana


Forest's Renewal
3.75 casting time for 671 hitpoints at 233 mana


Looks to me like Superior Heal is the most efficient heal in terms of mana, and there's no real reason to ever use Forest's Renewal.

I can see a reason for Healing Water though, the near instant cast probably eats into your melee dps less. Though it has a recast time, so you can only cast it once every 6 seconds.

replies.author: Istmael
replies.text: I exclusively use Healing Water (rank 6) and Efflorescing (rank 4) as DRU/MNK/ENC and easily tank even Bees and unslowed EoV in channeler at this point. Healing Water has no issues sustaining and I'd rather kill things faster (i.e., without clipping swings). I have no healing AAs yet, but periodically consider getting some of the HoT ones... but once you get even a little planar gear, sustainability and mana regen are not issues. I'm hoping Forest's gets tweaked to be more useful (or at least interesting) given it is supposed to be *the* heal but at this point, Healing Water does work. Given we get to use it on alts much sooner than the other heals, it just feels like a win-win-win on utility.
