replies.text: Efflo and healing water. I weave healing water and the arrow/call spells from ranger after applying negative debuffs from druid (fixation, fiery sundering, vengeance)

replies.author: Dastion
replies.text: Yea, I particularly like that Healing Waters is very effective without Inversion Invo going. I've only got it leveled to like 5 but it crits for over 1k and Druids give a bonus to all spell crits.

replies.author: Tover
replies.text: I feel differently about them now then when I first hit 50... Now that I have healing focus, the various healing AA's, and have upgraded my heals to 6+'s.... The bulk of my healing is done by Efflorescing Heal (HoT).. My fav filler is Forest's Renewal.... Upgrading that one to increase the casting speed and decrease mana cost really helped me to favor it.. I don't need it too often, but I enjoy the bigger heal instead of spam.. (it's especially nice when I see those 2k heals.)

replies.author: Mug_O_Tea
replies.text: There is no HW spam

replies.author: Dastion
replies.text: Forest’s Renewal probably isn’t as great as it feels. It is our biggest heal but not by much. It heals for ~10% more than Superior Heal while being 0.25s slower and ~12% less efficient on your mana. Add that to the fact that, with multiclassing, upgrading Superior Heal results in a faster, more efficient heal usable by several classes and there isn’t any real logical reason to use Forest’s Renewal - let alone for it in to even exist in its current state. If it’s just occasional burst heals you need then Healing Waters is way better for that. Inefficient bigger heals do have a place in modern MMOs. But in this situation it’s barely better in exchange for a pretty hefty extra mana cost and EQ has always been a game of losing by attrition. There might be some slim use cases I’m not thinking of but it’s really just a poorly designed spell that hasn’t received any love from when it was imported from the original game.

replies.author: Tover
replies.text: I'm not saying that it's better, just that I enjoy it more..The reality is that the great bulk of my healing comes from HoTs and War regen, not instants..... That said, in 3s I can cast it twice, healing for up to 5k... I can do it on demand, and infinitely. I end most D3/D4 fights at 80%+ mana. A cleric, considered the best, can only compete with this once every 18 seconds.

replies.author: Dastion
replies.text: Listen, do what you enjoy but this statement makes no sense. Clerics literally get Healing Light, which is exactly the same cast time and mana cost as Nature’s Renewal but heals for 33% more than Super Heal instead of only 10%, making it actually a mana efficient upgrade worth the increased cast time. So even if you could cast a baseline 3.75s heal with a 1.5s reuse twice in 3s and reliably crit both times… a Cleric would be able to do it better and even crit more reliably due to their Unbound AA, which is fine bc Healing is their specialty. So, again, play what you like but insisting Forest’s Renewal competes with anything isn’t backed by reality - it’ll blow through your mana faster when you want bigger heals and end up healing for less overall than just using Superior Heal. But hopefully any investment you have in the spell pays off if they ever give it attention.

replies.author: Lizelle
replies.text: I did quite a bit of testing with different weapons on a level 70 test dummy in the arena last night and today. I'm level a 50 BRD/PAL/MNK, all weapon skills are max. I had no buffs or songs on, i took all the procs out, turned off all autoskill melee abilities. I tried to keep tests to around 3 minutes each. I'm using EQ Legends Companion for parsing but I also matched logs to verify triple attacks. The parser seems pretty accurate when you're using different types of weapons in each hand or using 2 handed. When you're using two of the same type, there's no way in the logs to tell which hand is doing what. It all just shows up as crushing, punching, slashing, etc. Also, the parser does state that multi-attack is estimated. -- Impressions -- It seems like triple attacks on your secondary are very rare or not possible. In the testing I did, I saw zero triple attacks on the secondary regardless of the type or if I had a primary weapon equipped or not. Maybe this has always been the case? I'd love to hear from others on this. Triple attacks did occur on the primary hand with non-monk weapons (1H & 2H slashing, 1H & 2H blunt, 1H piercing, etc.) even with paladin only and bard only weapons. I don't have Cleric or Berserker leveled up so I couldn't test with the sky 2H blunt weapons. I did several parses of weapons of the same type in both hands to see if the stats would be similar. Wu's pulls ahead in multi-attacks against, 1H slashing, 1H blunt, and 1H piercing. Interestingly, the Smoldering Brand has the same delay as Wu's and 1H blunt is the same skill level (270) as H2H. I'm not sure why that is. -- Note -- I reorganized the info by weapon setup for readability after testing, which is why time stamps are all over the place. Also, I'm going to have to make the tests different posts as there's a character limit.

replies.author: Raph
replies.text: The impact of having a higher weapon skill cap is reduced when fighting mobs of higher level, so the sweet spot to calculate the base delta would be fighting regular mobs of your level (white con test dummy). Let's say with 1HS your base chance to hit a white con was 55%. Your skill cap with 1HB is noticably higher, so the base hit chance would be 60%, fighting white cons. Arbitrary numbers. But now you are fighting a yellow con with an avoidance value set to 120% of the white con's avoidance. Your 1HS chance to hit is now only 45,83%, while 1HB would be 50%, so the delta between the two weapon types is down from 5% to 4,17%. If you are fighting a red con with an avoidance of 150%, compared to the white con, your 1HS is down to 36,67%, and your 1HB down to 40%, so the delta is now even lower, at 3,33%. So parsing vs a white con test dummy would always give the base line hit chance / dps for different setups, while parsing vs a deep red con would give the hit chance / dps for "real" raid situations, and would always be lower than the numbers from the white con dummy fights.

1537511487176970250.title: What is the frequency of double attack with Range stance?

replies.author: 👻🏳️‍🌈Spooky🦇Bird🏳️‍🌈🎃
replies.text: I think it's the same.

replies.author: Sarion
replies.text: Its the same as the rate of double attacks from melee weapons. Last time I measured it (which was before the most recent changes to Archery) it was about 50-60% extra attacks. That said, there does seem to be something weird with archery double/triple attacks. Unlike melee, where all the attacks happen (essentially) simultaneously, there's often a delay between multiple bow shots landing. So if your bow has a delay of 60 (no haste) you might see something like: :00 - Bow Shot :02 - Bow Shot (this is your double attack) :06 - Bow Shot (New attack) I don't know for sure why it does it like that. But I suspect its an animation thing. Like with mage Fire Bolts - the damage doesn't register in the log when the spell finishes casting, it only shows up when the animation completes and the bolt hits the target. But if you test the same bow over a long period with double attack and without double attack and look at the total number of shots, the increase is substantially.

replies.author: Diogenes
replies.text: Quick test with Lava/Frost Storm. Can't have AM2 w/ Frost Storm due to levels. Observed values in game: Lava Storm base 5s Cast | level V + AA: 4.05s Focus: 3.38 Bless: 3.6 AM1: 3.24 AM2: 2.83 F+B: 2.92 F+AM1: 2.7 B+AM1: 2.88 F+B+AM1: 2.34 F+AM2: 2.36 B+AM2: 2.52 F+B+AM2: 2.05 Frost Storm base 5s Cast | level X + AA: 3.6s Focus: 3.0 Bless: 3.2 AM1: 2.88 F+B: 2.6 F+AM1: 2.4 B+AM1: 2.56 F+B+AM1: 2.08 Spell upgrades are -2% (additive) per rank, so X is -20% cast time to base cast time and it changes the base cast for all other interactions. The AA, Focus Effect, and Blessing are all the same thing but are calulcated independently agaisnt the base (upgraded) cast time and then each applied. For 4.5s cast time, both AA and blessing each subtract .45s from the final cast time to accumulate at .9s reduction. And AM1/2/3 are multiplicative after all focus effects. Demo: 5.0s x .9(level V) = 4.5s - .45(AA) = 4.05s - .45(Bless) = 3.6s - .675(Item Focus) = 2.925s x .8(AM1) = 2.34s as shown in game

replies.author: FatedEmperor
replies.text: To answer the question about why you should charm at lower levels, if you break charm by telling your pet to leave an then kill it at low HP you still get experience. Charm also instantly removes any additional pet that the mobs may or may not have and keeps it off the board, so even if it breaks you can use it wisely to have one less thing to deal with in the long run. Leveling up I never really bothered with over channel or trying to level up the charm line. The intent during those levels is drop and move to the next one. Trying to keep a stable charm mob only really comes into play in Hate, Fear, and Sky when doing bosses. Hate, fear, and sky general farm the goal becomes cycling through charms and dropping them much like the leveling process. If you are trying to get your charm to stay for as long as possible you do want to use tash (make sure you get the quested version), level up charm to 10, and make sure you use over channel when it lands. CHA does seem to play a small part but only up to a certain level If you have about 110-120 base CHA you should be fine and its not really hard achieve those levels.

replies.author: Icelf
replies.text: You can drop 3 infinitesimal notes to get level 2 and have charm last for a long time between that, tash, and overchannel. Definitely don’t need level 10 while leveling. When you consider you only get a few charm spells and will likely use it when re-leveling it’s a decent mote investment. Ultimately if you want to “drop and move to the next one” charm is the fastest way to do that.

replies.author: Cyanide Bunnyslayer
replies.text: It surprisingly holds aggro well. Don't over nuke and rip aggro, and if you do, back off until it gains it back. Against raid bosses, the mob will ignore the pet if you are in melee range so keep that in mind, however the pet will still occupy a spot on the hate list. The simplest way to maximize pet aggro is to maximize pet damage output. Give it two weapons with good procs, give high STR, DEX and ATK from buffs and gear, and spam Frenzied Burnout on cooldown. Spell Casting Subtlety also helps to reduce YOUR aggro. And if you have Feign Death from your other classes in your trio, use it

replies.author: Cyanide Bunnyslayer
replies.text: If you are coming expecting vanilla EQ pet aggro, you will be pleasantly surprised at how much better the pet can hold aggro here

1536858232717574376.title: Staff of Temperate Flux - A must have for easy pulling
1536858232717574376.report:
Just an informational post about a handy Wizard-only tool from a very easy to do, but slightly obscure quest. 

The debuff itself on the staff is not that interesting, -6 to FR and CR. What is interesting is that it is an instant cast that has no cooldown and a range of 200, the default for most spells. This is extremely useful for pulling large piles of mobs, like say if you are grinding Faction in lower level zones. Spam tab-target and the staff hotkey and start running around. It's also useful for pulling high-level mobs as it does no damage, so they won't be able to Summon you, as that starts after they've taken 1% of total hp damage. 

The icing on the cake is that it can be put in the Activated Items storage tab, and used from there, so you don't even need to use a bag slot for it.

There's also a giant difference in how a parser displays DPS of a line over an entire fight, versus it's real DPS while you are using it. Cast one Ice Comet on Naggy 0 and then finish her with a rusty dagger. The DPS line for Comet is going to suck if it's one cast over a 2 hour fight. Granted, he had Canni AA so got more total casts of DDD potentially (would be his mana pool+Canni mana+regen vs total mana of someone running Brd/Wiz/Enc with mana added from regen and ToT if you ran that). Just break his parse down though (barring crits since a build with Wiz has more and hit harder). 2700 min hit. No Wiz nuke comes close to that as a minimum hit. DDD casts (with aa's/upgrades/etc) in like 1.3/1.4 seconds with NO recast. So just as fast (if not faster) than AM3 rend/conflag/comet. So just on its face it's doing nearly double the DPS, moment to moment of Wizard nukes. Again, as I said previously, there is a break point where you have left over mana solely killing with Wiz nukes. That mana that is left over would be better spent using DDD to gain the highest possible kill time.

replies.author: SyntaxOmitted
replies.text: It just all depends on how long you can DDD for. As a rough example 2,000dps for 15 seconds using DDD + 850DPS with AM2 for 45 seconds = 68,250 damage over a minute 1,000 dps for 1 minute using AM3 = 60,000 damage. If you can't cast enough DDD's to make up for using AM2 for the rest of the fight, AM3 wins.

replies.author: Bandana Belmont
replies.text: I haven't tested it myself, but while you may be able to have all three out, are you getting the stats from the lower level ones? Assuming no fizzle rate, improved familiar is the only one you need if damage is your only concern as it is the only familiar to increase damage potency according to the wiki. If the mana regen stacks, you might want to always have improved and lesser familiars out.

replies.author: Ari Aquitane
replies.text: I've tested by summoning both and checking my stat changes. They do not stack, so there is no need to use Lesser Familiar once you have the AA. If Improved Familiar is already summoned, it will block the cast of Lesser Familiar. If you use Improved Familiar while Lesser Familiar is already summoned, it will replace the Lesser Familiar buffs from your bar, but keep the visual component. replies.author: SyntaxOmitted
replies.text: Wizard is a powerhouse with both of those classes. The class itself is very very strong in single target. Probably #2 to a specifically built Bard DDD build (which also uses Wiz, but more for the passives). Makes SK life taps super good on a crit (20%ish of the time). So lots of sustain. They both count as INT classes, so the Arcane Mastery invocation scales to level 2. Bard and Wiz make Denon's Desperate Dirge absolutely massive in damage for aoe or even single target if you build for mana. Though aoe will be more dangerous running SK instead of Enc and you won't have as much mana for DDD.

replies.author: Apollonius
replies.text: The problem with Harm Touch is that until the end game, it’s pretty useless. Fights don’t last long enough for the DoT component to be noticeable, while its counterpart LOH is exceptional both early on and late game. At a minimum the initial damage of HT needs a buff to address the ability’s lack of utility prior to level 50. Ideally the cooldown be brought down to 15 minutes as well.

replies.author: Larsen
replies.text: It would be nicer if it was a plain DD like it was back in the day, so multiple SKs can use it on a boss. The reason it was turned into a DoT was to prevent 40 SKs from instakilling stuff, but that's not a thing in EQL.

replies.author: Cald
replies.text: Get leech touch. Put reave on auto. Use HT as needed. Profit. To actually add something productive: It seems well balanced for what it is, in its current state. 1536358747180499024.title: Smite mana cost question
1536358747180499024.report: Does anybody know if the three percent is based off of current level base max mana or does it scale with gear and always take three percent of max manapool regardless of how large the pool is.

replies.author: Timminz101
replies.text: It’s 2% of current max mana per hit. If it misses you don’t lose anything

replies.author: Shinra Kuonji (Twice Punished)
replies.text: Also, if it double or triple attacks, it will consume 2% mana and grant the 1 minute cooldown reduction on LoH per hit. So a lucky triple hit will eat 6% of your Mana.

replies.author: Kromean
replies.text: It converts the 2% of max mana into 3.5x damage. If you have 5000 mana smite will use 100 mana (2%) and do 350 damage.

1536210314461184113.title: War/clr/enc
1536210314461184113.report:
From anyone that’s playing this combo, how does the playstyle feel and how does combat work? Are you relying heavily on pet damage? Are there any common issues with the build? Are you running 2h or dw?

Also curious whether you feel if it’s more powerful than war/clr/brd? It’s probably more micromanagement I imagine, but the haste, slow, mez and charm skills are all better.

replies.author: Bleedalbeans
replies.text: I did war/clr/enc 1-50. Just unlocked Bard in PoS. I feel like this combo can walk into any room and due to AoE Mez and Promised Renewal you are probably better poised to survive than any other combo. That being said, you can't kill your way out of those situations quickly. Charm pet damage is great, and definitely the answer to your low damage woes at higher levels (enchanter pally pet is probably better till mid-level) Cleric healing seems like overkill, and might be what makes me consider swapping it for Shaman to increase DPS, but then should I swap out chanter too, because slow and haste overlap between the classes? Cleric DPS with undead is pretty good though, and you can easily only face undead for most of 1-50 if you want. Cleric healing, while probably overkill, does make you feel pretty safe as long as the mana holds up even when being circle beaten by yellows and reds. War/clr/enc can do d4 everything pretty much with lower gear that many other combos, but I doubt its the most optimized for any one raid other than maybe PoS (and enchanter does the heavy lifting there). I did d0 Yael at 40, d0 dragons at 41, d2 planes at 46, d4 planes at 50 without sweating or pushing too hard. I solo PoS boss rush with charmed bee/meteor in about 30 mins. It is a great combo that can probably survive anything with little forethought. Slow going dps unless you get good charmed pets which can be a headache in other ways. replies.author: straydogsteve
replies.text: There was a post on the subreddit I read about this. Ranger gets much better returns than 1 AC per 10 past soft cap. Credit to the OP “smurfalidocious”: “There's several threads, and you can even look at the softcaps in the game files themselves in EQL\Resources\ACMitigation.txt. The AC Cap is a 'soft' cap, at which point the Soft Cap Multiplier comes into play. Looking at the first entry, it reads: Warrior at level 1 has an AC Softcap of 312 worn/buff AC, after which every point of AC past 312 you get 0.35 AC per point beyond. At level 50 (1^50^410^0.35) a Level 50 Warrior will cap at 410 worn/buff AC and get 0.35 points for every point of worn/buff AC beyond that. Conversely, the line (2^1^274^0.3^) is Cleric at level 1 has a softcap of 274 AC and each point past that provides 0.3 points. Shields aren't affected by the soft cap multiplier and always provide their full worn AC benefit. These are just the base values, too, and don't take Combat Stability into account, which pushes the armor softcap up by a flat percentage. And yes, AC buffs from spells count towards the softcap, and provide the same diminished returns when you exceed it. For the softcap returns, rather than make everyone look through this file to find per-class, here they are: Warrior: 0.35 Paladin/Shadow Knight: 0.33 Ranger: 0.315 Cleric/Monk/Bard: 0.3 Beastlords/Berserkers/Rogues/Shamans: 0.28 Druids: 0.265 Enc/Wiz/Mag/Nec: 0.25 That's also not quite the whole story since Warriors have an innate 5% damage reduction - essentially the RNG that does damage calculation can never roll a 'max' result against Warriors, only the second-best result, which pushes them ahead of Knights for tanking innately even beyond the .02 softcap they have over knights.”

replies.author: G_Funk
replies.text: A way to look at any Hybrid + Parent class is that those hybrid classes do not get spell school specialization. The parent class does. So pairing any classes like BST/PAL/RNG/SHD with their parent spell casting class now grants them access to a skill they didn't have. Hybrids trend towards getting more out of the spell casting from their parent than what they give that parent class. However, the pairing often does open up some itemization that the parent class may not otherwise get. When you pair up classes with the same attributes to scale something like Mana, that is also something that can benefit the combo. So, SHD being an INT tank does open some doors to INT-based items that any of the INT casters don't have access too. This includes some really good SHD-only Plane of Sky items with INT on it. In other words, if you want to build your mana pool up while leveraging a tank class, then SHD can be a very solid choice. In the more specific, SHD does enhance a very small amount of what NEC brings in the form of Soul Abrasion and the Unbound AA for lifetaps, but SHD is likely going to be the class benefiting the most from the pairing. How you approach the strategy of running a hybrid and its parent might alter some gear choices. The combo is not a waste of time, but it is also not some secret unlock to the best thing in the game either.

replies.author: Trykk
replies.text: Inversion stance adds 0 dps. You cast spells faster but the extra time gets added to global cooldown so you cast the same amount of spells over time. Imagine a spell takes 3 seconds to cast and you have a normal 1.5 second global cooldown. That means every 4.5 seconds you cast one spell and in one minute of chain casting you get off 13.3 spells. With inversion that spell now takes 1s to cast, much faster, but the extra 2 seconds go to the gcd so between casts now you wait 3.5 seconds. That means its the same 4.5 seconds to cast and the same 13.3 casts per minute. Now same spell in AM3 takes 1.8 seconds to cast but the gcd is also reduced to .9 so now you cast one spell every 2.7 seconds instead. That means in one minute you get 22.2 casts or basically 9 extra casts which is a 60 percent dps increase. AM3 also makes your spells 20 percent cheaper to cast to offset the faster casting. Its insane value and basically a 70 percent dps increase over inversiob

1535521107560636426.title: Warrior Threat (WAR/BER/BRD)
1535521107560636426.report:
I am playing WAR/BER/BRD in our little 4 man group. I was planning to be the tank. We have hit raiding and cleared Naggy/Vox/Yael all on D4.

My problem is that every fight starts off okay with threat. I can open with a rampage and Heroic Leap. I have a good amount of threat. On the bosses though, around 40% I just cant keep up with the rest of the group. From here till the boss dies it is just a spam taunt situation as I cant keep up with them. Is anyone else having a hard time with this? Would really like some insight on this.

Other group members:
ROG/BER/RNG
SHM/NEC/WIZ
ENC/CLR/RNG

replies.author: MAOU
replies.text: So I have been having similar issues with my group and basically what im seeing is the normal issue warriors have made worse. So in early expansions of EQ warriors have no good agro abilities. HL helps but it's still not enough. We don't have the berate line which would help too. Then you add on that classes that are already high threat dps class now add in 2 more classes and it becomes worse. In my group Im war/rng/shm and a buddy is sk/mnk/shm. Im not ripping agro from sk/mnk that can spam harm touch and monk damage. The way the game is setup atm it's very hard to keep agro on one person. In our 4 man it just bounces around most of the time unless the SK has a few harm touches in. But as a warrior good luck trying to hold the dps classes from ripping agro off you all day long.

replies.author: Kärrigaste verkstaden
replies.text: Are you using proc weapons like ykesha? Helps a bit with aggro and if you can sustain the damage switching to either striker or offensive stance should upp the dps/threat mby. Or switching to berserker stance before using taunt/rampage or similar to reduce the cd before going back to another stance

replies.author: EmanuelZorg
replies.text: I'm currently SHM WAR BER and can pull aggro easy by casting in succession slow malo and incapacitate, which is not really sustainable or practical but makes me think that ENC is the way to go for aggro generation. Tash is very fast cast and low mana, as is Color Skew the pb aoe stun, and mez always seems to piss mobs off so maybe try that? You could fall back to the slow debuff that worked for the SHM but are mana and cast time expensive.. This is just theory but I'd like to give it a try or hear others experiences with WAR/ENC/X for tanking.

replies.author: EmanuelZorg
replies.text: For your build, doesn't bard have a lot of debuffs? try stacking those

replies.author: EmanuelZorg
replies.text: I honestly don't know bards so looked up the spell list: Selo's Consonant Chain ought to piss the off terribly, snare AND slow, that's taunt gold.

replies.author: Ik
replies.text: it feels bad that we have to look so deeply outside of warrior for threat

replies.author: Ik
replies.text: I should have picked anything but a warrior if I wanted to tank, is the message I got

replies.author: Zelathor
replies.text: Bard does have a lot of dot songs, and I do play the songs. The songs seem to generate little to no threat. I am not sure if this is something they did to make bard not rip threat in live, but it seems they just generate very low threat. The problem with bard and the reason I will be getting rid of it asap is that anytime you press an AA ability like Area Taunt, Heroic Leap, Rampage etc, it stops your melody. This is compounded by the fact that you cant press disciplines while your melody is going either. So Skull Bash and Tendon Rip cant be used unless you halt your melody. On top of all of this, WAR/BER really seems to want 2handers. By doing so, you loose the option all the instrument focuses. This also forces you to have weapons/shields in your any slot. I picked bard because I thought it would bring some nice utility for the group, but with WAR/BER it feels more of a burden than anything else.

replies.author: Zelathor
replies.text: So I do sit in berserker stance as much as possible. From all of my data, it outpaces offensive by a considerable amount. I do have procs. I have tried Yekesha and Earthquake procs. Neither seem to make much of a difference. I was thinking of trying the tash proc cause I know it generates a good amount of threat. I will do more raids tonight and see. Also last night we had a PAL/BER/WIZ come raid with us and they seemingly generate threat just by existing. I am not sure if paladin gets some sort of built in threat bonus with bash, but they could hold threat off me with very little effort. I thought they were spamming their stun spells, but apparently they were not.

replies.author: xayle
replies.text: That combo has nothing to keep agro. You can taunt then leap if taunt is successful but you'll lose agro shortly after if dps in your group is half awake. I use group heals from my /CLR to keep agro.

replies.author: Zelathor
replies.text: WAR has nothing to keep aggro, so you use cleric to keep aggro. That just seems like a major design flaw. WAR is supposed to be a tank. Paladin and Shadowknight do not seem to have threat problems. Hopefully they can add a passive AA that gives more threat to warrior or maybe have cleave do more threat somehow

replies.author: xayle
replies.text: You won’t like the answer but Warriors always had issues keeping threat and knights always had tools that let them do it better in classic. I wouldn’t mind an AA or something that warriors could toggle on and off to buff threat from white damage… but this is modeled off classic EQ so here we are.

replies.author: Zelathor
replies.text: What a great opportunity for the version of EQ that is reimagining things to fix!

replies.author: #Hashtag
replies.text: Warriors eventually got Strike of Ire AA which procced hate which could be cool here, but I don't know what expansion it was introduced.

replies.text: Even with this test there's so much variance that it's tough to make definitive conclusions. replies.author: Gourd
replies.text: I assume they forgot to turn on the level scaling for Blood Draw, so it's forever stuck at 86 damage. Poisons in general need work. If you reapply Blood Draw 1s before it would have ticked, you reset that timer and have to wait 6 seconds to get the heal. Befuddling Strike just straight up doesn't work at all, it never procs. Banishing Strike removes poisons even though it's apparently not supposed to. Stunning Venom is nigh useless since the nerf to stuns. Cobra Venom is literally useless because it only does 86 damage, and isn't a DoT like it probably should be. Concussive Strike is nigh useless because poisons are so unreliable that you need the stars to align so that the poison procs while an enemy is casting, then they have to not resist it, then they have to actually be affected by it since it's only a 75% chance for some stupid reason. As for a solution to all those problems, fixing the bugs is obvious. Banishing Strike shouldn't be dispelling poisons, since they're poisons, not spells. Befuddling Strike just needs to be fixed so it actually procs. Cobra Venom and Asp Venom should be dots with the same duration as Blood Siphon/Draw. We should be able to level poisons using motes, and doing so should lower enemy resists, increase duration, and increase damage.

replies.author: Essay
replies.text: Its not as simple as that being locked to 30 delay based on the testing others have done (this is for summoned pets only). Here was the best summary I found and my testing shows the same outcome: > Cudgel of fools reduced my pets swings to 5-6 seconds. Earthshaker with a higher delay is 2-3 seconds Yes, this is because Cudgel is a better ratio weapon than the pet's base ratio, so it uses both the damage and the delay of the cudgel to take advantage of it's higher ratio. Earhtshaker even though it has very high damage has a lower ratio than the pet's ratio, so the pet just uses the weapons damage but with the pet's default swing speed (30) so an Earthshaker when used by a level 10 BST pet becomes a 74/30 weapon which is way better than the Cudgel. Cudgel maxed out is 90/52 which is a 1.73 ratio Earthshaker on warder is 74/30 which is a 2.46 ratio Hope this makes sense."

1535055135334473769.title: Nec stance when you are doing the tanking (as a knight)

I had been playing a traditional melee focused dps class and using offensive and striker stance mostly.

Switching out melee dps for NEC, I was wondering if I should just do defensive or evasive and give up on dps?

If the dots to all the work should I just sort of be a sponge?

replies.author: Cyanide Bunnyslayer
replies.text: Evasive will let you dodge incoming attacks, so that your spells don't get interrupted. I recommend switching to Evasive to get your spells down, and then Defensive or Offensive as the need arises. When its time to cast again, go back to Evasive.

replies.author: Cyanide Bunnyslayer
replies.text: Inversion is fantastic when you have to get a spell off asap, but Empowered and Arcane Mastery are the MVPs for caster invocations. Empowered for maximum damage (especially for DoTs), Arcane Mastery for chain casting nukes and non-DoT debuffs

replies.author: Shivan_Angel
replies.text: I bet its using the focus templates that were updated later in the eq life cycle. Before foci had specific effects on pets like raised damage by 2, level by 1 etc. The sol ro focus items just boosted the pets hp to the next level”tier”. So focused water pets had the hp of an earth pet etc. earth pet just got an ac boost. Eventually they changed them to a power increase notated by a number. Shovel, broom etc were 5, the staves 10, etc etc. these raised the pets level and all the stats accordingly and let you hit breakpoints. For example the PoTime pet focus would increase your water pets level enough to actually put it in the OoW tier of pets (on the tlp), which boosted its dps by like 30% because the difference between the pop water pet and the oow water pets templates were so significant. Basically instead of making a new template for each pet based on the focus item, the made a template for each level of the pet, and focus effects increased pet level to boost their effectiveness. Was a much simpler process.

replies.author: Jokon
replies.text: Druid DoTs are in a strange place. There's two lines we care about at level 50; Sunscorch and Swarm. Druid also have the Blistering Line, but it doesn't come into play at 50 due to level wonk. The two representatives we care about are Vengeance of the Wild (Sunscorch) and Drifting Death (Swarm). What's bizarre about these is that they start out pretty comparable to our nukes, and then rapidly outstrip them as they level up. They do this because they increase not just in damage, but in *duration*; basically, any DoT that does less *total* damage than a nuke is a loss of mana and DPS. It's pretty interesting actually - although Vengeance starts out doing a bit more damage as Starfire (732 vrs 634), it actually keeps parity at much lower levels of upgrade(1022 damage at rank 6 compared to 1041 damage for Starfire at rank *10*). This is pretty important to keep in mind; druids are intended to DoT targets and fill with nukes. You do need to keep the rotation going though and note that the DoTs get much, much more powerful with levels.

1534768317859106936.title: Alright it's been a few days - how do we feel about BST?
1534768317859106936.report: I know there was a lot of concern in open beta about BST being left out a bit, but with all the changes leading up to live, how do you think BST fares at the moment?

replies.author: teewiler
replies.text: Still behind overall, down with rogues and berserkers. The pet absolutely sucks from about 20 until you get the 46 one leveled up

replies.author: w1oux3v
replies.text: Gotcha. But sounds like the leveled up max pet is throwing some punches? My initial build plan was MNK/BRD/BST but I traded out BST for SHM last minute. Kind of looking back at BST like

replies.author: Broken Stoic
replies.text: BST pet (on pet page) BST class itself, is underwhelming.. It does have a slow and some heals.. some unique buffs. All the AA being post 30 is rough and most of them dont really play to the kit all that well. even the flurry is a little strange since their pet has such poor accuracy. The pet can do "some" dps, im not sure what i would rate it over all, i have been seeing 100-120 dps and that isnt much for how much you have to put into it. thats at +10 46 pet with REALLY good gear.

replies.author: w1oux3v
replies.text: Man. You guys and your extremely thorough spreadsheets, haha Good write up, appreciate it. 100-120 dps at the top end does seem underwhelming

replies.author: w1oux3v
replies.text: The pet spell level thing I think is a great change/improvement overall for the game, but its also bringing up classes like SHM where their pet is pretty darn good now too when leveled up Which doesn't directly "take" anything from BST, but it does keep the gap small

replies.author: Faydark
replies.text: One niche (maybe?) that beastlord has is that caster mobs are not an issue. Between the interrupt on the pet proc and the interrupts from alternating ice nukes (which are decent efficient dps on their own), you can basically stop any caster mob from casting, even with the diminished returns on stuns (I think these interrupts don't seem to trigger it). Overall, I think Beastlord in EQL is much better than Beastlord in normal EQ through Classic. I feel it fits well with various builds, but by no means all, of course. It does what monk does well enough (at least until/if they introduce melee burn discs, then Beastlord will be left in the dust as usual). The DPS between them is comparable, monk brings FD and a bigger heal (with a bigger cooldown). On the shaman side of things, shaman is better in all respects, but Beastlord does "enough". If you want to have monk/shaman in your trio, but also two other classes, Beastlord fits there. Pet stat issues are still an issue. Hopefully further changes are made to improve things. But overall, it's fun to play and that's what's important to me. I plan to level monk so eventually i'll compare them at level 50 (I've previously only compared them at level 30).

replies.author: RooBee
replies.text: Sounds like both the Beastlord and the Warder ( able to cast it ) requires the Bloodlust AA to not only be a unique AA but a boost in Dps over all. Devs?

replies.author: DirusJay
replies.text: BST is not good. Shm does basically everything that BST does only way better. The only reason to play BST over shm is pet buffs and pet gear slots. Even the shm pet is decent. I'm not sure how a hybrid of two of the best classes in the game is so bad but it is. Only good thing is there are a ton of minor tweaks they could do to improve BST. Like better combat skills/access. Can't tank, low DPS, low utility, low healing and bad pulling options. The Warder is probably the biggest issue. Of all the pet users BST leans on theirs far more but the pet isn't great.

replies.author: Faydark
replies.text: Your summary at the end is just a tad hyperbolic. Beastlord tanks as well as monk does (I'm yet to see a parse showing monk tanking better than BST at these levels, since they both get the same skills, just different skill caps). Beastlord has similar (but less) DPS to monk, the tradeoff is the utility beastlord has. Low healing, I'll grant Bad pulling: not really specific to Beastlord though, many classes are bad at pulling. I'd put Beastlord as "average", certainly not the worst. I'd also suggest Magician relies on their pet more than Beastlord does (currently at least, it's slightly different once the DPS buffs that require a pet come in, if they do for EQL).

replies.author: Darkov
replies.text: I think the BST is in an okay place, considering it wasn't designed to cap out at level 50. All I really think they need to do is increase the damage output of the Warder, both its melee and magical attacks. The class will still be a little off by itself, as its not complete at 50, but I don't see the point of them spending time adding new spells or adjusting the spell levels when Kunark will turn up at the end of the year, and we have two other classes in the trio to make up for current short comings.

replies.author: Uncle Brian
replies.text: Maybe good enough if the dev fix the problem of many stats on the equipment has no use to pet. And let us choose what spell it use.

replies.author: Rutts
replies.text: Im current leveling one up to pair with my mage chanter combo to see how she runs will report back in a few days.

replies.author: Broken Stoic
replies.text: I think if they took the pet and made it zerker again, that wouldnt be a terrible move. they would need to "fix" frenzy so that it didnt under perform even if it was just for the pet. I think using bloodlust as a way to balance it will only make many of the other classes that are already strong, even more strong as a result by just taking bloodlust. Its a fun ability, it was cool in another iteration, however it was also massively imbalanced and was used in almost every way to exploit damage, mass pulling, and a lot of the things the devs here have gone against. So while folks may want it, i think its unlikely to make an appearance. They have AA's currently that dont really "do" anything. I think thats true of a lot of the classes but would love to see them normalize required levels on AA in general. There is already a massive control method for how many aa and when people get aa. Having level reqs doesnt make a lot of sense. Maybe allowing their haste and attack to exceed haste cap? Allowing them an accuracy buff component to their pet as an AA. Many of their buffs dont stack with other classes buffs and it is somewhat antithetical to the triple class synergy system. I think they have a place in the game but I also think they might be in the worst position against all other classes. Someone has to be at the bottom but that doesnt mean it feels any better to be there.

replies.author: DirusJay
replies.text: It has less melee skills and lower caps on nearly every skill. BST utility? A slow. That's it and limited access to ways to make slow actually stick.

replies.author: Faydark
replies.text: It does have lower caps on every skill. But throw both classes on a parser and you'll see that those skill caps aren't really a major difference between the two classes. Monk has triple attack, punches and kicks. Beastlord has alternating ice nukes, dots, pet that uses ice nukes and proc spell. The DPS is pretty close - I haven't parsed them both at 50 yet though, and I expect monk to pull ahead once the game really moves into meleequest with future expansions and items. Monk Utility: mend and reliable feign death. Beast Utility: slow (easy to land if you raise its ranks, lands on the raid bosses when they're 16 levels higher than you). Mana/HP/endurance regen buff, HP/atk buff, permanent str/dex/AC self buff, AC buff, str/dex/stam buffs. Spell shutdown (between pet proc spell and your two fast cast ice nukes.). Snare. Unreliable Feign Death. Paragon. I feel like a lot of people comparing Beastlord to Monk just don't play Beastlord or don't know how to play Beastlord tbh, seen some crazy takes on the comparisons that aren't backed up with evidence. I'm prepared to be completely wrong once I get to parse level 50 monk vs level 50 beastlord. But at the levels I've parsed them at so far, I feel they're both pretty balanced vs each other for the things they can do.

replies.author: Seafoams
replies.text: I've already posted some of these in feedback channel, but.. 1. Make Paragon do a % of hp/mana/endurance instead of the small flat number it is now. A fresh 50 has enough HP and mana that it's pretty pointless to begin with. And lower it's CD... 2. Lower cooldown of our Spirit Frenzy AA (100% haste 250attack) - either just a flat reduction, or a mechanic like how smite lowers lay on hands. Our frost spell like could reduce its cd. Gives us a cool burn mechanic that already exists. Current 12 min cd and 40ish second duration is bad with EQL's pace. 3. Growl line from other expansions - self and pet % dps increase with a HoT component. This gives us both DPS that we're missing pretty badly, as well as some sustain. 4. Remove the BST tag from our pet - make it pure melee as war/monk or war/zerk (to remove the low-level casting that lowers it's DPS) OR give us a UI element like our autocast UI where we can tell the pet what to/not to cast. Letting us turn off terrible things like sicken, but also letting us define his role. Maybe you want him to only slow? Maybe be a healer? Maybe no spells at all? Play how you want. 5. Give beastlord their own combat abilities like flying kick. In later expansions I'm pretty sure they get combat abilities like Rake? Again, helps with our DPS. 6. Pet Procs - Later expansions give pets a proc that slows the target and also there's a pet proc that heals the targets target. Both would be AMAZING, but especially the heal proc

1534757936696398036.title: Pet tanking raid mobs
1534757936696398036.report:
Today j got my pet spell up 6 levels which makes him a level 49 warrior sk with 7.4k hp.
I took him to sky and had him tank every raid target from first to last island. I had him tank inny d0-3, CT d0-2, Yael d0-4. 

My trio is a shaman, necromancer, berserker. I didn't intend to do a pet tank run but I decided to try it when I had already hit 50 with berserker.

I haven't tried higher difficulty CT but I imagine it wouldn't be too difficult. 

The strategy was to send pet in, malo, slow, and stack 6 dots. Using hots on the pet, puma, and feign death to keep aggro on him. If I had any adds I'd tank them myself and burn them down first before applying dots on main target.

1534665133761233016.title: Pet Damage Scaling w/ DW and Stat Boosts -- Any data?
1534665133761233016.report:
Has anyone done extended parsing showing the damage benefits of stacking strength and high ratio dual wield weapons on pets? My assumption is currently that if the damage does not modify the pet's max hit, it doesn't actually affect it (and in most cases the delay is not seeming to apply either).

IMO, ideally ratio would impact pets in some way to give them a mechanism to scale better.

Additionally, would be good to understand how stat stacking, i.e. strength, impacts their damage and whether it's worthwhile or not. I plan to invest time into parsing eventually, but was hoping someone already had some.

replies.author: Cyanide Bunnyslayer
replies.text: Pets will use weapon damage/delay if it is an "Improvement" according to whatever internal logic the game thinks is an improvement. It's most evident at lower levels, less so at high levels. STR and ATK is supposed to improve the likelihood of hitting for maximum damage, so that can be something easy to parse. It also skews the bell curve more towards maximum damage and away from minimum damage. DEX is supposed to improve the likelihood of triggering a proc, so again something that can be relatively easy to parse.

replies.author: Mitagi
replies.text: Str is suppose to Increase atk specificially the ATK value as a whole every few points I believe 3 and as a secondary function bring the internal pet damage minimum with/out weapon closer to the maximum damage. Atk is suppose to dictate value the player can alter to effect the internal pet formulas for damage, Crit Damge and Hit chance. And the effective ness of strength based combat skills IE Bash. Dex is suppose to effect proc triggers, crit chance and Dex based combat skills IE backstab. Agility effects AC and Evasive AC and increase the internal minimums towards the maximums AC /Evasive AC is what is says on the tin Stamina is supposed to effect HP INT and WIsdom are suppose to effect depending on the type of pet Mana, spell damage to a degree, spell success rate, and spell resistence. Cha...does nothing Most of the stats are broken and either don't contribute what they are suppose to. Or only partially the only stats that really matter on pets is AC/ATK/Ratio of Weapon/ and Haste

1534579851594432663.title: TIPS FOR GRIMROT (TORRID CORRUPTOR)
1534579851594432663.report:
For Those of Evil minds Interested in the Torrid Corruptor line and find themselves with a soulfire in hand and the soul from Brother Hayle.... Lord Grimrot has a bit of science behind his spawn. 
For OPEN WORLD (PART ONE)
1st. Swapping difficulty picks in S Karana is good for when you do not have instance charges. This will let you potentially find him up during low server pop times. 

2nd. There will be many other knights doing this quest... do NOT be afraid to join forces! After much testing, watching timers, and seeing just how rare the living version of Grimrot is, it behooves all of the knights to coordinate and work together spread out across different pick difficulties to get initial timers on the placeholders. Your entire 4 man team can complete this quest as a single unit, will explain below. 

3rd. Placeholder Camping: The Brewall Maps Label for Lord Grimrot is 100% accurate down to the tiny little hut he spawns under. A Putrid Skeleton is his placeholder. It is going to hit you for a -2 Bloodsabers rep. Do not be fooled by the other Putrid skeletons near the location, the one you want is the ONLY one that is standing, the rest will appear to be lying down, do not kill these
 as they will lower your Bloodsabers rep (by -1), and you need to maintain Kindly in order to turn in to Lord Grimrot. The respawn timer is a wide range from 3 to 4 hours. It can spawn at any point after the 3 hour mark so just turn timestamps on in your combat log or whatever displays your faction hits and notate the time (I've had a few at exactly 3 hours ive had one at exactly 4 hours and a couple just under 4 hours). Once your party has multiple difficulty picks on a timer you begin to increase your odds of seeing a Lord Grimrot spawn.

replies.author: RepoMane
replies.text: For Private Instance Creation (PART TWO) 1st. Get familiar with the /time command. This will be important as you will want to start creating your instances to fish for living Lord Grimrot at 6 AM GAME TIME. Bright and early in the morning. We did many tests of the old internet information on Grimrot saying 6pm to 9PM killing a PH then to spawn a live version. With EQL there would be no feasible to way to "hold a PH alive" until a specific time, if another knight on the quest shows up odds are hes going to kill everything in the area he thinks is a Placeholder. So we apply this general idea instead to private instance creation. We created many private instances fishing for a living Lord Grimrot at 6PM Game time and saw about a 50/50 rate of PH OR the UNDEAD version of Lord Grimrot. After about 4 or 5 Dead versions we gave up on that and tested 6 AM game time instance creation. After 2 PHs we still didn't see any Undead version and on the 4th attempt I finally had a live Lord Grimrot in my instance. Use your charges wisely! Coordinate with your party, let one person "fish", making a private MULTIPLAYER D0 respawning instance of S Karana. If they land a live Grimrot awesome! They can then reinvite you to a party, go down to the pick difficulty button and click "Invite Group" button once everyone is in, at that point they can all join your instance by clicking the pick difficulty button and "Enter Instance" . At the point you and your party get a living Lord Grimrot (Congratulations!!) make sure everyone has CLICKED on the soul they got from Brother Hayle and that they have at least Kindly rep (there have been bugs reported saying Amiable was sufficient to turn in the sword and soul but I wouldn't rely on that, just get to kindly) and then they can turn in their Dark reaver and Soul. Once everyone is good, BURN HIM DOWN and win the game.

replies.author: Korshay
replies.text: The in game description is trash. Here's what's relevant: +5 levels means your AoE DoT spells are doing more damage. Traditional EQ mechanics modify resistance checks based on level disparities, with higher enemy levels significantly boosting resist rates. So you want every source possible to reduce resists. You'll see this first hand when fighting mobs in PoSky, such as Eye of Veeshan being a level 70 mob. I have Selo's Chords of Cessation X which is -150 MR. Even in Overchannel Invocation, raid bosses routinely resist it.

replies.text: In EQL, I don't know what that level disparity looks like under the hood. I could only find two references in the patch notes: June 2, 2026: Removed enemy resist bonus from enemies that are yellow considered. 1534289672392413194.title: What are we using for weapons?
1534289672392413194.report:
I'm currently using fist weapons, but I'm not sure if they maintained the hand-to-hand bonus damage monks get or if we should be using one hand blunts? 

What speeds for offhand and manhand?


This is my first time seriously playing EverQuest and I know a lot has changed. 

Is it still just best ratio?

replies.author: Yxtta
replies.text: From a purely monk aspect ignoring other classes you have in your trio. Flaming fists are probably the best until you can snag either some smoldering brands in the hole or raid weapons. Roll best ratio. Try to stick to 1hb/h2h for the accuracy bonus due to higher skill mod. Unless you have access to knight weapons those are worth losing the higher skill cap for. Like mentioned with knight weapons could also run into exceptions if your trio also has access to the proc from say earthshaker. It’s higher dmg dd component could likely turn a 1hs weapon worth using also. As far as the dmg bonus. The innate dmg bonus to hand to hand is ignored if using a weapon like flaming fist and the flaming fists damage bonus takes over just like any weapon I think the bonus dmg starts showing up mid 20s-30 range for weapons. Weapon speed matters much less. But can be meaningful depending on situations like a mob having a ds and your combo not having a dispell to remove it, or if you can’t sustain through the increased damage intake a slower weapon to take less ds dmg could be impactful. But long story short, ratio >all else, 99% of the time.

replies.author: Bandana Belmont
replies.text: Dual wield (dw) and two-handers (2h) are the common terms used as well as saving time and effort. 2h will NEVER out dps dw under your hypothetical. Dual wield, from what I heard, at max skill cap and ambidexterity purchased for monks using 75% of your off hand ratio

replies.author: Bandana Belmont
replies.text: More specifically, if you dual wield two weapons with the same ratio, you effectively have 175% of that ratio. Using a 2 hander with the same ratio as a 1 hander is only 100%. Of course this only applies under your proposed hypothetical. Reality has 2handers (for the most part) with higher ratios than a 1 handed weapon. That being said, wu's fist of mastery is primary only, and is a much higher ratio than the best 2 hander available to monks.

If you're casting 2h might make more sense because you may lose less swings while casting. You also trigger fewer enemy ripostes while your ripostes hit harder. But in just raw attacking damage right now dual wield is simply a better option for monks.

replies.author: Boisterous
replies.text: I wrote up a little bit about bard macros here Melody isn't a thing that has to be turned off - you interrupt it when you cast, but you do have to turn it back on. Bard songs don't get cancelled, they run for a duration and then end. Charm, like mez, is cast on a mob, lasts for a duration, then ends. So you can charm a mob and then immediately start casting other songs or spells until the charm wears off and you need to cast it again. So yes you charm, then melody a few songs, then charm again when it wears off. Depending on which charm you're doing and what you've upgraded it to, this could be 18 seconds or upwards of 90.

It doesn't get any better in later expansions until Underfoot when there's a PB AE mez with Wave of Slumber. So I doubt we'll ever see a PB AE mez in EQL.

replies.author: Ponzicar

replies.author: Kethigar
replies.text: oh yeah back in the day bard mezzing was a full time job. mez a target tab, mez another target, tab etc. the lost melee dps wasn't a big deal because our melee dps was fairly horrid. but I always used to tell groups, "if we get extra adds, I'm going to charm one FIRST, and have it hit one mob so I can control two at once. so don't be surprised when a mob gets charmed". I always defaulted to charm being my primary go-to CC before mez, because bard mez required complete commitment. in EQL so far, I've operated much the same, with the caveat that our melee dps is *not* horried (if you're taking a melee dps class). so I try to lull pull first, then if I get adds I charm one, then if I feel I need to start mezzing, I'll use the extended target list to pick a mob, start singing mez, and before it lands, tab back to my attack target so I lose minimal dps

1533886985368895611.title: Instrument of Nife - Upgrades
1533886985368895611.report: I was told in General to make it a priority to upgrade the Instrument of Nife self buff - does it actually increase the damage of the proc? What about any other self buffs. Can some pros help me here please?

replies.author: Shinra Kuonji (Twice Punished)
replies.text: Proc buffs like Nife deal one ranks worth of damage per two ranks of actual upgrade. So you always want to upgrade it in even numbers. Very much worth it. At rank 8 it does a little bit north of 300 damage. As for other buffs, they do not gain potency from upgrades. They only gain duration, reduced cooldown, and reduced Mana cost. So upgrading other buffs is purely a quality of life question. The notably, he'll overtime effects like celestial cleansing do gain potency with each rank, as well as duration increase and Mana cost and decrease. So buffs and heal over time effects are operating on a different set of rules.

replies.author: Shinra Kuonji (Twice Punished)
replies.text: Also, just to clarify: buffs not gaining potency from upgrades is entirely by design.

replies.author: RonJohnson
replies.text: It may be worth investigsting if the paladin haste increases in potency by a relavent amount. In case you want to drop enc/sha

replies.author: Shinra Kuonji (Twice Punished)
replies.text: Buffs do not increase in potency, with the exception of proc buffs. So Valor of Marr will always be 25% haste. Its duration is already infinite, so there's no reason to upgrade it.

replies.author: Dranikos
replies.text: Almost all the regen buffs get removed by some very common DoT lines. Boil Blood is one I know for example. Chloro, Regen, Bear Form, Divine Purpose, they all go poof. Also, it reduces your mana regen for HP regen. Generally you can much more efficiently just turn the mana into HP. It's -3 Mana Regen for +8 Health Regen. Or 2.666 Health per mana. Unmodifiable (it's not affected by AAs or Improved Healing foci) Superior Healing +0 is 600 HP for 185. 3.24 Health per Mana. And that's fully modifiable by AAs and Foci (including Paladin's innate Unbound Healing AA), plus it can be upgraded for better healing AND lower mana (with each upgrade reducing mana costs by 2%, and increasing healing by ~5% or 8% IIRC). VASTLY improving the efficiency of the spell.

[Sat Aug 08 15:26:35 2026] You begin reciting the empowering invocation. ## After Swap (Increased Damage) [Sat Aug 08 15:26:45 2026] You hit a ratman warrior for 62 points of poison damage by Blood Draw Strike. Writing a script to estimate if overchannel has any affect on poison attacks.

replies.author: Razel the Rogue
replies.text: ## Results from my combat logs My scripts scanned the entire file (10.3MB. I archived everyone before level 50) and found: * Cobra Venom Strike hits: 479 * Blood Draw Strike hits: 4,242 * Total Poison-based "Hit" events: 4,721 * Overchannel activations: 11 separate sessions Poisons landed 100% on regular run of the mill Mobs like The Hole's ratmen. The only time poisons got resisted where against named mobs--which is good--they should be harder fights. Dread and Fright are resistant to magic, fire, and cold; so we would typically use poison/disease spells. Shaman and Necro's have some notable spells like Venom of the Snake and Torbas' Poison Blast. The table only shows a few note worthy sections; but when in overchannel, I had fewer resists. I did not include Innoruuk in my results because I had only 3 procs before swapping to overchannel. In recovery stance he resisted only 1 poison proc, so it would show 33% resist rate. In overchannel he resisted 8 or 16, so 50%. replies.author: ❄Ẕ𝕐𝕃𝕀𝔼❄
replies.text: Varies based on which stance you're using for delays, but effectively like this... Line 1: /pause 25, /cast 1 Line 2: /pause 30, /cast 2 Line 3: /melody 3,4,5,6 Where the first 25 pause is equal to a 2.5sec cast + gem refresh time, and the secpnd 30 sec pause is equal to a 3.0 sec cast and gem refresh time. IMO calculate the cast & gem refresh then add like 3 to the delay to ensure server delay doesnt clip it for the hotkey to work every time. But remember if you are in a stance that lowers either casting OR gem refresh, then being out of that stance will jack up the hotkey cuz the timers will be all off. But thats the gist of making a multi-cast hotkey. If you want this to also kill yoir current melody to refresh the 2 first dots add a /stop to the first 2 lines instead and mo v e thise down to lines 3 to 5.

replies.author: Shinra Kuonji (Twice Punished)
replies.text: Consider reframing the way you view smite. It's not an always on thing like other class features. It is a high impact way to convert resources into damage very quickly for when fast damage takes priority over other things. And it comes on a class that does not normally have the ability to do anything like that. Paladin's usual methodology is that slow and steady wins the race. So, being completely outside the classes normal wheelhouse, it comes at the cost of being inefficient. And that's okay. This provides you an avenue to make a choice as player as to how you want to spend your resources, and particularly, how quickly you want to burn through them. This is where metering the usage comes in. If you've got excess Mana to spend, click the button. If you're barely scraping by trying to survive, don't push the button. Not everything needs to be automated and active all the time.

replies.author: Shinra Kuonji (Twice Punished)
replies.text: One of the key factors that people tend to overlook when discussing the power level of promised renewal specifically is that it requires you to play predictively. You need to cast the spell far in advance, before damage has actually happened, and you need to be able to predict how far in advance to cast it so as to not waste healing, or not die. It's efficiency especially over the long term is largely dependent on the player's ability to do that. This also means the spell is much more powerful insights where enemy damage is very predictable and consistent, and much less powerful in fights with unpredictable spikes such as the eov. Likewise, if the player can't predict the damage consistently and time the spell properly, it loses a huge chunk of its value. More conventional heels like what the shaman has do not have this consideration. One of the big counterpoints though is that Shaman does not have much in the way of big burst heels to get back on track if things start to get out of control. With their heel over times and such they are good at maintaining your health at a consistent level, but if you drop into the danger zone, they can struggle to get back out of it.

replies.author: nirafelos
replies.text: And like, I agree that an abnormal amount of the class' power centers around the stance. Beta parsing data had BER stance further ahead than the tooltips would imply, probably due to it being easier on endurance than the others. I still think a decent portion of the "when not in the stance what do we bring that other triple-attacking classes don't" question is a little overplayed. 3 of the other 4 triple-attacking classes could be asking a variant of the same question that doesn't even include BER stance. When you really strip classes down to just the skill caps that they provide access to, the offensive and defensive melee skillsets they all provide are extremely similar. There are of course fairly obvious answers to that question -- monks bring blunt caps and mend and FD and 10% overhaste, rogues bring Shroud of Stealth and Escape and poisons, rangers bring tracking and procs and invis and 30% strikethrough and like 200 atk. We bring 6% crit and 7% flurry and a 20s cd interrupt and access to the game's best current 2handed weapon. I'm not saying these things are of equal value. EQ was always an extremely asymmetrical game. Zerker has always had less utility than the other classes, and has always had an issue of being indistinct from the warrior. As time went on in EQLive AAs and itemization did help address this. Starting this server with an extremely small selection of class AAs (and with significantly fewer offensive melee AAs than casters get in general/archetype) has had the obvious consequence of zerkers feeling indistinct from warriors.

1533289015548055613.title: Feelings on Rogue?
1533289015548055613.report:
I’ve been playing both rogue paladin enchanter and ranger paladin and enchanter and both feel quite strong. I am only level 25 so far, on both.

How are people feeling about rogues after a few days played?

replies.author: Greg The Cleric
replies.text: Rogues are good. I think a lot of folks don’t necessarily realize how nice it is to get SoS and just ignore trash in dungeons and raids.

replies.author: Razel the Rogue
replies.text: My two copper. If you like an assassin, thief, swashbuckler, or general stealthy character—the rogue fits that archetype perfectly. You can stealth from target to target taking down foes and getting away unnoticed. You get the roguish tools like lock picking, stealth, and picking pockets. You’re also an assassin with poison, backstabbing, and evade to get away. You get solid defensive skills that allow you to stand toe to toe with foes like a swashbuckling pirate ( had an in game brother that choose rogue and RPed a DE pirate), but your HP pool is limited. If you are looking for face roll dps, it doesn’t fit the bill. You’d be better served with monk or zerker. I hope one day we get a few changes (same offensive skill caps as Monk, higher parry dodge riposte skill caps, and a way to scale backstab), but I still love playing rogue.

replies.author: Zrazzt
replies.text: once you get used to having rogue hide/sneak, it's really hard to not have it lol

replies.author: Zrazzt
replies.text: I think rogue is good, just hopefully a few things get changed as Razel said (offensive skill caps, BS scaling, poison resist modifiers need to go way up so they actually work on non-trash mobs). I paired sk/shm with my primary ROG and those complement well so far. SK for vampiric embrace/taps/FD/defense, and SHM for buffs and (especially) its huge slow and heal over time.

replies.author: Zrazzt
replies.text: Plus the rogue aesthetic in EQ is unmatched imo!

replies.author: Yakub
replies.text: Rogue is fun. All the downsides of playing rogue in classic are mitigated by having 2 other classes to round out the edges. Backstabbing is very fun, sneaking around is very fun, being able to just lockpick doors feels great lol. They got huge stamina issues in striker stance, which is also where most of your damage comes from. I'm level 42 backstabbing for 1,000 damage and kicking for 400. I'm not sure if they're as "good" as monk or something, but I enjoy playing them to the point where I don't think I'd swap it out of my main combo. If we get assassinate in Kunark it'll be even better.

1533059598951645254.title: Augmentation Spell
1533059598951645254.report: Is the spell Augmentation not actually providing stamina endurance as it states in its description? I see a couple people have posted in the bug report but no response to either.

replies.author: Janus (Tashan - Neriak Server)
replies.text: It always provided Stamina Endurance. In the game early on and in the manual, the developers called it Fatigue. It was used for jump, swimming and it went down if you were hungry and thirsty for a prolonged amount of time. When fighting in melee it went down slowly and if under like 10% Stamina, you would take slight stat losses to Strength and Agility.

replies.author: Janus (Tashan - Neriak Server)
replies.text: In EQL, we have Endurance, which is a new resource for melee abilities, Stances and the like, but they've only modified Jaxxons for Bard and included the Regeneration of Endurance in Chloroplast. I expect to see them add more to include modify Augmentation like they did Jaxxons and with Yaulp and other abilities that have the old Stamina code

replies.author: Janus (Tashan - Neriak Server)
replies.text: Additionally, two spells in the game used to exist to HoT and Heal Stamina called Invigor and Extinguish Fatigue. It would be cool to see them return, possibly for Enchanter since they had the largest number of methodologies to heal and regenerate Stamina; then apply it as a form of Endurance heal with a Cooldown or something

replies.author: Janus (Tashan - Neriak Server)
replies.text: That is one of the problems with Augmentation. The other is that the AC component conflicts with Fury/Rage from Shaman and would hope that gets looked at too

replies.author: Dixa
replies.text: Augmentation isn’t worth the effort unless it haste caps you. It does not currently regen end. It’s supposed to, but it does not and at this point probably never will

replies.author: Kaptn
replies.text: I have the 45% belt, so I am using Augmentation because of its duration and was hoping for an endurance regen.

replies.author: Dixa
replies.text: clerity and swift like the wind both have 20 min duration with spellcasting reinforcement

replies.author: Kaptn
replies.text: Both my Augmentation and clarity spells are lasting over an hour.

replies.author: Janus (Tashan - Neriak Server)
replies.text: And that's the best option if you don't have a Shaman. Augmentation is a late game haste switch where you're working on smaller incremental gains to things like AC, Health/Mana etc. It will get you to cap with a 48%+ haste items due to it doing 27% at 50. Once you hit that Haste level, switch to augmentation for the added 30 agi which helps with avoidance and adds like 5-7AC and then the added 9AC which gets you to 14-16 added AC.

replies.author: Janus (Tashan - Neriak Server)
replies.text: I detailed Shaman as a caveat due to the Rage/Fury line AC component not stacking with Augmentation. Also Augmentation has a longer innate duration than the pure haste lines. Although pure haste with max AA and max spell rank with Enchancement duration focus, you can get it past an hour. Augmentation though can get well past that into the near 2 hour range

replies.author: Tewas
replies.text: Augmentation was great back in the day for the buff duration compared to the shorter higher haste % spells

replies.author: Francisco  (he/him/his)
replies.text: It's great while leveling. Lasts a long time. 5 min haste isn't with the extra 10% or whatever

replies.author: theBruce
replies.text: so if you have shaman it's not worth using (at least until it gets the endurance regen)?

replies.author: Janus (Tashan - Neriak Server)
replies.text: Or it stacks. Both are the consideration

replies.author: Gojetax
replies.text: Was experimenting, yes it doesnt add the Endurance Regen, but it does add a flat 250ish Endurance to your pool....

replies.author: Janus (Tashan - Neriak Server)
replies.text: I'll have to see this when I get home. Does Agility add to endurance?

replies.author: Dixa
replies.text: Dex adds to end not agi

replies.author: Janus (Tashan - Neriak Server)
replies.text: That's what I thought, so his findings are a bit confusing. Unless someone else can test before 4PM EDT, I'll ltake a look

replies.author: Janus (Tashan - Neriak Server)
replies.text: So, I just tested on my naked Ogre. All three stats are below 200 even buffed. Start Endurance = 2154 40 point DEX buff gave 144 Endurance at 3.6 Endurance per Dex 43 point AGI buff gave 160 Endurance at 3.72 Endurance per Dex 27 point AGI buff from Augmentation gave 104 Endurance at 3.85 Endurance per Dex All three buffs stacked took me to 2554 Endurance which is 8 points lower than if you added the top values up which means there's probably a DR variance in there somewhere But it seems both stats improve Endurance

replies.author: Adrastia
replies.text: Hope folks dont mind a few lengthy posts but hey, information. I managed to do the quest line without tanking my factions too hard. In the end finished positive with almost everyone involved, though there'll be a few repair steps. I did all of these to max for the achiement/race unlock progress/etc. Here's where Im at so far, if it helps for factioning. Qeynos 1) Buy some Crow's Special Brew from Crow in North Qeynos. If you've done nothing else you'll need 160, or at worst 320 if your Bloodsabers faction is tanked. Hand them to Gharin in South Qeynos to recieve a huge pile of notes (80 in all, they'll overflow onto your cursor its fine. You can keep them all in hand while you go to turn them in.) Go to the Qeynos Sewers and hand them in to Nomaria Doseniar. Hide/sneak is your friend. This will max your Bloodsabers rep but tank quite a few others. Corrupt Qeynos Guards and Priests of Life will hate this. You'll gain a bunch of Qeynos Guards in the first step but lose a lot in the second. Feel free to destroy the note that Nomaria returns to you. 2) To fix some of those, buy some Silver bars and head to North Karana. Every bar handed to Fixxin Followig (runs along the north wall of the zone) will increase Guards of Qeynos, Karana Residents, Knights of Thunder and Priests of Life by 5. If you were at the absolute bottom for any of these, 800 silver bars will max everything out with no negative faction hits.

replies.author: Adrastia
replies.text: Freeport 1) Kill paladins in north freeport until Dismal Rage is maxed. Increases Dismal Rage, Freeport Militia. Decreases Knights of Truth, Steel Warriors and Priests of Marr. 2) Kill guards in East Freeport until Priests of Marr is maxed out. In particular, kill Lucan D'lere for the soul fire quest item (recommended to grab at least two or three, they can all be quested at once). This raises Priests of Marr and Knights of Truth, but loses Freeport Militia and Coalition of Tradefolk Underground. You'll probably max Priests before Knights of Truth, at which point you can move on. 3) Hand some Tumpy Tonics to Groflah Steadirt in the Seafarer's Roost bar in East Freeport. He spawns against a table opposite the bar, in the same room as Tkyar Renlin for the Soul Fire quest. Good time to do both. If you absolutely bottomed out your factions you'll need to hand at most 572 Tumpy Tonics to him. This will max out Coalition of Tradefolk, Coalition Underground, Knights of Truth and Merchants of Qeynos 4) Off to Erudin. Do the Inert Potion Quest in the Erudin Palace; fill your bags with potions from Toresian Fhabel on the top level and hand them in to Slansin in the Vials of Vitality shop in the lower level. This may take a few trips, but you can max out Carson McCabe, Corrupt Qeynos Guards and the Freeport Militia this way with no negative faction hits. And while we're here..

replies.author: Adrastia
replies.text: Erudin 1) Head to Paineel. You can either kill in the Warrens until you have enough rep (amiable) with the heretics to get a key into the city, or you can simply hop onto the elevator when someone else is using it. Kill every guard in sight. In particular, Atdehim Sqonci in the cleric guild is worth 100 faction a kill. This step will max out your Deepwater Knights, Gate Callers, Craftkeepers and Crimson Hand factions and tank Heretics. 2) Off to the Warrens! Slaughter enough kobolds to max out the Heretics faction again. This will also max out your High Guard of Erudin faction. May want to save any Kobold Hides you acquire. To recap, the steps above will leave you with maxed Bloodsabers, Corrupt Qeynos Guards, Guards of Qeynos, Karana Residents, Knights of Thunder, Priests of Life, Merchants of Qeynos, Dismal Rage, Coalition of Tradefolk, Coalition Underground, Priests of Marr, Knights of Truth, The Freeport Militia, Carson McCabe, Deepwater Knights, Heretics, Gate Callers, Craftkeeper, Crimson Hand, and High Guard of Erudin factions. Everything you need to do your Soul Fire, Firey Avenger and Torrid Corruptor Quests. As of right now I don't have a super easy way to fix Steel Warriors or Circle of Unseen Hands without lowering everything else. Circle can be done by killing Karana Bandits, which will also increase Highpass Guards faction, but they're spread out a bit and kinda annoying to kill. Four Kobold hides will give a good chunk of faction with the Steel Warriors at the cost of the easily fixed Freeport militia and Corrupt Qeynos Guards, but you need to be at least Amiable to turn those in. Will update if I find a good solution.

replies.text: Unfortunately gold is the worst case, since control-click with it on your cursor *puts it back in your inventory*. 1532213098658791584.title: How to fix annoying sounds
1532213098658791584.report:
Locate your soundassets.txt file in the installation directory. Mine is in C:\Users\Public\Daybreak Game Company\Installed Games\EverQuest Legends\soundassets.txt. Start the game, but don't hit play. Open the soundsassets.txt file in a text editor. Use something like Notepad, not a rich text editor like Word. You will have to do this each time you start the game. I created a script to change it.

Change the following lines:

320^Skel_Hit.wav^
321^SkelAtt1.wav^
322^SkelAtt2.wav^
348^WereBAtt.wav^
350^WereBHit.wav^
351^WereWAtt.wav^
353^WereWHit.wav^
355^Wolf_Att.wav^
357^Wolf_Hit.wav^

to

320^Unknown^
321^Unknown^
322^Unknown^
348^Unknown^
350^Unknown^
351^Unknown^
353^Unknown^
355^Unknown^
357^Unknown^

Save the file. Then click play, and log into your server as normal. No more ear blasting sounds. If you lost a sound you like, change them back one at the time until you find the one you are missing.

replies.text: MNK DRU WIZ I'm crushing reds lv 27 to my level 11. replies.author: Tarr
replies.text: Right, i see they just changed it. Okay I just did a bunch of testing. I took off my weapon and the items in my any slots, so attacking unarmed, my bashes hit for 1 damage consistently. I equipped a 12 AC shield with in the secondary slot with no weapons and the bashes were hitting for good numbers. Highest I saw was a 128 crit. Regularly hitting for 35-70. It worked the same in the any slot, I didn't notice a damage difference. I tried the same thing with a low level 1 hander and no other weapons/shields equipped. 10 base dmg, 6 bonus dmg. The damage was a little more volatile, I saw more hits in the 12-17 range, but it would often still hit in the 30-60 range, but normally closer to 40. Highest crit was 110. Same thing with the 2 hander, +6 BABS, 34 base, 12 bonus dmg. The damage seemed a bit better than the one hander, but about the same as the crappy shield. Highest crit was 142. Commonly hit for 40-70. But given the damage difference, I would have expected BABS bashes to hit way harder, so I think either damage is normalized, or it doesn't make a difference what weapon/shield is equipped and the damage difference I noticed was a placebo effect. I should try with some other items with a much greater range of damage/AC, although BABS vs that 1 hander is a huge margin so I dunno what's going on there. Each one of these tests had no other items equipped in the weapon or any slots. I did test with ONLY a piece of high AC armor in an any slot and the damage was still 1 as if unarmed, so it is for sure only taking into account weapon or shield, as the tooltip says. I also saw a disproportionate amount of 40 damage bashes with all weapon options. I didn't parse any of this, but I feel like around 15-20% of all non crit bashes were exactly 40 damage regardless of weapon/shield. Not sure what's going on there.
