replies.author: malkavon
replies.text: This is simply not true. First off, Improved Familiar I gives +9 "casting level", not +6, so 56 wouldn't even make sense. But second, it's the exact same spell effect ID (112) as provided by the Enchanter spell line for Intellectual Advancement and Intellectual Superiority (among many others, but in this era and at this level, those are the spells with that effect). For reference, here is the full list of effects with that spell effect ID: Unless you're claiming that Intellectual Advancement/Superiority functionally improve spell resist rates (which they don't, and as their descriptions state they improve fizzle rates), that effect does not do that. What it does do is give you effective spellcasting skill levels, which *would* have the effect of improving fizzle rates, because fizzle rates are determined by two factors: your spellcasting skill level relative to the level of the spell being cast, and your Int or Wis respectively, depending on which class the spell is from. We know those spells don't improve Wis and Int (there's an entirely different spell line for that for Enchanters), so the other effect that would confer that benefit is increasing effecting skill levels.

Erudite with their really high Int can turn out to have a total Mana + HP on par with Ogre's Mana + HP. The difference being one race is more biased towards Mana than HP. replies.author: Devlyn
replies.text: From natch potes: - Stunned players now receive a short-term immunity from additional stuns that lasts beyond the duration of the current stun. This will prevent chain stunning. However players beware, NPCs also learned the basics of this skill.

replies.author: Gil
replies.text: We dont know how far beyond the duration of the current stun. It could be something as simple as a 3 to 5 second "stun immunity" on a mob after a stun wears off. Players get the same treatment. The exact duration for both is currently unknown but I would expect them to be the same. Whats good for the goose and all that. I cant imagine it being less than 3 seconds or that much more than 5-7 seconds on the high end. Chain stunning is simply gone, for both players and NPCs. Overall a good change, but I hope its not gonna end up eating Enchanter aoe stuns. But chaining Whirl til your Hurl will no longer be a valid strat, and is likely part of the reason players got this nerf too.

replies.text: Does Dex or Str increase archery atk/damage/accuracy?

replies.author: Vaenivo
replies.text: Strength increases Attack. Dexterity increases chance to hit/accuracy - I forget offhand if Dex also has a positive affect on Attack. Regardless, Attack and Dexterity are what directly come into play for Archery damage. You want to increase all three, but the most commonly available - and controllable opportunities - are by raising your Strength and Dexterity. Thankfully, as Rangers, we have some of the best pure Attack buffs. Itemize for both Strength and Dexterity. Build your combos around it, and find as much extra Attack as possible.

replies.author: Desmond (Three-Time Titan)
replies.text: Little weird looking but the pause happens after whatever is on that same line

replies.author: Desmond (Three-Time Titan)
replies.text: Pause times are also tenth of a second, so the 30 in this example is for a 3 second cast

replies.text: Might need to tweak the pause times slightly over the cast time just in case of any lag or anything. You'll have to play with it, but that should work

replies.author: blackfox1225
replies.text: I highly suggest /queuemelody versus /melody. This was way more reliable for me in beta, particularly when starting a melody while on global cooldown. It is also useful to minimize downtime on your songs when interrupted or casting so that you don’t always start at the first song (and therefore reapply DoT1 over and over for example). You should also consider /stopsong instead of /stopcast as if you hit this macro twice, you would stop casting whatever spell you were trying to use. Finally, unless you have Mastery of the Past, you may fizzle the spell, it can be useful to have multiple /pause 5, /cast X lines at early levels to ensure you actually do cast the spell. You call always tweak the pause times.

replies.author: Jon
replies.text: See, I'd disagree and would suggest melody in case you run into a dot that a specific mob resists non stop so you don't get stuck on just that one casting over and over. Different strokes I guess.

replies.author: blackfox1225
replies.text: Queuemelody doesn’t keep singing the same song. It simply starts the rotation where it left off. So if you had already hit 1 2, it starts with 3 4 1 2 3 4 instead of restarting with 1. I also tend to remove things from the melody midfight that have repeated resists and then just hit the macro again to restart with the nee lineup.

1531397011713294547.title: Over all thoughts on the class.
1531397011713294547.report:
First off BL is my favorite call in any MMO. I have been waiting for something like EQL for 20 yrs. The BL feels weak compared to other hybrids in EQL. There is not a reason to add BL to your Trio other than you really like the class. My suggestions.

1. The idea mentioned here around improving the reuse time of Paragon. You need to be able to lower the cool down while in combat with say Cleave or Reave.

2. The lack of useful spells at lower levels and the time frame between spell upgrades is too wide the heals and slows specifically. We should get SL slightly earlier or a weaker version and SL should get a slight buff. Also there needs to a small haste in there somewhere. Maybe some lower tier HoT's or DoT's. 

3. Since the Warder is the primary thing we bring to the table how about adding useful procs to the warder. Like have procs slots or spell buff slots to you can add heal procs or slow procs to the warder. Basically take any spell a BL can cast and have it added to the Warder as a proc. A good reason to make sure you keep your warder alive. Maybe as they level up they get more proc/buff slots.

4. Allow training or acquiring different types of Warder. While I hated the EQ2 BL I did like their Warder system.

1531361493902299156.title: Playing Bard with limited ability to use hotkeys?
1531361493902299156.report:
I have dexterity/mobility issues in my left-hand, which leaves me restricted in how many button presses I can manage. As a result, the idea of Symphony Aura letting me run abilities with no button presses is very appealing, specifically slow, even at a lower percentage always being on is a huge boon.

I am looking at Bard/Cleric/Zerker.
This gives me plate, double attack, dual wield, slow, haste, pacify splitting and great healing.

My hotkeys are going to be Stun, Stun, Heal, Heal and that's about all I can use.
Things that are done out of/before combat are ok to use (things like pacify for example)
But it also means that much of my trio's strengths are being done passively (zerker stance, and S.A. Haste, slow etc)

I guess the question is, am I losing too much of Bard's potential if I don't use the DoTs and charms/mezes?
I really want to play Cleric, so that is a given, and will probably be my primary, which also makes me having 2 priests in a trio somewhat redundant.

My other alternatives are CLR/Monk/Chanter, but again, playing chanter without using Mezes and charms seems wasteful.
Cleric/Monk/Shaman could work, but double priest.... /unsure.

Any thoughts regarding this situation would be appreciated.

replies.author: Jon
replies.text: On top of Symphony, you can run 4-5 dots via a macro using melody as well. I'd say you'll be in a pretty good spot using the bard to it's potential.

replies.author: Ponzicar
replies.text: If you have aoe slow in your symphonic aura lineup you probably won't need to stress too much about crowd control unless it's a huge pull or a high difficulty setting.

replies.text: the higher level charm can be level up as well and can last up to 2 minutes, so its not 'as' demanding as it is on live and nice to have if that's something you ever get around too. Definitely some use of macro to switch stances and cast songs could be useful, but a lot of bard as others have said with SA and /melody can make it very easy to use most of the songs with a single button click. I also mainly just use the mouse and just use keyboard for mainly movement and a few hotkeys like you use.

replies.author: acey
replies.text: Since Bards can do so many things, there’s not any one piece of the kit that’s super critical, you are always balancing opportunity cost. Never doing charm is totally fine, you can get really good DPS from a melody doing single target chants instead of using a similar amount of time maintaining a charm.

replies.author: Hoshimi
replies.text: One of the great things about Bard is that, if you’re willing to put in the effort, it can do an incredible number of things—though that’s true of most classes to some extent. replies.author: Greg The Cleric
replies.text: warrior will be waaaay tankier due to higher AC soft caps, access to better defensive gear, and a flat 5% damage reduction. having said that, if you rock an enc or shm in your monk build, the power of slow spells will probably make up the difference and allow monk to easily tank raid bosses

replies.author: paladoc
replies.text: The Warrior's answer to Mend is Warrior's Endurance AA, at base regening 1% max hp every 6 seconds. While that doesnt sound like much at first glance, its actually extremely good when considering all the factors that go in to it. -Warrior has the highest ac softcap and beyond with their gear. -massive hp pool (you're regening hp based on that huge hp pool) -scales with unyielding Invocation. You will have much better returns over time with Warrior's regen. Compare: At level 50 warrior, with +3/4 planar gear a war will have roughly 7k hp. Thats 140hp/sec in unyielding baseline, not including the extra from natural regen, other AAs, spells, rubicite bp, etc. Its not uncommon for this number to easily push past 200/tick. Alternatively, a monk will push around ~5200ish hp max, with much lower regen. Mend will heal 30% of their (or more on an exceptional through their AA) every 1.5mins. A warrior can do the same, at the very base passively in unyielding, but its for much greater amounts of hp. Paired with a class that can HoT, a warrior will easily regen 5-8% hp every 6 seconds. The tankiness and sustain is unparalleled, especially when factoring in taking much less damage per hit. A monk, will provide a Kick and a Strike, and solid primary weapons, higher haste, and better DPS. Warriors are going to provide basic kick, slam/bash, Cleave, and now Rampage, so they wont be slouches in the dps department. Monks definitely have a better utility in the form of FD, higher attack values for more consistent hits and max hits, better chances to block and dodge (but no parry). It also comes with Evasive Stance which is pretty amazing for leveling and certain situations in end game. Im biased. While ill miss FD and slightly better DPS, I prefer not having to worry about my hp bar as much. For a tank minded player, who still wants to put out some damage, warrior is the way to go. If youre looking for FD skips, slightly better dps, control over your heal, go with Monk.

replies.author: Essay
replies.text: Almost everything you wanted to know about Spirit of the Puma TLDR: Puma, with 350 dex, procs on average of 16 times per minute regardless of dual wield, weapon speed, 2hander, haste, or delay reduction. Spirit of the Puma — Proc Testing Field Report *Melee proc testing, Aug 12, 2026 — Ranger/Warrior + Shaman combo, DW capped 210, ~350 DEX (Warrior subbed for Zerker on zerker-stance tests)* Key Findings Does weapon speed matter for average procs/min? — No. Procs/min held flat ~14–16 across swing rates from 47/min all the way to 298/min. Does dual wield or 2H matter for average procs/min? — No. 15.1/min (dual wield) vs 14.7/min (2-hander), despite DW attempting way more swings. Can the offhand proc Puma on its own, with no mainhand equipped? — Yes, but lower: 56 procs / 5.6 per min with the mainhand fully silent — well below every other test. Can attacks other than swings (kick/bash/cleave) proc Puma? — No. 0 procs across 414 attempts with both weapon slots empty. Can Puma proc on a miss? — Yes. In the 2H test, all 40 clean proc+miss seconds show the same order every time: proc line first, miss right below it, same second. Does haste matter for average procs/min? — No. +40% haste pushed swings/min up 28% (two separate runs), procs/min stayed in the same band both times. Does lowering delay via zerker stance matter for average procs/min? — No. Zerker nearly doubled the swing rate (99→178/min), procs/min barely moved (15.1→15.0). (more raw data when slowmode lets me post)

replies.text: Full Puma Test Cases — every swing count includes misses, hits, and crits. These were all 10 minute tests on a level 60 dummy. 1531253082728566954.title: Plans to upgrade buffs/debuffs with motes?

replies.author: Shinra Kuonji (Twice Punished)
replies.text: Correct. Buff and debuff potency does not scale with upgrades, so you're just in it for duration and Mana cost. One notable point: Blessing of the Paige (and its upgrades) have below average durations and oppressively high mana costs. Upgrades can help alleviate this.

replies.author: Rekoj
replies.text: If I recall I was upgrading Echo line for faster cast/lower mana, Celestial line for lower mana/cast time/duration, and stuff like Paige line for lower mana/duration. This is outside of the obvious PR.

replies.author: Rekoj
replies.text: The only buff i'd spend on is the Paige line. I wasn't swimming in motes enough to go all the way down to buffs in the totem pole of things to upgrade. Leveling up, key spells you'd mote them to IV and thats usually the sweet spot. Your final versions of spells were the ones you'd overload with motes and it becomes hard depending on your trio to get them all maxed out, so again, you're going after the most impactful ones. 90% of buffs in game dont fall into that category until you're swimming in fully upgraded key spells per class to then trickle down into buffs to even see if it mattered

replies.author: Shinra Kuonji (Twice Punished)
replies.text: Heal over time effects double dip from motes because both the potency and duration increase. With Echo heal specifically, you get an extra tick of duration with a pretty small upgrade due to fairly generous rounding, but it takes a good long while to get the second bonus tick.

1531241001061060668.title: Highlighting a Bow Improvement and Making it a thread...
1531241001061060668.report:
I am copying a post I made in the strikethrough thread and bringing it to its own thread to have a streamlined talk on the Bow Improvement thing...

The problem with Beserkers and Beastlords is they were not part of the OG EQ and were designed for 50+ play in mind. So when you cut them off at 50, some of their smoother progression tools are not there. The class AA's are the same way. Those were AA's that would not come online until much later in leveling. Strikethrough seems to be an AA that, as originaly designed, allowed Rangers to catch up to other classes at 55+ cause they were falling behind. In this iteration it is WAY more powerful given the fact you will always be hitting the mobs face ( most of the time) so the parry, blocks and ripostes are so much more impactful to bypass. The bow focus would be and can be a thing later when things like Veeshans Peak happen etc, where it will be more likely your running a party of 3-8 to get in and really have a good time and folks can specialize their builds and not cover 3 or the 4 bases. The best approach I can think of to boost Ranger defining Bow use would be to allow the first couple of shots on a boss or mob, to do things like Slow, pillage/cancel enchantments . Some AA like Imbue Arrow, you can assign a spell or effect to your next shot. Make it like a pet bar ( and instead of the commands like taunt, follow etc they are one of several effects you can assign...Slow,Pillage enchant, Resist debuff etc) Now scale these to be weaker versions so they arent just gods, but on par with other hybrids and give it a CD in the mid teens in seconds but influenced by Zerker stance and now you have something that can be class defining?

replies.author: Jokon
replies.text: Let's discuss! I'm gonna start by breaking your thoughts into distinct points: * Strikethrough is a pretty amazing ability that works with melee and archery. It is definitely stronger in solo relative to multiplayer as you can get a lot of strikethrough's benefits by being behind a mob. * Your point is well taken that archery right now is pretty basic. A lot of the utility you're describing is stuff you can get from other classes; this is a big part of how EQL works. I don't think giving rangers all the tools is good because at that point you don't have good identity (IE, what is UNIQUE that rangers bring?). As an example, shaman have the best slow, so if I need slow then I can run RNG/SHM/???. Swapping loadouts is going to be part of the journey - not every fight, of course, but also as a great way to refresh how the game is played over time. * Forcing a proc through an AA would be a way to expand on what Spellblade currently provides, as your Imbue Arrow AA suggests. * A lot of current ranger complaints revolve around that we don't have The Button (tm) like Reave, Smite, Cleave, Frenzy, Backstab, Eagle Claw, Dragon Kick, etc. What we do have is 30% strikethrough and +130 odd attackpower from AA, which means that the current ranger identity is *reliable* damage.

This is what I found if original poster is interested: Main-Hand Rate: The baseline formula generally approximates (DEX / 170) + 0.5 procs per minute in continuous combat. Off-Hand Rate: Off-hand weapon procs scale similarly but operate at roughly half the rate of the main hand dependent on your dual-wield proficiency. Dexterity Impact: Higher Dexterity directly increases your modifier linearly up to server caps, while over-cap Heroic Dexterity from late-expansion gear and augments further optimizes the frequency. Normalization: Because it targets PPM rather than a flat per-swing percentage, weapon delay does not inherently break or multiply your overall output per minute.

replies.author: GameKnight
replies.text: Combat Skill & Ranger Procs Where Berserker Stance drastically changes your proc economy is through ability acceleration and extra attack mechanics. Halved Cooldowns: Berserker Stance cuts combat skill recharge rates in half. If you are utilizing class combinations with hard-hitting combat abilities (like Monks, Rogues, or Knights), you can fire off twice as many skills per minute. Frenzy and Extra Swings: The stance grants or supercharges abilities like Frenzy, which forces instant double or triple attacks every few seconds. Class Specific Synergies: For multi-class combos like a Ranger/Berserker, community testing shows that Ranger-specific spell and ability procs do scale heavily with Berserker Stance. The rapid skill spamming and massive influx of sudden extra swings create significantly more opportunities to force procs outside the basic auto-attack PPM calculations.

1531057373832024074.title: Wizard Spell Leveling
1531057373832024074.report: Anyone who played beta have a list or any advice on which spells it's worth investing motes into as you level? Since reincarnation is a thing now, it feels like it's really, really worth it to invest in leveling spells just so you speed up each subsequent leveling burst.

replies.author: Rathwirt
replies.text: Any nuke you upgrade is going to be resisted less, cost less mana, do more damage, cast faster, and recover faster. Not really any bad choices for Wizard.

replies.author: Meanwhile
replies.text: If you look at the wizard spell list, you'll see a few places where there's a big gap before you replace your best nuke. That's the spell you want to pour motes into.

replies.author: Tanasinn
replies.text: Garrison's is a good first one to actually level up, I think

replies.author: Aren
replies.text: It's not always obvious that you won't be replacing a spell for a while as it's not linear, unfortunately. The first spell that's worth taking high is your level 18 DD, Garrison's Mighty Mana Shock. It has a base damage of 333, and you will want to upgrade it to at least +5 as you can keep using it for a while. The next spell is Inferno Shock that does base 600 DMG (in reality it starts off less from what I remember -- around 540?), but by that point you should have Mana Shock at +5 or +6, which will be doing similar damage (~465). Even upgraded, Mana Shock will be more mana efficient due to it being a lower spell (and your spells start hitting for more damage as you level up). You finally upgrade it at level 34 when you get a similarly mana efficient Ice Shock, which you will want to use in SolB. Lightning Shock you get at 37 is another good one, but Ice Shock is a little more efficient. Either one of those is an upgrade to your Mighty Mana Shock though. Conflagration you get at 43 does a base of 900 damage for 250 base mana, which was the final spell I was using. The frost version of it is not learned from your spell vendor (you get it from Vox I think?). Those are the DD spells I was using.

replies.author: Aren
replies.text: You also want to upgrade rain type spells, as those will be your most mana efficient sources of damage. 32: Lava Storm. 41: Frost Storm.

GMMS is quite good but it isn't *critically* important to get it much past +3. Inferno shock at +2 is going to do a lot more than GMMS at +6. replies.author: Cal
replies.text: Gotcha. So your SA is the last 5 slots that just create a fire and forget Aura with buffs that pulse for your whole group/self/pet. Melody works with the Single Target abilities (mainly the Red Icon Songs) Snare+Dot, Slow+Dot, DD, etc type songs. You make a macro that plays them in order from your Spell bar. /melody 4 5 6 7 Melody locks out all other skills while its being played so you need to have an Auto Atacker class to do damage with (Monk, Zerker, War +) You get the point. Those auto attackers can still use SKILLS like Kick, Taunt, Bash etc while Melody is playing. If you are playing Cleric and need to toss a HEAL out, then you have to make a /stop casting Macro in order to do that. THEN you have to reactivate Melody.

replies.author: Reis
replies.text: SA lets you passively play upto 5 songs which are non-targeted aoe. These songs do not get interrupted and are essentially on all the time. They will still "tick" as normal for things like runes and regen. These songs are still on your spell bar. Melody allows you to autocast (note they still actually need to cast) as many songs as you would like in a order you specify. in EQL you cannot melody a song which would be applicable to SA while active, even if not one of your 5 SA songs. With the correct aa's and song lvls you can easily melody 5+ songs at once on top of the up to 5 from SA. Because of the SA restriction your melody is mostly used for single target dots (you will get 5 by 50 in EQL) and a few other specific songs. queue Melody is the same as above accept any song which is currently "on" will get skipped in your order in favor of ones that are not. This has benefits and challenges sometimes particulier with resisted songs and npcs with high resists. ("on" would be on you or the target") Bard will require heavy investment into your spell gems if you want to take advantage of everything. Depending on your comp that can be prohibitive. Melody is not required to utilize most of what bard has to offer. Comps with limited combat casting (like war / clr / brd) can fully take advantage of using 10 spell slots for bard. YMMV here.

The other stupid myth was that it had to be in a specific inventory slot, it does not nor has it ever. The game simply checks for a WR quiver in inventory (in any base slot, such that it can act as a container) and then grabs the WR% to calculate with. It doesn't matter if you have multiple, it takes the highest WR% the same way you can wear 2 haste items and it will only use the best to calculate with. replies.text: Generally speaking, the best stats currently for pets are AC and Strength. As for weapons, once you get the max tier mage pets, they seem to have a base ratio of 21 / 30. Currently pets DO use weapon delays (unsure if this is intended or a bug). So you do not want to give your pets weapons that have worse ratios than that. This means you wouldn't want to use a 2 hander that has a ratio worse than 1.4, or a 1 hander worse than .7. This means for the most part, the only weapons really worth using are very heavily upgraded items, most of which will come from raid. As for haste, the pet is haste capped by any pet haste spell. Haste items are currently pointless.

replies.author: serrasin
replies.text: Archery with endless quiver and the ability to keep out of melee range is essentially free infinite damage, the various bonuses just increase the rate of application. i know, duh, just wanting to underscore that archery has an inherent and distinctive advantage if you are able to take advantage. Face tanking your target is obviously a solution granted by ranged stance, as is having a pet or party member tank for you. If you have sufficient run speed then you can circle kite the target, or root & shoot, or reduce its speed to zero (such as a snared mob fleeing due to low health), or fearing it. Those are some very surface level tactics, but there are still others. For example, using constant stuns and whirls. As things stand now most bosses are resistant if not immune to most CC effects, so pet tanking is the most efficient solution since ranged stance eats up endurance like tequila shots in a singles mixer. If I were to make a suggestion to the devs for mechanical changes prior to seeing parses to gauge the real world difference between archery and other dps strategies, then it would be to fold the mechanics of the ranged stance into Mastery of the Scout - spreading them out across the ranks. This is less about pure power and more about removing a obstacle from allowing archery to synergize with other classes and abilities.

replies.author: nirafelos
replies.text: I think there's some hyperbole on one side and some dismissiveness on the other that are equally unwarranted. Yes, WAR, MNK, RNG, ROG can all bring triple-attack and the same or better skill caps than we can across the board. That said, the variance in skill caps is....not large in any of these cases. Yes, they also all have relevant melee passives that stack with stances. So do we. We get 6% crit and 7% flurry chance. (the flurry chance fully overlaps overlaps with WAR, but the crit chance synergizes with their 30% critDmg passive). All of them other than rangers get at least one melee attack skill, and all of them are better than frenzy currently is. Devs have already stated that frenzy needed work. We have no data yet on how the Rampage changes will perform. MNK, ROG, RNG all bring significantly more utility to the table with FD, Sneak/Lockpick, Spells, than we can with a 20s cd endurance hog of a snare or microstun. Our endgame weapon itemization is rivaled only by PAL/MNK dw. So saying that we bring _nothing_ outside of our stance is objectively untrue. We lack enough hard data to provably assert that another melee class would perform better (outside our stance), so all that's left is the utility and how it feels, both of which are highly subjective. Phrasing complaints as if they are backed by numbers when they're actually about something subjective is a very easy way to get that feedback dismissed by developers who look at the data they have and see that it does not match. Talk instead about how it feels, because that on its own remains highly valuable feedback.

1530764944591814787.report: WIth the EQL system of permanent gear for Pets, what have you found are some key concepts to use for equipping them?

replies.author: Cyanide Bunnyslayer
replies.text: Since all necro pets below 50 are WAR/SK, you will want to focus on gear in this way: - AC and HP if your pet is going to tank. HP Regen is helpful too - STR for increasing chance of maximum damage - DEX for increased weapon and buff proc chance - AGI for increases dodge chance - Mana and Mana Regen (mana Regen doesn't exist in classic EQ, so this is for future expansion) - Haste to increase auto attack attack speed The pet won't benefit from STA, WIS, INT, or CHA A LOT of research is going into pet weapons, but generally you want to dual wield weapons with procs, and you want to seek out weapons with at least 25 base damage AND a delay of 30 or lower (ratio of 5/6 or better) which are rare in classic eq.

replies.text: remember that tier II focus effects are fully effective up to level 44 spells, so Frost Storm/Conflag are at full power with just the focus from Rokyl's mask. Likewise, don't ignore Mana Pres and Spell Haste. The faster and cheaper your nukes are, the quicker the target will die. replies.author: Kashari/Ariketh
replies.text: Re: Faction: Faction is a value between -2000 and +2000. Everyone starts at 0 unless you’ve done something to change your faction. (Killing mobs, doing quests, etc.) Your race, class, and deity provide modifiers determined by the faction you are dealing with. The way NPCs con is based on the value +/- the listed modifiers. Note, when it comes to class, the faction calc always uses your best class modifier. So if you change from human to ogre, you will now use the ogre modifiers. Example. Let’s say you start as a human paladin/rogue/enchanter of Mithaniel Marr. When you interact with the Knights of Truth faction your modifiers are human (0), paladin (25), Mithaniel Marr (100). Final modifier is 125. Assuming you’ve done no faction work, you’ll be at +125, which puts you at Amiable. If you swap to Ogre, your human modifier changes to the ogre -750. The total is -625, which puts you at the middle of threatening. If you plan on race changing from human to ogre, I recommend doing the paladin related quests as a human. Reap the benefits of FA once you’re done. Especially since the ogre modifier may very well lock you out of steps because there’s faction thresholds and the racial modifier can’t be overcome.

replies.author: Kashari/Ariketh
replies.text: As a side note, the rogue modifier for the Knights of Truth is -100. Enchanter is 0. Which is why paladin is the best mod in the example.

replies.author: Kashari/Ariketh
replies.text: The faction spells give you a boost to your faction as another modifier. When you cast the spell, it affects the target and every other NPC of the same faction in the current zone. The spells can’t be used on (most) vendors or guildmasters. Going back to the Knights of Truth example, your best option would be to tag the paladin guards roaming around North Freeport rather than the Knights of Truth guildmasters. The spells only affect the NPC’s primary faction. Not the associated factions they may be related to. So what’s a valid target and how do you know which faction they’re on? You google it. And sometimes play guessing games with the results. Take Tynkale, one of the High Elf paladin guildmasters. If you could kill him, he drops your cleric of Tunare and King Tearis Thex faction. It’s fairly obvious that his primary faction is clerics since he’s one of the clerics and not the King. If you cast the spell on a mob with the primary of King Tearis Thex, Tynkale would be unaffected. But if you found a non vendor non GM cleric of Tunare NPC, Tynkale would be affected as would every cleric of Tunare primary in the zone. (Which is all the guards, I believe.) The highest enchanter faction spell gives a 300 pt boost. Bard song can technically go north of 600, based on instrument and skill and blah blah, but its effect is capped at 300. You could mitigate some of the ogre penalty with enchanter/bard, but you’re still suffering a -350 pt modifier. And now that I’ve looked at the point scale… +1100 is the bottom of ally. I was wrong, it looks like you can overcome the ogre penalty entirely with work on the Knights of Truth faction. (This may not be applicable to all factions.) Side note: when you use the sneak or feign death tricks, you set your faction to 0 with no modifiers.

1530320798466965504.title: How to value DW vs 2H ratios?
1530320798466965504.report:
I’m curious if anybody has a good rule of thumb when judging the ratios of two 1hd weapons vs 1 2hd?

For instance, while leveling I had the Najena fist weapon and the mace from befallen, when upgraded to somewhere around +4/+5 they were somewhere in the .4-.5ish range. Then I also got the TornEar Thumper that upgraded to +5 was somewhere in the .7ish range.

Is there a rule that makes the decision easy, or is it more feeling things out?

Thanks!

replies.author: najitaka
replies.text: All of my testing was under level 20 where I assume the damage cap was keeping two .167 1h weapons the same as a .333 2h.

replies.author: past_tense_of_dig
replies.text: I believe a decent rule of thumb is that, at level 50, monk will dual-wield like 75% of combat rounds due to its class-leading dual wield skill cap. So you should do like 1x your main hand ratio plus 0.75x your offhand ratio. If that's better than your 2her, you should dual-wield. Note that at lower levels that 0.75x will be a lot less, so it may make sense at lower levels to 2H, depending on the comparative ratios

replies.author: past_tense_of_dig
replies.text: So if you have, say, 2 1h'ers with ratio 0.25 each, then at level 50 that would be equivalent to a 1.0 x 0.25 + 0.75 * 0.25 = ~0.44 ratio. So if your 2her is better than that, go with that.

1530317203105386608.title: Druid Recommended AAs?
1530317203105386608.report: What Druid specific AA's should be prioritized, especially early on? Which AA's increase the healing and effectiveness of their new bloom heals?

replies.author: Vaenivo
replies.text: The AA descriptions are fairly intuitive. There is a line that boosts the immediate direct heals, another for the heal over time, mana efficiency, nuke boosting, dot boosting, crit chance, etc. I ran Bard/Ranger/Druid during beta, focused more of the Bard AAs due to the relative power it offers, but as I reached endgame I was investing more on the Druid side and it was impactful. I'm unsure which you should prioritize early on - that will depend on your combo needs - but there's a breadth of options that are worth it even if you choose a balanced approach by slowly investing a little into everything. With that said, I think the AAs for healing and general mana efficiency are probably what I would choose earlier on.

replies.author: Amerzel
replies.text: Did you find yourself using both direct healing and the bloom heals frequently?

replies.author: Vaenivo
replies.text: Definitely used both. HoT as an early engage tactic, but during fights I kept it up. Would use the direct heals when I dropped down towards 30%.

1530302396310491166.title: Pet pulls aggro, no matter what I cast.
1530302396310491166.report:
Ideally, I want to play Paladin, Beast and Druid as they are all classes I like.
Played this (or rather *Tried* to play this) more than once in the beta, but kept giving up.

Even at a fairly low level, I pull with Cease, follow it up with Desist yet as soon as the mob gets close, it looks straight at the warder and stays focussed on him for 80% of the fight, even on casting stuns 3 and 4, it barely pulls aggro back to me. Pet taunt is OFF, and pet not buffed with anything external.

Am very confused why this is happening, as I played the same combo with both Magician and Necro, who have arguably stronger pets, and Mage has burnout too, and those pets would only pull aggro once or twice out of a 2 hour session. So why is BST warder such a aggro magnet?

Doesn't seem to matter if I pull with stuns, a DoT or Slow. Pet just keeps pulling aggro off me, to the point it makes me swap to something else.

Suggestions or someone else's experience in similar combo's would be appreciated.

replies.author: Cyanide Bunnyslayer
replies.text: The Spirit procs for the pet generate enormous amounts of hate, even more than the mage or necro pets can generate. Check the tooltips for those spells. One of them has a non-hate generating version. It's ok if your beastlord pulls aggro most of the time, it's more than capable of taking a hit. Another thing to check is whether or not you are closer to the mob than your pet. Aggro AI is wonky, and mobs will sometimes turn to pets over players *even if* players have more aggro. You might consider pulling mobs with a different spell than Cease. The Beastlord Slow line is probably a better spell to pull with, as it generates *enormous* amounts of aggro

replies.author: [FOE] Viltor
replies.text: the proc dd / threat for pets is psychotic aggro. tested it with a bst/mag/nec combo and no matter what pet i threw it on, would always get aggro

replies.author: Deleted User
replies.text: As has been said. The sole culprit is the pet proc buff. It procs a lot hate. At later expansions BST got a lot to choose from in terms of pet buffs (even jolt like buffs that lower agro) so there is hope part of that finds its way into EQL.

replies.author: Saberine
replies.text: Each pet proc is +50 hate+damage with a slightly stun component (I think they had that?) which is another +100 agro (I could be wrong about that number but this is just to give an idea of the threat it generates) so a single pet proc is about 200-300 threat, that's 3 of your stun casts mind you.

Lifetap
Heal
Dispel

replies.author: ManiiNames (5k2k Club)
replies.text: Have to think about this from memory. Using SHM-NEC-PAL. - Lifetap - Envenomed Bolt - Odium - Ignite Blood - Cessation of Life, because My Lord Innoruuk hates mobs which heal! - Slugs - Slow - Malo - Lull. Swap for another DoT when raiding. - Puma - Cease and Desist - FD, because am not a Monk like - Harmshield. This is a fun one. For EXP I will sometimes carry it, but for Raids I almost always carry it. Mine lasted for 18s, and against a. Boss you could: Layer Dots, Slug, Canni V, Recovery Invocation, Harmshield. You would get three full ticks of the dots doing damage, the HoT healing you, and free mana from Recovery. It was actually quite excellent, and made some super-tough fights much more manageable. Even though I had Divine Aura as well I judged carrying them both to be overkill in most circumstances. If you do carry Harmshield, you will need to also have it listed on your other spellsets so that it never leaves your bar. Otherwise you get to wait the 10m for it to reset.

replies.author: ManiiNames (5k2k Club)
replies.text: One takeaway I have from your list is you’re spending a slot on regen (Chloro?) and haste. Both of those should have ~15m duration with the AAs, focus item, and maybe upgrade to +4 or so. I would move those to a separate spellset, mine is called Short Term Buffs. That would free up two spell gems for other things. If you were really serious about it you could write a macro along the lines of: - /pause X, /memspellset myCoolBuffs - /pause X, Cast Haste - Cast Chloro - /memspellset myCombatLoadout I did not have a macro like that which I used regularly, because I grouped just enough that I had other targets I wanted to cast the spells on. So I would just use /memspellset MyCoolShortTermBuffs and then manually cast the spells. Was also handy for buffing the pet if it needed haste or whatever. I tend to run six spellsets minimum, for each loadout. Name them appropriately so you can tell which loadout they belong to. Combat, Perma Buffs, Buffs, Short Term, Pet, Raid

replies.author: Gudbeast/Gudknight
replies.text: Ya I compiled the info using this stupid feature but where it comes from is listed:How AC Works in EverQuest Legends In EverQuest Legends, Armor Class (AC) is a composite stat that determines how much damage you can take from melee attacks. It’s made up of two components: 1. Mitigation – This is your base resistance to physical damage, determined by your Stamina (STA) and gear. Higher STA increases your mitigation, reducing incoming damage before it’s even applied YouTube YouTube . 2. Evasion – This is your ability to avoid melee hits entirely. It’s based on your Agility (AGI) and gear, and is used in the hit roll to decide whether an attack lands eqltools.com eqltools.com . How AC Affects Combat When you swing at a target, the game resolves four key numbers: Your Accuracy (vs. target’s evasion) – determines if the swing lands. Your Offense (vs. target’s mitigation) – determines how much damage lands if it hits. Target’s Accuracy (vs. your evasion) – determines if their swing lands. Target’s Offense (vs. your mitigation) – determines how much damage they deal if they hit eqltools.com eqltools.com . AC is the sum of Mitigation + Evasion on your stat sheet. A higher AC means: More damage absorbed (mitigation) before it hits your HP. More chances to avoid hits (evasion) before they land.

So what equipment in this version of the game should we be chasing? Obviously planar/dragon stuff is going to be most of the endgame equipment, so I'd like to also get some low to mid level options. Thanks to the two Any slots and being able to extract instrument focus, there's actually a reason to care about them as loot now as we can have all four instrument types at once without giving up our weapons. Also bards are often the fifth class on otherwise enc/wiz/nec/mag exclusive items, so I'm wondering if there's anything useful from that angle.

Things I've found so far:
 Just a good ratio sword from Runnyeye
 Better than storebought stringed instrument from Mistmoore
 seems like a good proc to steal for a better ratio weapon, SolB

replies.author: Reis
replies.text: You will never want to willingly equip an instrument right now. All instruments should have the focus pulled and put into your normal equipment. bards do not benefit from other spell foci, you will always want to have your instrument focus on at all times. This does present a problem though because each of the 4 instrument mods are a primary/secondary only focus. This locks you into duel wield or shield, and weapons/shields for the any slots. It would also prevent you from getting any other primary/secondary focus for your other classes due to them being in use. You can swap these based on the usecase but its old pretty quick. I would recommend droping wind to allow you some flexibility( for ExE 3 for example or 2handing) . In most cases you only really need percussion and stringed. Brass does have its uses but it is more niche. I think more testing is needed on the impact of keeping a slot for wind when charming for breaks since you can lvl the spell now and have overchannel invocation.

replies.author: Callius

replies.author: Callius
replies.text: LOY is 15 min reset, every time you smite it reduces it by 1 minute, berzerker stance means your melee skills reset twice as fast, thus you get double the smite hits, likely look LOY every 3 minutes or so Berzerker stance will eat endurance though, need shaman or ranger end regen buff Personally i only enable smite auto skill when LOY is down , due toi the also 3% mana drain per smite

replies.author: Kärrigaste verkstaden
replies.text: Smite also work with double and tripple attack which also lowers the cd faster because every proc reduces cd by a minute

replies.author: Kärrigaste verkstaden
replies.text: And from what i have read dual wielding also makes smite proc with both weapons (might be a bug) and then lowers it even faster

replies.author: Deleted User
replies.text: Smite is not a proc. It's a combat skill based on a timer that will autofire (when enabled) each time the timer is up. It is not linked to dual wielding. It can double and even triple attack if you have that skill. It will drain 3% of your total mana when it lands but will convert that mana into damage. So the larger your mana pool is, the more damage it does.

replies.author: Deleted User
replies.text: I had great success on my PAL+BER+X trio but tbh the quick recovery of LoH was unneeded and mostly went to waste because there never was a need to spam LoH for me. If your +X is an AoE capable class you could just pull more mobs of course so you have an actual need to LoH more often.

replies.author: Sir Potato The Nohope
replies.text: would like adding monk make it go faster with duelwild ?

replies.author: DirtyPotions
replies.text: Like frozen said. Its not a proc. It's an ability that goes off when the CD is up if you have it on auto cast. and if you have double attack or triple attack it can do that. zerker makes it faster cause smite CD comes off faster.

replies.author: Deleted User
replies.text: In terms of being able to double and triple attack, here's proof from my combat log hitting a level 50 test dummy in arena: [Mon Jul 20 17:56:08 2026] You smite Test Fifty for 56 points of damage. (Critical) [Mon Jul 20 17:56:08 2026] You hit Test Fifty for 284 points of magic damage by Smiting Strike. [Mon Jul 20 17:56:08 2026] You smite Test Fifty for 17 points of damage. [Mon Jul 20 17:56:08 2026] You hit Test Fifty for 284 points of magic damage by Smiting Strike. [Mon Jul 20 17:57:25 2026] You smite Test Fifty for 7 points of damage. [Mon Jul 20 17:57:25 2026] You hit Test Fifty for 284 points of magic damage by Smiting Strike. [Mon Jul 20 17:57:25 2026] You smite Test Fifty for 24 points of damage. [Mon Jul 20 17:57:25 2026] You hit Test Fifty for 284 points of magic damage by Smiting Strike. [Mon Jul 20 17:57:25 2026] You smite Test Fifty for 37 points of damage. (Critical) [Mon Jul 20 17:57:25 2026] You hit Test Fifty for 284 points of magic damage by Smiting Strike. It shows the actual smite hit is fairly low but but the damage added (3% of total mana converted to magic damage) is where the numbers get bigger. It also shows the extra magic damage does not crit, just the small physical smite hit does. ( 284 / 3 ) * 100 = over 9000. I surely didn't have 9k mana so it's not 1 damage per 1 mana, more likely about 3 damage per 1 mana.

----------------- old feedback post ---------------

This spell line given to wizards is obviously foremost for NPCs to cast at players, and that is extremely disappointing.

The first, and major issue of why this spell should not function the way it currently does, groups are COMPLETELY intolerant of you casting it. I dislike the spell, but for the sake of giving it a fair shake I played with it. Seven, yes seven, grinding groups/raid groups either told me stop casting the spell or I would be removed, or just went straight for the kick. That is how annoying they found to play with somebody casting this spell.
How can you justify a spell remaining the way it currently is if is that much of a nuisance to other players?

Second, which is also important, it feels awful to actually cast yourself. If you are in a zone that inhibits levitate you lose large amounts of damage output because of how much your character is pushed around, even if you are lucky enough to press your character against a wall. If you do have levitate you are still pushed around, and if you lose cast time if you push your recovery time up.

And third, with all spells now gaining a potential -150 resists, it's "theme" of being a low resist spell is greatly diminished. Since it's on a wizard, it is now entirely in the realm of "I'm too lazy to change my Rend, Ice Comet, Conflagration spell slot" as these three spells were basically made equivalent and you re just choosing your resist type.

replies.author: Gudbeast/Gudknight

So when you cut them off at 50, some of their smoother progression tools are not there. The class AA's are the same way. Those were AA's that would not come online until much later in leveling. Strikethrough seems to be an AA that, as originaly designed, allowed Rangers to catch up to other classes at 55+ cause they were falling behind. In this iteration it is WAY more powerful given the fact you will always be hitting the mobs face ( most of the time) so the parry, blocks and ripostes are so much more impactful to bypass. The bow focus would be and can be a thing later when things like Veeshans Peak happen etc, where it will be more likely your running a party of 3-8 to get in and really have a good time and folks can specialize their builds and not cover 3 or the 4 bases. The best approach I can think of to boost Ranger defining Bow use would be to allow the first couple of shots on a boss or mob, to do things like Slow, pillage/cancel enchantments . Some AA like Imbue Arrow, you can assign a spell or effect to your next shot. Make it like a pet bar ( and instead of the commands like taunt, follow etc they are one of several effects you can assign...Slow,Pillage enchant, Resist debuff etc) Now scale these to be weaker versions so they arent just gods, but on par with other hybrids and give it a CD in the mid teens in seconds but influenced by Zerker stance and now you have something that can be class defining?

replies.author: Buckley
replies.text: I don't think anyone is looking for that perfect solution right now. They're looking for a minor adjustment that allows it to be functional in the way that other forms of combat work. None of the proposed adjustments have been extreme, or time consuming. Some number adjustments, itemization, and it'd be fine (for now). Often what happens when people have a big job with a lot of tasks is that they see a problem that they can't immediately correct completely the way they would like is to table it and put a pin in it. They do this for a couple of reasons obviously time is a major one. But another reason is because they know they'll have to revisit it later regardless if it is dealt with now. This doesn't sit well with some people as they feel like they're doing twice the job. once to put a bandaid on it and again later to flesh out the more grand solution that they have in their mind. The problem is, the can gets kicked down the road, other adjustments happen that take priority, and by the time you get to it you now have to take into account those new adjustments. I.e. They find rangers struggle in some other fashion, bump up their melee and spellcasting to get them more in line to keep them going. Then by the time you want to work on that fix for their ranged options, you have to consider all of those fixes you did before that have shifted their power balance as a whole. Which means you have less wiggle room to play with the new system. It paints yourself into a corner. Gudbeast, the argument that this isn't how it was in classic, doesn't hold up here. The devs have stated many times that this isn't EQ1. And it is overwhelmingly clear by the great many changes they've made that it doesn't hold true for nearly every other class.

replies.author: Buckley
replies.text: In fact, they have gone to some effort already to add new itemization, a stance, endless quiver built right in, and incorporate AAs that suggest to players that they intend for it to work better than it did at classic.

replies.author: Kethigar
replies.text: The attraction of HW is that you can stay in recovery (or any other inversion) and cast w/o clipping swings or getting interrupted. here are some stats comparing rank V HW/sup: HW 489 hp, 135 mana, 3.62 hpm, cast time 0.6s, 5s reuse. raw hps is 815, but you can only cast every 5s, so overall max healing is actually 97.8 hps (489/5) factoring in recovery inversion it increases the hpm to 3.81 with the 5% discount - but recovery ALSO doubles your mana regen, so if (for example) you're casting say, 1 heal per 6 seconds and your base mana regen is 50, the true hpm of HW ends up being 6.25. It gets even better the higher your sheet mana regen gets. Let's say if instead of recovery you do divine with just the single divine class. raw hps will increase to (489 + 135)/0.6 = 1040, and factoring in recast max 'true' hps spamming on CD is 124.8. and it gets better with a 2nd or 3rd wis class (133.71 and 142.62, respectively) Sup heal: 690 hp, 167 mana, 4.13 hpm, cast time 2.8s in inversion, cast time 0.93, cost changes to 134 mana 17 end, so the hpm increases to 5.15hpm. raw hps is cast + recovery (2.8s cast + 1.3s recovery - inversion just moves cast time to recovery so the hps doesn't change in inversion) so 168.29 hps.

replies.author: Kethigar
replies.text: so if you're spam healing with a rank V spell, superior healing is about 72% more hps over HW, but while you're spamming sup heal you aren't able to cast anything else, whereas with HW you can cast other spells between recasts. but once you also factor in that sup healing basically forces you into inversion lest you risk losing melee dps, HW even bridges the gap because you can choose between more hpm (recovery) or hps (divine). at rank IX, HW goes up to 15 casts/min and ends up at 135 raw hps, but that goes up to 165.75 hps in divine (x1) invo. Rank IX sup heal (spammed) goes up to 221.5 hps

1529952873432092805.title: Shadowknight Benefits
1529952873432092805.report:
I see a ton of comments in the discord deriding SK (especially compared to paladin) and I wanted to start a linkable thread discussing many of the useful benefits and utility SHD can bring to your trio.

1. Tankiness - This is the obvious one, and overlaps with paladin of course. Plate, shields, high AC cap, defensive skills (parry riposte), defensive & mage hunter stance.
2. Lifetaps - They may be worse self healing than just about every other class, but there are a number of ways to improve them enough to sustain your self healing alongside your natural tankiness, such as class AAs from dru/wiz or spell crit AAs. Notably you also get proc-based ones for passive dps and self-healing.
3. Arcane mastery - SK counts as an "int" class for your caster builds, offering a significant benefit to anyone using that invocation.
4. Invis & invis vs undead - Great utility for sneaking around anywhere, unless there are mixed live & dead mobs.
5. FD - The classic pulling / get out of jail tool.
6. Various stat taps/buffs/debuffs - Steal strength, atk, AC from mobs, and/or buff your own.
7. Threat - SK is famously excellent at maintaining agro in group settings.
8. High ratio weapons - just like paladin, SK gets access to many high ratio weapons.
9. Heal debuffs - very underrated, SKs get the necro line of dots that reduce mob healing taken by up to 30% - only 5% less than necro. A great tool for dealing with mobs that heal.
10. Pet
11. Snare - the classic snare dot line, mostly not necessary in EQL because mobs only run at D0.
12. Fear - also mostly not used in EQL as it's especially poor CC in dungeons.
13. Calm - only up to level 30 and undead, so limited in usage overall.
14. Invulnerability - I'm not sure what the best use of this is for, but including it for completeness.

Harm touch is now upgradeable to leech life, and a dot has been added, making it way more useful!

1529912533014679562.title: Dot Stacking. Shm/Dru or Shm/Nec
1529912533014679562.report:
Curious to what everyone thinks is the best to combo Shm with in-wise of DoT stacking? 

At level 50. What is the Dot Stack with Shm/Dru?

At level 50. What is the DoT stack with Shm/Nec?
Does Bond of Death stack with Sluggs?
Does anything not stack other than Ebolts?

Which Combo do you think would do more dmg?

replies.author: ManiiNames (5k2k Club)
replies.text: In Open Beta i did SHM-NEC-PAL. You get the Shaman and Nec DoT AAs plus the generics and they all stack. DoT wise if you're really serious about it you can cast eight of them on a big boss. Best dmg DoTs were Odium (VIII), Envenomed Bolt (VIII) but the others are good. NEC has a flame dot which is great against things which are resistant to one of your other lines. I ran Slugs to VIII and it was fantastic. With the AAs affecting beneficial spell duration + focus effect it lasted for 54s and healed ~250 a tick. I would normally cast it with Empower and pick up another +15% since I had two non-hybrid casters in my loadout. You can pre-cast it before fights too. Puma adds huge DPS to your pet. At VIII with the AAs and focus I think my Puma lasted for 3:30 or so and proc'd for 200ish. If you stand around in Empower, your procs will benefit from Empower, so when you're just meleeing and waiting for DoTs to expire I would milk some extra damage from the proc. My overall DPS against D4 stuff was ~280-320. I had decent stuff but no sky gear, and my planar/dragon gear was ~+3-5. Pet added about 60-70 with SHM buffs, haste, and Puma. My own DPS was 80% DoTs, 6% white damage and the rest was misc. Cannibalize is wonderful, heal back up with Slugs.

replies.author: picks631
replies.text: Anecdotally since I haven't tried myself, I've heard others say Shm/Nec is better early on since you're relying on Nec taps to heal. Once you have the gear/AA/spell upgrades to make Shaman healing not terrible, replacing it with Dru is probably more dot/spell damage

replies.author: picks631

1529906032367632526.title: AC, Shields, and the any slot
1529906032367632526.report:
I recall conversations from the distant past that mentioned the AC from shields was computed in a manner unlike that of armor and other items.
If that's still the case, does it require the shield to be equipped in the secondary slot, or can it be in the any slot.
And if the calculation for shield AC is viable from the any slot, then what effect, if any, does it have on the calculation if one were to equip shields in both of the any slots ?

replies.author: Murak
replies.text: My understanding is the "bonus" is only received in the secondary slot.

replies.author: Cyanide Bunnyslayer
replies.text: Shields in the Any slot count towards the AC softcap. You need to use it in specifically offhand to have it bypass the AC softcap.

replies.author: Classified
replies.text: My AC soft cap only went up when i used a shield in my Secondary slot. It di dmake a difference on Inny D3/4.

replies.author: Shangfei
replies.text: Given that a shield is no longer required for Bash, is there any reason a Warrior, or other tank class would equip a shield in the secondary? I'm not certain what the ac is on the endgame shields, but I will hazard a guess of something like +30 Ac for the primo end game shield? But even at that, would something like +30 ac be enough to warrant a restriction on weapon choice during a "difficult" encounter?

replies.author: Shangfei
replies.text: I guess what I'm asking is, are there any other benefits to the shield other than AC over the softcap?

replies.author: Classified
replies.text: Once they put in the DW Bash AA, no.

replies.author: Doinker
replies.text: Not as far as I'm aware, no. But the benefit from bypassing the softcap cannot be understated. I cannot test values at the current moment obviously but I encourage you to try it for yourself. It seriously made the difference of being able to solo D4 or not on my war/clr/brd for most raids. Editing to clarify that you have to think bigger picture here too. Equipping a shield in my secondary then opened up an Any slot where I threw in the highest AC stat stick possible. The loss in DPS from going from 2h to 1h was tiny compared to the massive boost in defenses.

replies.author: Zansobar
replies.text: Well remember the soft cap is just a soft cap, warriors get 35% of any ac that exceeds the soft cap to count towards their overall AC. But then again you could get 50 AC from a fully upgraded shield in your secondary that would count outside the soft cap, which would take about 142 total AC to get the same net effect in other slots.

replies.author: Softcap
replies.text: Let's say your soft cap is 400/450. If you add a 50ac shield to your secondary then it will become 450/500. Now if you put your shield in Any Slot, then it will be 450/450 and every piece of AC you add after that you will only receive around a 3rd of your AC due to diminishing returns. Keeping your soft cap as high as possible will minimize you only getting partial AC to what the actual items ac really displays.

replies.author: Dastion
replies.text: I have a few ideas: ## Create Thrall Converts the targeted enemy into a Thrall whose level is based on your ranks in this skill. Level begins at -X compared to your level, improved by additional ranks in this AA. The Thrall retains its classes and appearance but not its abilities or statistics. Thralls will use a set of standard skills and stats appropriate to their level and classes. This skill takes 10s to cast and cannot be cast while in combat or on enemies who have players on their hate list. Rares and special enemies are immune to this effect. Thralls are lost when you leave the zone or die. -# Design note: This is really just a thematic standardized pet with the potential to be any class combination an enemy is, with the thematics of looking exactly like the enemy. If you want to rank it up like you would a normal pet it's going to take an AA investment to make it worthwhile. ## Doppelganger Craft an illusion around yourself that mimics the target's appearance and provides a boost to any faction they are associated with. The faction boost and cooldown improve with each rank in this AA. -# Design note: Thematically this lets the Enchanter act like the traditional "Doppelganger", you copy the target's appearance and read their mind in order to mimic them. Mechanically this is represented by a boost to any faction associated with them, which is just an extension of a role Enchanters already play. ## False Memory Adds a chance per rank that mesmerized or charmed targets will suffer a memblur effect when the spell ends. -# Design note: Mesmerize already has a similar low chance to do this, this just adds an additional chance so when mez or charm break unexpectedly you aren't the target they go after. ## Drain Delusions When you cast an Enchanter mesmerize or stun spell you have a chance to siphon mana from your current enemy target. Each member of your party restores a portion of this amount. Proc chance, amount drained, and restored increases with rank. -# Design note: Thematically you're siphoning away the thoughts of enemies while they sit there looking at the pretty colors . Really though I wanted to give enchanters more incentive to lean into their original role as the masters of CC, especially if AoE mez ever gets nerfed. ## Decoy Target grouped player or pet gains your appearance and a % of your threat generated for X seconds. While near you and above 50% health they intercept 30% of your damage taken. -# Design note: Effectively a defensive spell for mesmers, thought about making it longer duration to allow you to, in effect, share your illusions. ## Illusion: Life Casts a powerful illusion over a recently deceased ally that temporarily allows them to ignore death. The target returns to battle for X seconds with a portion of their health and mana. When the effect ends the illusion is broken, and the target dies. Duration and returned health/mana increase with ranks. -# Design note: A temporary battle rez. The Enchanter doesn't restore life, they just convince you that you have it. Do what you gotta do before gravity reasserts itself. Definitely didn't steal this idea from GW2 mesmers ## Illusion: Life Casts a powerful illusion over a recently deceased ally that temporarily allows them to ignore death. The target returns to battle for X seconds with a portion of their health and mana. When the effect ends the illusion is broken, and the target dies unless they have been resurrected during the duration. Duration and returned health/mana increase with ranks. -# Design note: A temporary battle rez with a catch. ## Rude Awakening Causes mesmerized targets to lash out in confusion upon waking at an enemy who is not mesmerized. Damage increases with higher level spells and based on how long they were mezzed(Longer mez deals more) -# Design note: Gives high level mezz a DD effect. Level variable prevents AoE mez becoming an effective AoE dmg spell and duration variable prevents spamming mez break for damage.

1529897772361453568.title: Force of Nature sucks
1529897772361453568.report:
It doesn't stack with nature's precision or wolf form and gives barely more ATK than nature's precision alone. Either increase the ATK it gives so its worth using alone or make it stack.

Side note: the regen doesn't stack with chloroplast either.

replies.author: Jim Jimmerson Esq.
replies.text: Your points have nothing to do with what I'm bringing up

replies.author: ManiiNames (5k2k Club)
replies.text: Jokon and I also had a feature request on the stacking. It doesn't stack w Garou either. Devs are considering if that would be just too much ATK and promised to get back to us when they have time.

replies.author: Jokon
replies.text: It can stack with Illusion Benefit: Dena (Great Wolf Form) if you cast it in the right order. What you have to do is order your buffs like so: cast Nature's Precision, Cast Form of the Great Wolf, Cast Force of Nature. If you do this correctly, Force of Nature will overwrite Nature's Precision but NOT Illusion Benefit: Dena. If you do it incorrectly, FoN will fail to land altogether (or be overwritten).

replies.author: serrasin
replies.text: FON is an incredibly powerful and broad buff that just doesnt stack with certain other buffs in what would be obviously overpowered ways.

replies.author: Nasaan
replies.text: Unless I'm missing something, Force of Nature is a direct upgrade over Nature's precision? So there's no reason why it should stack? However, wolf form is atk slot 3, while FoN is atk slot 1, so by standard eq spell rules, they should stack. Garou is atk slot 3, and should stack with FoN, but not any of the wolf forms. So unless this server is just doing some weird stuff with their spells, there is an issue here.

replies.author: serrasin
replies.text: its probably an intentional balance choice since ranger already has so much attack rating.

replies.author: ManiiNames (5k2k Club)
replies.text: I forget the exact ATK I was hitting, it's a big number though. The free AA adds a ton, then all the ranger buffs, then stat buffs and gear.

1529851167587307562.title: Backstab damage MUST upgrade to make rogue viable in the lvl 50 game
1529851167587307562.report:
Backstab is a significant part of a rogue's damage, but it atrophies after you stop leveling. It never increases, so the class brings less damage to a build as you push into the lvl 50 game (gear and AA). 

A lvl 45 rogue with a +0 yael dagger does the same backstab damage as a lvl 50 rogue with max AA and a +10 yael dagger. This is a problem.

Let backstab damage increase at even half the rate of weapon damage. So every even upgrade (+2, +4, +6 ect) it increases. Otherwise rogues fall behind other melee in what they bring

Maybe at +3/6/9. I would really love to see the Sky Rog primary only weapon get some love also. It should be BS 13 (like Yeal Tooth) and add secondary. I ran as a War/Clr/Rog

replies.text: I agree... though for some reason they think throwing more procs of minimal effect at us that occur rarely is the way to compensate for the nerf on backstab. replies.text: true, backstab is screwed by stances. Because the skill reduction to endurance is a flat amount. So many smaller hits benefits hugely from it, while a single big hit doesn't really benefit.

1529817273215488071.title: Getting This Party Started - DW vs 2H in EQL So Far

replies.text: Getting This Party Started - DW vs 2H in EQL So Far

replies.text: 2H for warriors scales Cleave better, from my personal experience.

replies.author: pry
replies.text: 2h with striker stance and improved bash was significantly better than dw-offensive while leveling. At 50 with sky weapons dual wield offensive and 2h offensive both became competitive, but my testing still slightly favored 2h striker stance. Though it was close enough that it probably doesn't matter that much. Depending on your other classes though dual wield may be better at 50 with raid gear. The warrior options just aren't that great. On later playthroughs though striker stance won't be as good because your base auto damage will be so much higher than it was during your first run.

replies.text: Use whatever weapon is best at the time you have access to it as you're leveling up. Once you're 50 and farming Sky, you have access to Dagas. At +5 it's a 0.762 ratio. If your trio has CLR, then that's your offhand and you use Theurgist's Star primary. At +5 it's 0.88 ratio. If you have MNK in your trio, you use Wu's Fist of Mastery. At +6, it's 1.136 ratio.

replies.author: Classified
replies.text: Looking back at my logs, on July 15th I killed CT D4. The fight was 673 seconds with him having 76k HPs. I think I had a Thornbringer +4 (Rog Sky) with Frost strick proc (Phinny) and Serpent tooth +5 (Ykesha proc) but I might be wrong as Piercing was ~31% of my dmg with no other type. DS, Clr ward, backstabs, procs, kicks/cleave was the rest. Anybody have a 2HS to compair?

replies.text: I used DW because it was better for dps and I could easily outheal all the dmg I was taking as war/clr/enc. I can definitely see an argument of going 2h if you feel you need the survivability, but with the right gear and the current procs available, DW just going to be better for pure dps output.

replies.author: pry
replies.text: I did extensive parsing on 2h versus dw while both leveling and at 50. Striker stance 2h was *significantly* better during the leveling process because of scaling cleave damage and improved bash while leveling. (It was really having bash more than anything else, lol) At 50, it wasn't until I got plane of sky weapons that dual wield became a viable option. But comparing sky 1h weapons to sky 2 weapons, offensive stance Fangol and offensive stance Garduk/Dagas were both fine at that point. Striker stance Fangol was still a little higher average dps though, but they were close enough you could do whatever. The striker stance Fangol had much variance too, so if you were looking for consistency it would be with the 2h or dw offensive setups. And then subsequent leveling playthroughs offensive stance 2h was slightly better than offensive stance dw. The raid weapons were just better than buffing up striker stance kick/bash. This will all probably changes though as I've heard improved bash is set to work with dual wield.

replies.author: pry
replies.text: With War as your only melee 2h was better than DW for a couple reaons. 1. There's a better warrior 2h option in Fangol than there are 1h weapons for Warrior. 2. You could bash with a 2h but you could not dual wielding. 3. Cleave scales with weapon damage making 2h better for those hits. If you have something like Monk, Paladin, etc in your build then dual wield might already be better at 50 just because of how much better the 1h options are with those classes. If you're looking at Warrior alone though the weapon options do favor 2h. Improved Bash is also supposedly being changed to work with dual wield. I'm not sure if this makes dual wield better right out of the gate, but it'll be worth looking into! I think it's also important to point out that from the time you got a 2h weapon and improved bash AA your optimal stance was Striker as it boosted Cleave, Bash, and Kick. At 50 once I picked up Fangol offensive stance ended up pretty competitive. Striker had more variance but the average result was still a bit higher. On later playthroughs though you always went offensive stance while leveling. The auto attack damage was way higher than buffing cleave/bash/kick while re-leveling with a Fangol lol. Dual wield mostly used offensive for the best results. I'm not sure if getting access to bash will make Striker better. Maybe? Maybe while leveling but then offensive still at 50? We'll have to test and see. This is just my experience looking at my logs and parses way too long both while leveling and at 50 running War/Nec/Sham. I think if I were to run War as a solo melee again starting out the safe play would be to rush getting a 2h + improved bash and leveling that way. Then at 50 when you have AAs to spare you can look to pick up ambidex and give dual wield a go. Thanks for coming to my ted talk.

replies.author: cerotoneN
replies.text: I'm running War/Shm/Nec and was curious about Fangol +10 vs Garduk +10 and Dagas +10. I asked our buddy chat gpt to run some numbers, and here's what I got. Could be AI slop but I had it taking its time coming up with an answer and was referencing eqltools.com, eqlwiki.com, and eqlegendstools.com. I had it assume a level 50 Warrior with all relevant melee AA's: > Weapon +10 damage/delay, Ratio > Fangol, 58/35, 1.657 > Garduk, 46/40, 1.150 > Dagas, 22/21, 1.048 > > The dual wield chance break-even point with Garduk and Dagas against Fangol is: 48.4% > So Dagas needs to swing successfully only 48.4% of the time for the dual-wield setup to pass Fangol in raw weapon ratio. > The available level-50 Warrior estimate places the pre-AA dual-wield chance around 54.74%, although the wiki explicitly labels the underlying formula conjectural. EQL’s exact combat constants remain unpublished. > > There are two plausible readings of the Ambidexterity AA: > > Multiplicative: 54.74%×1.32, 72.26% > Additive: 54.74%+32%, 86.74% > > Either interpretation comfortably exceeds the 48.4% break-even point. > > Results: > DW chance and Lead over Fangol > 54.74%, no AA, +4.0% > 72.26%, multiplicative AA, +15.1% > 86.74%, additive AA, +24.2% > > Thus, before damage bonuses and activated attacks, Garduk/Dagas is plausibly 15–24% ahead. Of course, Garduk is an outlier, the ratio on that weapon is insane.

replies.author: cerotoneN
replies.text: It goes on to factor damage bonuses: > As a sensitivity check, suppose Garduk has an 8-point bonus and Fangol has a larger 12–15-point bonus. Dual wield then breaks even at approximately 55–59% offhand success. > > That is still well below either reasonable Ambidexterity estimate (additive or multiplicative): > > At 72.26%, dual wield remains roughly 7–10% ahead. > At 86.74%, dual wield remains roughly 15–18% ahead.

replies.author: cerotoneN
replies.text: > Fangol still wins on attacks that are specifically primary-slot based: > > A Fangol primary hit uses 58 weapon damage versus Garduk’s 46—about 26% more per ability hit. > Rampage performs a primary-slot combat round. > Burst of Power’s flurries occur after a primary-slot triple attack. > Riposte-related attacks generally favor the stronger primary weapon. > > Therefore: > > Ordinary autoattack and Cleave: strongly favor dual wield. > Rampage, primary flurries and ripostes: favor Fangol. > Overall sustained melee: still favors dual wield.

replies.author: cerotoneN
replies.text: > Garduk +10 / Dagas +10 is the clear sustained-DPS winner on paper with Ambidexterity. > > My estimated advantage is: > > About 15–24% in raw weapon-ratio output > Probably around 8–18% after accounting for Fangol’s larger primary damage bonus > Somewhat less after including Fangol’s damage proc and primary-only combat attacks > > Fangol remains useful for: > > Rampage and primary-flurry burst > Riposte-heavy situations > Encounters where its poison proc performs especially well > Enemies with dangerous damage shields > Situations where fewer, heavier attacks are desirable Here's the ChatGPT answer if anyone wants to dive into it. It first was mistaken on +10 ratio increase (thought it was +50% instead of +100%) and had some wrong values for Ambidexterity, but once I had it start referencing eqltools.com it started making sense to me:

replies.author: blackfox1225
replies.text: Not to negate anyone's experience, but I actually had a lot of success with Largo's and Selo's Cessation on my Clr/Brd/Mnk combo as the only slows. I got a lot out of it and was able to successfully solo AND duo (which is actually harder) through D4 on both dragons, both gods, and Yael of course. However, Plane of Sky was very temperamental as I had to essentially be in overchannel the whole time and used evasive very often (particularly in non-solo instances). So much of the damage there comes from mobs proc'ing unresistable spell damage when they land hits that not having mage hunter/defensive or a top teir slow was challenging. I only fought there for the last 2-3 days of the pre-order beta and never bothered going above D0 since it does not actually make a difference with regards to most of the loot as they are largely quest drops.

replies.author: blackfox1225
replies.text: All of that said, I did not have time to build up Jam Fest, which would have made a considerable difference on the level 60+ mobs that you encounter in Sky. As a reminder, the Orb of Tishan is incredible and can easily be placed into various bard usable weapons.

replies.author: Korshay
replies.text: The Orb of Tishan proc rate is not reliable. I ran it offhand in the POB and was always disappointed how long it took. Ranking up spells for reduced saves will be way more reliable. Grab eight friends and head to OW D4 Hate to farm motes.

replies.text: On CT D4 as BRD/WAR/NEC i was able to stay in defensive for most of the fight, I briefly had to swap to balance to regen a bit of endurance but not for very long with bard song regen. He did hit harder in balance though! CT is an a-beater.

replies.author: Darkvenger

replies.author: Gudbeast/Gudknight
replies.text: Throttling Evasive stance? Promised renewal spam? lil bit of both

replies.author: Hoshimi
replies.text: I want to know too. It seems like once you have the gear (and AAs), it’s possible to kill D4 bosses even in Offensive Stance. But it feels like you need Defensive Stance to get the gear required to reach that point.

replies.author: blackfox1225
replies.text: Gud is right, I was playing cleric too. I would start the fight in evasive until slowed, then switch to balanced and keep myself healed between PR and Sacred Echo, using Mend for a scary round. Once I got to 80% mana, I’d swap to evasive while regenning mana. At around 40% endurance, I’d swap again to balanced and gain it back. When I had worse gear, I would even throw a shield in off hand when I wasn’t in evasive for the extra mitigation while I gained back mana and endurance, then I’d go back to DW once I moved to evasive again. For high D3-D4 and pretty much everything in sky, I did find I needed to use overchannel to keep slow and dots on, which sucked because it capped my mana regen around 30ish versus the 60 I could get in recovery. Balanced stance with cantata and jig had me at 52/104 I believe which was great.

replies.author: blackfox1225
replies.text: I wanted to add here that for so much of what you want to kill (aside from EoV in Sky) you very often have an excellent charmable pet nearby. So much of my damage when I was first killing Nagafen and Vox D0-D4 at 42-46 (i.e. before planar gear) was just making sure I could live long enough to keep the giant alive for most of the fight. Solo instances are quite a lot easier than multiplayer instances and open world fights though. Sky multiplayer is very tough solo without defensive/mage hunter. Sister of the Spire doesn't do her 1000 dmg stun in solo instances and Essence of Veeshan and the Efreetis have far fewer hitpoints. When I did those alongside my wife (enc/sk/ber), I had her tank in mage hunter to mitigate the DDs and even out the damage spikes.
