I leveled ranger shaman necro to 50 and cleared a bunch of stuff with pretty crap gear. It felt good. Never saw the sky bow though. I’m thinking it could be possible to dump necro for monk. I’d loose a pretty nice pet but the shaman pet can still puma. Also the level 48 lich is very good mana. Lifetap was nice but once you get the shaman heals buffed you don’t really need it. I think though I’m wasting a bunch of attack and ranger stuff by not choosing another melee. 

If I choose monk I can lean into the higher blunt weapons further. There is a bit of overlap with block. Warrior has pretty much the same issue as block but would add a bit of defensive that I don’t need quite yet but may. Berserker I’m not sold on and rogue utility might overlap a bit much with shaman. 

I think farming d4 hate the ranger shaman necro wins if only for charm. 

Another thought is paladin for the triple wisdom pool. Block doesn’t overlap and paladin weapons are pretty strong. 

I guess the question is, “what have you guys done to extract the most from ranger”

Have not had the chance to try out the ENC pet, thus, have a question for those who did (well, some questions, actually):

- Is there a way to control the pet like a MAG pet (via AA, maybe?) or is it purely reactive like in classic EQ?

- a druid pet buff would apply to the ENC pet, correct?

replies.author: Gunthak
replies.text: I found that pet control for me was not even something I thought about. It will stop attacking anything you mez. So your pet will naturally hit the target you are on as long as you are utilizing the core identity of the enchanter class. The summon pet is also a pal and is a good healer while you are leveling.

replies.author: Gunthak
replies.text: I did not utilize the charm mechanic because of how convenient the passive healing was from the summoned pet.

replies.author: NcjE | Myth
replies.text: thanks!

replies.author: Shines
replies.text: The pet did have the default controls as per the mag pet out of the box. Experience with charm seems to be all over the place- some people adore it, some people hate it. A d4 three-class mob will, by my understanding, become a d0 three-class mob. It maintains it's class abilities but loses the difficulty modifier of the zone. There's also no dire charm, so maybe you hit your pet with mako and tashani, and while your odds are better, there's no promise that it won't break twice in three minutes. For me those things combined to make charming just not worth it but other people swear by it.

replies.author: Shines
replies.text: Also, pet specific buffs apply to your pet. You can have nec pets with magician burnout, necro pets with bst proc buffs, etc Do note that last I checked, statistic buffs like shm buffs for sta increased the number, but the pet got no benefit like extra hp

replies.author: NcjE | Myth
replies.text: The pets seem to have their individual caps, so the buff lines do not all stack up. Thanks for the answer - the main issue I had was the control set; the calss combo of the ENC pet and its general viability and the combined HP pool with the druid pet (even if that one is rather less than top notch) as well as the (strongest in game) druid pet buff should make ENC/DRU viable and not laggig too much behind MAG/SHA or NEC/SHA

replies.text: Just to clear a few misconceptions I saw in this thread: - Pets can equip anything that matches their own classes OR yours. I was able to equip the MNK/BST Flaming Fist H2H items. Whether or not they have skill values for weapons their classes can’t normally use is something I hadn’t considered until just now. - The WAR/PAL Animation pet has standard combat abilities (kick, bash, cleave, etc) for those classes. It will also sometimes use the Warrior’s /shield Discipline on you (maybe others?). However, it does not use Smite - but resummoning it does reset its LoH cooldown. - It will LoH itself (and only itself) but does so at such a high HP% that it wastes most of it. I’m guessing this is a hold over from enemy AI so that Paladin enemies have that thematic without resetting the whole fight. (Before anyone argues, I did specifically try to force a situation where the pet would LoH me and it didn’t. I also logged my combats from the first week and searched them) - As to spells, it will cast Paladin Courage and Symbol buffs on itself. If you upgrade it enough it will cast the Paladin haste buff on itself too but I think even Augmentation beats that. It will offensively root and stun and cast heals on you sometimes. The healing isn’t bad when you max upgrade the summon at 50.

Rogue poisons (and all spell-based procs to my knowledge) apply to both hands, so dual wielding gives these an effective 50% proc rate buff over not doing so. With the current DEX cap being 500, although probably impossible to reach in Classic, it would place the current PPM cap for a proc that effects both weapons at ~5.16 (again, assuming no formula change has happened). I had fun as a BST/DRU/ROG but just want to know what are the drawbacks

replies.author: Cyanide Bunnyslayer
replies.text: At the end of beta, the reasons to put BST on your build over Shaman were: 1. Access to dual wield 2. Access to Evasive stance 3. Access to better armor than Cloth 4. A few specific unique spells that are BST exclusive. 5. The pet. The issues: 1. No access to Double Attack, so this would mainly benefit knights and if you didn't have another class in the trio that could do that 2. Again only a benefit if you don't already have it 3. This mainly only helps primarily INT builds like WIZ+ENC 4. DEPENDING on the specific trio you might have a hard time dropping them into your spellbar 5. Making the pet BST/WAR did nothing to help it's DPS. It actually hindered it. 6. Shaman DOT DPS was INCREDIBLY strong at the end of beta. Probably to the point that Shaman outclassed a lot of other classes altogether, including BST.

replies.author: Jokon
replies.text: Yeah, Beastlords have an issue with their baseline damage capabilities. A lot of their abilities are end-loaded, meaning you don't have a lot of your kit finalized until you're at high level. This makes the leveling journey a bit of a struggle. What BST does to a kit though is give you pet utility. Hobble is great for agro, especially if you stack it with the Spirit procs. You also have the best direct pet heal. Unfortunately, your pet is incomplete unless you pair it with another pet class like Magician or Necromancer. One thing we didn't really get to see due to how late it came in the beta was the effects of gear on pets. How much better does a pet get if you can add three more pieces of gear? Two? One? It's also worth noting that the new spell mote system allows you to upgrade the pet level, and as a BST class pet it can use some *nice* weapons. This doesn't help the low/leveling game for BST, unfortunately.

replies.author: Dastion
replies.text: As others have said, Beastlord’s hybrid nature doesn’t translate well into EQL because of multiclassing, you can see a similar issue with Druids and funnily enough the class that tends to edge out both is Shaman. They are supposed to be Monk/Shaman hybrid pet class but their only Monk qualities are H2H skill, Evasive Stance, and maybe Block. They don’t even get sneak, safe fall, and need an AA for a worse version of FD. And a good portion of their spells are probably outclassed by another class in your trio. That said, they do still have a niche. They shine best as a gap filler in a Knight + Caster trio, so long as that caster isn’t Shaman. Their best builds are probably Knight/BST/MAG. Up until a few hours ago I would have said Paladin because SK self-sustain and HT don’t compare to Paladins but they just announced that HT is gaining a DoT component and they have two new AAs. An auto granted lifetap damage bonus and “Leech Touch” that makes the initial DMG and DOT components of HT lifetap. So with that knowledge I think the extra pet slot and lifetap proc abilities might synergize better with Beastlord than before - especially if they ever get Bloodlust.

I got into the habit of waiting to use it until I’m at 70% health before I spent points in the AA then I waited till 45% to hit it. No number countdown timer on it, doesn’t need one imo, just wait for the hotkey to go fully grey again. No hotkeys get number timers on them, just filled with red and slowly goes down. You can set a macro line to your other hotkeys that you make if you want to add the red cooldown on it by adding “/timer 600” (for 10m).

replies.author: DorfUnderlord
replies.text: Mend could use a cooldown modifier like loh with smite.

replies.author: Mogwai
replies.text: IMO the "random chance to double Mend" AA feels kinda bad and seems like janky game design. random % mechanics make more sense for passives like Slay Undead, Crit, etc.

replies.author: Mogwai
replies.text: Getting that AA forces you to wait until lower health to use it and disappoints you 70% of the time. Changing it to a +10/20/30% flat increase to Mend heal would be effectively the same increase in power without the annoying randomness attached.

replies.author: Defenestrating
replies.text: While we're at it, let's change our crit chances to just flat damage increases. Flatten mob damage across the board and we can live in a generic, boring hellscape that doesn't resemble the game we're here to play.

replies.author: Halfwise
replies.text: I get the criticism, but while people like to "Win big" from RNG and find the concept fun.. they tend to dislike "Losing big" due to RNG. Different vibe / concept, and the variability between heals and damage. People love to roll that 20 and get the big boom, they hate rolling the 1 and dying because of it. Having it go both ways is *fair* and reasonable, but fair isn't always fun. Still, if it was all or nothing, I'd rather have the highs and lows.

replies.author: Defenestrating
replies.text: Mend is already busted. I feel like topping off your health constantly and playing the way you're referring to is a behavior issue moreso than a problem with the game design. If you understand statistics, you won't be counting on crit to mend. It'll just be a nice surprise when it does and you factor your decisions and lineup accordingly.

replies.author: Defenestrating
replies.text: If we're talkin about feelings and vibes, I love it when I use my canni AA, and then crit my mend. Getting a full 50% is great. Losing 20% under your suggested scenario kinda sucks. Most loadouts have sources of healing other than mend, so adjust the way you're healing vs. adding additional burden to the devs. EQ is in a lot of ways similar to tabletop RPG's and crits are a large part of the charm and fun.

replies.author: Defenestrating
replies.text: So if you're "losing" by not critting 70% of the time as intended, that's a very correctable mindset issue.

replies.author: Mogwai
replies.text: you ok bro?

replies.author: Defenestrating
replies.text: Livin' the dream. You?

replies.author: Mogwai
replies.text: I don't have time to write up when RNG/chance-based mechanics make sense from a game design standpoint and when they're poorly implemented (e.g., Dodge % being removed from LoL as a gameplay mechanic). It's a non-passive implementation that serves only to make the skill *less reliable*, if not less powerful. I think you look at whether that's the goal and if that actually feels good. I don't care if they nerf Mend healing or adjust the values of it.

replies.author: Mogwai
replies.text: e.g., if you ran an all-melee class trio and you needed that AA to fire off exactly 50% of the time to do a D4 boss, you might get unlucky rolls 8 times in a row. Or you might get it on the first try. If that's what we're going for, cool. I'm not against randomness if that's the intention.

replies.author: Defenestrating
replies.text: You should look at the live AA progression. They've stated something like 7 proposed expansion. Needing to leave space for growth is reasonable. If you're running an all melee trio and you want to change a fundamental design piece of a class to fit your niche situation so you can farm the highest level content, again-- that's a you thing.

replies.author: Defenestrating
replies.text: There are plenty of situations where I fire off mend before it drops past 75%. Catering towards getting the absolute maximum benefit is something I understand from some folks-- I played at the highest level and did some crazy stuff with my monk. But from this iteration of everquest, it's kind of a silly ask. Just my opinion. I don't work here.

1529740783937126460.title: Druid viability in a trio
1529740783937126460.report:
Has anyone found that having a druid as part of your trio of classes was a solid choice?

What Pros/Cons have you found with Druid in EQL beyond "getting the ports" from the class?

replies.author: 👻🏳️‍🌈Spooky🦇Bird🏳️‍🌈🎃
replies.text: Dru has one of the strongest pet buffs in the game, and has a pretty good array of dots (magic / frost / fire dmg.). You get root, a mob calm, and a charm for beasts. You also get a very strong HoT spell with a burst heal at the end. I imagine they pair well w mag because of mag's malo and strong pets.

replies.author: 👻🏳️‍🌈Spooky🦇Bird🏳️‍🌈🎃
replies.text: They actually pair somewhat poorly with the anti-undead classes due to the lack of high level beasts in zones good for farming undead, but that HoT does *wonders* for uptime, and has an *amazing* mana to healing ratio.

replies.author: Qendal
replies.text: I like the big resist mod on their line of magic DoTs. Especially once upgraded, you hardly ever have to worry about those getting resisted.

replies.author: Graham
replies.text: In beta I tried Bard/Rog/Dru figuring I would go to 25 for the ports and then change to Shaman. But I really liked Druid. HoT was better than I expected. Just need to time it right. Biggest issue I faced was the lack of spell gems. Bards can take up to 9. So, what to pick from Dru list for other 5?

replies.author: Shaithis
replies.text: The druids rain ae and pbae spells are pretty good too, nothing to sneeze at. My spell bar with brd/rng/dru was in order dru direct heal (for spellblade testing), dru dot, rng flaming arrow, dru rain ae, dru ds, dru bloom, brd charm, then my 5 symphonic songs.

replies.author: Jokon
replies.text: I leveled with druid in my first loadout during beta. The healing is great, anchored by the Bloom heals and Healing Water, the fast casting heal. They perfectly supplemented melee builds. I also found the druid buffs best-in-game for group attack power - share great wolf form is the best one in game unless Game Jawn brings the ranger attack power buffs down from the Kunark era. Their DoTs are fine, definitely not the best, but they do stack well and so if you're gonna play a rot style you need druid in your kit somewhere. Druid nukes are garbage. However, they have the only AoE nuke that doesn't have a longer reuse cooldown than cast time, which means they are the only class out of the gate that can AoE Spellblade.

replies.author: Kutsuu
replies.text: Their unbound nature crit buff combines well with any class, especially when you're combining nukes, dots, and melee in some way. The DS and regen buff plus AOEs gives a nice combo choice with anyone looking to make a defensive AOE farming build (warrior with cleave, bard AOEs, etc). Their HoT line works great without a snare or combat slow. It doesn't have the most obvious synergies like a shaman does, but it does have things beyond ports going for it that will be apparent as buildcrafting matures. I'm planning to try some combos like war/bst/dru, mnk/enc/dru, and war/brd/dru.

replies.author: Jokon
replies.text: Unbound Nature also works with heals.

replies.author: Juff
replies.text: The druid magic dot is the 3rd best dot in the game right now (behind only plague and ebolt). Overall, druid is a pretty strong choice to support most caster classes with spell crit/healing/extra pet inventory/the best pet haste. For melee you get healing/ds/ac/str.

replies.author: Juff
replies.text: Been playing dru/shm/mage. solo you do singles using mage pet to tank, in a group you do all the buffs, can lean on divine invocation to do a lot of healing, or fill more of a dps roll leveraging dots + mage nukes + pet

replies.author: rplumb
replies.text: I'll probably run something like paladin/beastlord/druid. 3 wis classes for divine. Bst gives duel wield the paladin lacks and pet is decent, as well as providing slow and some minor end/mana regen. Druid vs Shaman is a hard call but putting a bst in there at least will help you trick yourself into saying "it's already a shaman hybrid, there's too much overlap" so you can justify the Druid better lol. Druid vs shaman utility for melee is very different but probably similar in impact overall. Shaman dots are strong to the point that any comp I've played them in ends up feeling like a dot focused build, so they'll provide more damage overall. I know people say SHM is better but I felt that I'd rather save Shaman's Haste/Slows for another build since I had Enchanter and without those being part of the equation Druid is a lot more appealing. Besides the conveniences of teleports Druid offered: - The heals are solid. By end game I didn't have the normal healing line memorized. I just used the highest blooming HoT and while that was ticking I'd use Healing Waters (400ish heal base, 0.75s cast, 6s CD) it remains useful if you upgrade it a bit. - Passive crit chance on heals and direct damage spells. - Best self damage shield and decent DS on allies/pets. You'll be doing most of the tanking solo. - Tracking to help locate rares in zones like LGuk where there are a LOT of rares who all have placeholders. - Great pet buff with 10% more haste than even BST or MAG can give their pets (careful, BST will overwrite Druid bc it grants a little 20 ATK) - Atk buff from wolf form until you can unlock Garou on ENC - If you don't start Ogre you'll need a LOT of Fruit to unlock them and Forage is the only way to get it other than manually camping like 3 spawns. Create a forage/auto-inventory macro and assign to A and D, or even W.

Having expel summoned has been great in Najena. The Druid nukes are all more mana/DPS efficient than the ENC nukes. ENC DoTs, slow, mez and stun are great though. Taking down crowds hasn’t been an issue. I stopped worrying about Pacify. I typically throw a HoT on myself and engage a named with slow in defensive/inversion. Throw an PBAE stun and then AE mez when the room has piled up. Some random thoughts… Have only used motes so far on upgrading AE mez. Najena drops a good PAL 1H that I can’t use but my pet can. Druid doesn’t get many ports autogranted but it does get surefall glade, so if you go agnostic DEF ENC primary, wait until L15 to buy Druid spells and you can port to surefall glade and buy them, then origin back to Neriak to buy ENC spells, then gate back to Nektulos.

replies.author: Hoshimi
replies.text: MNK/DRU/BRD has been a really smooth leveling trio for me. Even against 5–6 red/yellow cons, BRD’s AE slow combined with MNK’s avoidance gives the group excellent survivability. DRU’s HoT feels much better to use than SHM’s, and its nukes are very mana-efficient too. The caster mobs in D2+ Lower Guk and Paw hit hard with their DD spells, and they definitely make me wish I had Mage Hunter. Still, HoTs and Healing Water have been enough to keep me alive so far. I’ve heard spell damage gets even nastier in Sky, so I’m not sure if this setup will keep holding up there. But for now, I’m having a blast.

replies.author: Kethigar
replies.text: Running the same combo and loving it. I highly recommend channeler stance any time you would want defensive or mage hunter. Other cool tricks: If you're in a pinch, you can FD to wait for the druid hot to pop. When charming, don't forget druid's 70% pet haste buff. Healing water is one of the best healing spells in the game. You can easily keep yourself healthy while sitting in recovery stance, restoring tons of mana. Brd/dru has some of the best end regen possible. Make good use of evasive stance. Combining improved mend, a hot pop, and healing water can put out a massive amount of healing at once. Bard lull + monk FD means every pull can be engaged on your terms.

1529740584602832936.title: Wizard viability in a trio
1529740584602832936.report:
Has anyone found that having a wizard as part of your trio of classes was a solid choice?

What Pros/Cons have you found with Wizard in EQL beyond "getting the ports" from the class?

replies.author: Viskar
replies.text: Wizard nukes are great starting around 15 and 18. 1-14 is a bit more of a slog for them. After 18 it's a pretty smooth leveling experience. You can dish out solid damage while also behind the safety of Defensive/Evasive/Channeler stance for mitigation. Mana Regen is nice to build into if you can group with bards/enchanters, or are yourself one of those or a necro. They do get +6(12 In Recovery) at level 45 with the familiar which helps a lot too. Unlike dot classes you can usually find a nuke or rain that works on each boss among their magic/fire/cold spells. Don't forget to grab Mana Pres and Improved Damage early in Blackburrow, helps a lot when you can rely on their Lv 18 nuke for a long time. I ran Pal/Wiz/Dru initially for ports, but ended up just taking it to 50. I didn't really use the Dru spells much so I think Pal/Wiz/Support would make it a solid combo.

replies.author: Tanasinn
replies.text: Pros: Nuking for 2500 in the mid-30s Cons: I guess they use mana, and need to use up motes. Did SK/Wiz/Cleric up to 43ish during the beta, had fun. Mostly relying heavily on wizard damage and crit nukes modified by AAs to just explode things. Spelledge could have me killing things the instant I turned on autoattack with sometimes double-crit-nuke-procs.

replies.text: What AAs did you acquire first and/or thought were best for this? What spells did you use with Spellblade?

replies.author: Tanasinn
replies.text: Crit %, Crit damage modifier. I just used strongest nuke for spellblade.

replies.author: Viskar

replies.author: dysnomia
replies.text: Bard/Wiz/Dru felt surprisingly good.

replies.author: Halfwise
replies.text: Wizards will carry any class trio pretty far, in my experience. The early porting unlock is convenient with rituals. And the spell tiers help significantly with the higher end resists that undermine wizard casting in the planes. I've also found a wizard nuking with Divine will outheal a ranger or beastlord.. so its a good consideration when paired with those classes.

replies.author: Snoji
replies.text: Played Wiz/Enc/Mag to 50 - didn't grind much on gear. I upgraded Mighty Mana Shock to 8 or so and that carried me hard to mid forty or so. At that point, investing in the mage pets became necessary to do any 'end game' bosses. My earth pet at the end was becoming a bit of a tank, soloing naggy with my pet heals and enc buffs. The trio was not strong compared to others, I reckon with maxxed out AAs and key spells like enc charm, this sort of trio would be able to clear 0 difficulty but without any real heals it has limited scope. The wizard was the most active part of the trio though, i imagine with upgraded ice comet you could do some serious dps and mixed in with tank and someway to regen mana & heal like a shm, would be pretty beasty.

replies.author: Halfwise
replies.text: Upgraded lightning bolt is definitely worth the motes. Let's you skip a few DD spells (~200dmg per cast at +4), fast, cheap, interrupts, and the 1.5s recast time on even the base spell outdoes any of the other "stun" spells Wizard has, that have reuse at 12s +. Because of its low cost / high damage / stun, it would be interesting if you are hyper intent on doing a spellblade build (various arguments against Spellblade set aside)

replies.author: Captain Kvass

Also how different just one class makes; so it is not out of what I would expect that people with various trios and comps are getting different results. I for example played Pal/Ber/Wiz and when I was on long fights I would sometimes need to mana up (say a d4 raid boss solo). I would pop in def stance, recovery invoc, turn off autoskill smite and go into a heal loop for a lil bit recovering mana. This is something that I was thinking would be cool to avoid by having a melee class so I swapped to rogue. I found that with Pal/Ber/Rog my endurance would drain so much faster than mana (regardless of pal/ber/wiz or pal/ber/rog) that I was getting better performance out of the wiz trio even though on paper rogue has no mana, and has slow from poisons + backstabs for mana free dmg. Just didn't meet what I expected. To me this is part of the great fun of this version of EQ. So many possibilities to try that have such nuanced interactions it is very challenging to be confident on how something will perform without actual empirical data from playing it. ------ That said, Ice Comet with Imp familiar and a few levels lands extremely reliably on Naggy d4 -- even before all of those things it works well. So not sure exactly your setup but I think if you went in without familiar at all and no debuffs to resist maybe that could explain what you saw. Could be that just in general you weren't 'ready' for d4 and doing it a bit early? However, if you were able to do it fine with druid then prob not the case.

replies.author: FatedEmperor
replies.text: Yeah, I am glad that people are finding better success with the wizard than I did. And I was also really shocked because my plan was to rely on the cleric for early leveling vs undead and then have the wizard carry. The druid had a fire and ice line but those couldn't be used on dragons, and then when I did master Yale the first time, I was just so used to relying on the druid's dot that I just relied on that after the first chain of spell resists from the wizard. If I were to include the wizard as part of a primary raiding trio I would probably try to pair it with the enchanter and shaman, or in a spell blade build. However, one thing that I learned from this beta is that currently, dots are just far more reliable baseline without any additional factors. replies.author: Vophren
replies.text: The real difficulty in the D4 raids is whether you can actually get to do the wizard thing or not. Which is entirely down to gear and AA. Wiz based builds have this exponential curve of how much damage they do and it's entirely dependent on how much time you can dedicate to casting nukes vs all the stuff you need to do to keep yourself alive. The tankier, healier, and better AA'd you are, the more time you spend dumping mana into their health bar. If you get things up to +8 and 150-200 AA you're going to be doing quite a bit very quickly.

1529732057922797731.title: Best Ranger Weapons?
1529732057922797731.report:
Title pretty much covers it!

What are the best current in game weapons a Ranger can acquire?

replies.author: Callius
replies.text: depends on other classes, but purely ranger would me erm, Sky sword (like mostly classes) , fear axe / yael dagger maybe. But likely other classes in your trio might have better

replies.author: Jokon
replies.text: Windstriker, Blessed Guardian Arrows, and Arydryidriyorn are the absolute best. There are great main hand weapons depending on how you multiclass, but these three are the best.

replies.author: Soransis
replies.text: You will want blessed champion arrows and blessed guardian arrows for your bow depending on the resists of the raid target

replies.author: Noxx
replies.text: For Wiz/Rng/bard . I'm planning Arydryidriyorn and revultant whip. My other two in my multiclass don't have strong weapons that I could find that beat out the rangers offerings.

replies.author: Jokon
replies.text: One of the neat itemization hacks that rangers unlock is the ability to have a decent white damage weapon in your bow and ranged stance, allowing you to put stat sticks into your primary and secondary slots. You can have two instruments AND still bow things down.

replies.author: Sips
replies.text: Rangers SHOULD be about their bows. Sadly, this isn't set up to let them shine.

replies.author: Jokon
replies.text: That's just an itemization hole at the moment. There aren't enough bows in game.

replies.author: ola
replies.text: I do not agree with the statement that rangers should be about their bows. Rangers should be proficient in both I always preferred meleeing on ranger, playstyle is excellent with a mix of spells and melee combat.

replies.author: GamerGramp
replies.text: Snare, snipe, melee, then when they run, shoot 'em in the back. (Dirty cowards.)

replies.author: Fest
replies.text: Both melee and ranged should be viable.

replies.author: Scuzzies
replies.text: I can’t imagine fluxbladed axe parses well at all. On a server with really high white damage and things like offensive stance, procs are going to be a much lower percentage of total dps.

replies.author: Saberine
replies.text: Come Kunark/Velious they get more bow options, and that will fix a lot of their ranged issues, (Better ratio or just raw damage bows will exist) Melee, they always outshine bows, just because that's how they were designed (There were a few expansions PoP being one of them where bow>Melee but they patched that either later in that expansion, or the next expansion) BUT if/once they get their cascade arrow line (spell that lets them either shoot an ae of 8 arrows in an arc infront of them or the focused line that hits a target with 8 arrows all at once) it gets a lot better Assuming they dont roll that spell into a stance effect

replies.author: ola
replies.text: being at 300 yards away, safe firing away with your bow should never out-dps being in there in melee taking aoe damage, and what not., imo but! it should be a nice alternative

replies.author: Dalor Darden🔮
replies.text: What is "White Damage"?

replies.author: Scuzzies
replies.text: Auto attack damage.

replies.author: ManiiNames (5k2k Club)
replies.text: It's white in the chat window, thus the name

replies.author: serrasin
replies.text: The problem with archery is that on a server where you can solo face tank multiple red mobs, dealing damage at a distance isnt a distinct advantage, especially when it competes with melee that every other white damage based class uses (outside niche uses obv).

replies.author: serrasin
replies.text: probably the second melee weapon will be either a sky 1h from one of your other classes, or the scimitar off of inny.

replies.author: ManiiNames (5k2k Club)
replies.text: Archery is good for spellweaving, because bows are slow but high damage. You can pretty easily cast between shots without delaying the autoattacks, which is extremely hard if you are dual wielding. Also there are a bunch of things which multiply your white damage with archery.

replies.author: ManiiNames (5k2k Club)
replies.text: Baseline archery is 2H without base damage boosting for player level. Very streaky, you can hit for 1 damage or you can hit for 300 damage. - If you're a ranger, you deal double damage to any mob that isn't moving. Rooted or otherwise. So that 2x - With AA, you can double it again, resulting in a damage range of 4 to 1200 to keep the math - Ranged Stance allows you to double and triple attack, assuming you have unlocked those skills. This is how ranger damage with archery works - you can single hit for 4 damage, or triple for 1200-1200-1200 (before crit)

replies.author: Jokon
replies.text: Fluxbladed Axe exists to be leveled up to where you can steal the proc off it and give to a different weapon.

replies.author: serrasin
replies.text: take the fluxblade proc and stick it into Briarzephyr off Inny.

replies.author: Jokon
replies.text: That's the idea, yes. There's a 4/28 weapon in Kunark that procs Conflagarate (900 damage).

replies.author: serrasin
replies.text: ranged stance needs tuning. imho just fold it into the aa. also, the double damage vs stationary needs to be enabled against rooted mobs. maybe make that an aa as well.

replies.author: Diogenes
replies.text: That was already changed, you get (Double Bow Shot) on rooted targets in EQL.

replies.author: Jokon
replies.text: Yeah, that's already in. Rooted targets take double damage.

replies.author: serrasin
replies.text: oh i missed that, when was it changed?

replies.author: ManiiNames (5k2k Club)
replies.text: I had fun doing a root-rot Ranger-NEC-Druid combo. Worked pretty well. Druid AA helped the root stick.

replies.author: Nicolai
replies.text: Rangers aren’t working currently

replies.author: serrasin
replies.text: ranger is the best kept secret on EQL. a lot of players arent aware of all the buffs the class has enjoyed.

replies.author: Jokon
replies.text: The root change was a while back. It never had an official natch pote

replies.author: ManiiNames (5k2k Club)
replies.text: I remember Ailia just mentioning it one day when we asked

replies.author: serrasin
replies.text: ah, thats why i missed it. i just never tested root/shoot. well that good then, actually opens up some useful gameplay loops for archery

replies.author: serrasin
replies.text: ranged stance still sucks on your endurance hard enough to pull a golf ball through a garden hose.

replies.author: Dalor Darden🔮
replies.text: When you say double damage, rooted or "otherwise" what exactly do you mean? Like if combat hasn't started?

replies.author: ManiiNames (5k2k Club)
replies.text: If you are in melee and the mob is just standing there unmoving and hitting you, it is unmoving Or in a group, and your tank is holding aggro, it is unmoving. Or if you root it, it is unmoving.

replies.author: Dalor Darden🔮
replies.text: I didn't know that Rangers did double damage like that...

replies.author: ManiiNames (5k2k Club)
replies.text: if you are fear-kiting / snare-kiting it is moving, and that multiplier does not apply. The doubling is only w bows, and only for rangers

replies.author: serrasin
replies.text: yeah. traditionally the way rangers would do double damage with archery while solo is to root one mob and face tank another. you target the rooted mob, but since arrows are projectiles then they hit intervening mobs, which would be the one you are face tanking. it would then check for the double damage on the tanked mob and it would be stationary, but not rooted. all of that is no longer required in EQL.

replies.author: ManiiNames (5k2k Club)
replies.text: Main issue is the wide damage range. Do anywhere from 1-300 on your shot, multiplied up to 4-1200. Then Ranged stance gives double attack and then transitions to triple attack when you hit L46.

replies.author: Diogenes
replies.text: Yeah, getting a single digit crit with a weapon you know can crit for 1000 does make you sad.

replies.author: serrasin
replies.text: well there are four main issues with ranged currently. - ranged stance potentially locks out other stances. - ranged stance consumes a lot of endurance, in part because archery is slow but hits hard. - lack of itemization - archery doesnt always synergize with buffs and features of other melee classes

replies.author: serrasin
replies.text: I do love how on EQL your character will auto-magically swap between melee weapons and archery as you move in/out of melee range. that helps minimize lost engagement damage.

replies.author: ManiiNames (5k2k Club)
replies.text: 1. Yes, but yiou will either choose the thing which does the most damage or something which keeps you alive. True for all combos. 2. Yes, but you have buil in endurance regen. And it consumes more like Offensive than Striker so I found it OK. 3. Low level bows kinda suck, this is true. But the arrows are great. If you make good arrows even the Sabretooth Bow starts to look decent. Otherwise yes, you want Windstriker. This itemization is a known issue and will eventually be fixed. 4. Archery doesn't work w buff proc effects designed for melee, this is true 5. Auto-swap is great

replies.author: serrasin
replies.text: yeah. i think the general consensus is focus on melee until max level (if its your first playthrough), then once you can get windstriker and a fleeting quiver then buy into the AA and incorporate archery where it makes sense.

replies.author: Jokon
replies.text: Another perk of archery is that unlike melee damage, it isn't level capped. You can still hit mobs for 1000 damage if you delevel a loadout to 10.

replies.author: Diogenes
replies.text: I would argue the single biggest problem is the variance and floor. Lack of damage bonus and it would seem that Dex doesn't have any effect on ranged create drag on averaged performance. The other issues do compound but aren't too far outside of what other aspects of the game deal with. I will say that while itemization is boring....in beta I had Trueshot on 2 characters at level 16 and level 10 that I used motes up to +4 and combined with even a low end arrow can be a 32/45 weapon to elvel with.

replies.author: ManiiNames (5k2k Club)
replies.text: It costs ~1200pp or so to make your first Mithril arrow +0. I think a +5 arrow and the Sabretooth or a Darkwood bow is quite compaable even when you have much better melee weapons. Plus Archery is fun.

replies.author: serrasin
replies.text: trueshot/shabertooth bows are still valuable for leveling, if for no other reason than Distracting Shot and pulling.

replies.author: serrasin
replies.text: i personally dont see a huge difference in fun between archery or melee; maybe the big crits if thats your jam. its great to have as an option and I want it to be viable, just never wanted it to be the only flavor of ranger.

replies.author: ManiiNames (5k2k Club)
replies.text: Setup Bow Stats Arrow Combined Ratio Sabertooth Short Bow +5 9/30 17 + 3 fire 29/30 0.967 Darkwood Compound Bow +5 28/41 17 + 3 fire 48/41 1.171 Windstriker +5 (Plane of Sky) ~67/60 17 + 3 fire 87/60 1.450

replies.text: #'s are wih a super-chaievable +5 bow and +5 arrow. Anyone serious about archery will end up with a +10 arrow but that's a hella lot of money early.

replies.author: serrasin
replies.text: the ratio value for archery has always been somewhat deceptive because it's less direct translation of power as compared to melee. its still an indicator, but gotta keep in mind things like quiver haste and damage doubling scaling. (and huge hit variance)

replies.author: ManiiNames (5k2k Club)
replies.text: Yep, but it's a number. And people are used to looking at a ratio.

replies.author: serrasin
replies.text: yeah, i didnt want to undermine the value of your information. I just wanted to add context to it with an asterisk

replies.author: Diogenes
replies.text: The double damage for still targets is the bandaid that was put in place to account for the the fact that bow damage isn't doubled in it's normal calculation like melee is.

replies.author: ManiiNames (5k2k Club)
replies.text: The interesting thing is it shows how much the arrows impact fast bows, like the Sabretooth. It's kind of a cappy bow at 6 base damage, but the 30 delay means the arrow bonuses are incredibly magnified.

replies.author: Jokon
replies.text: All weapon damage upgrades, arrows included, are 10% per level. Where it gets squirrely is that higher levels allow for *partial* upgrades. Going from +0 to +1 is instantly 10%. However, from +5 to +6 you will get some degree of upgrade based on how far along you actually are. This also applies in reverse; if you have a weapon with *less than 10* base damage, then you may need multiple levels to see a damage boost.

1529731623229329478.title: Meshing the Paladin with 2 Other Classes
1529731623229329478.report:
Personally, I am hoping to end up with Paladin/Enchanter/Ranger as my three main classes after leveling Druid and then Wizard to about 25 each.

From a Roleplaying angle I have all that figured out as to "why" for my character.

But what I'm hoping to do here is discuss how the various classes mesh with the Paladin as an anchor for armor, healing, and general "tankiness" when mixed with other classes.

Anyone care to offer their input on a Paladin/Enchanter/Ranger for Pros and Cons?

What about other trios? I've seen MANY Paladin/Monk/Enchanters out there!

Thanks for anything you have to offer!

replies.author: 👻🏳️‍🌈Spooky🦇Bird🏳️‍🌈🎃
replies.text: I'm running pal rng rog as my primary, but I might also swap for pal rng enc or pal rog enc depending on dps. Paladin alone is conceptually a trifecta of tanking, healing and dps versus undead. Our knight swords allow us to push physical damage with dw above and beyond. Our plate armor is some of the most tanky in the game, and we boast a robust set of shields to pick from to boost the ac soft cap with. I initially ran pal rng rog on the other server, because those three classes all had boosts to proc chance available as aa's.

replies.author: 👻🏳️‍🌈Spooky🦇Bird🏳️‍🌈🎃
replies.text: Rng grants ambidexterity and a massive amount of accuracy + atk, track, and ambidex. Rog gets 4 procs on hit, backstab via the any slot, the rog exclusive armors from planars, sneak and hide, and ambidex. I'd say that enc would probably be better than rog due to the utility of Ally, Charm, illusions, pet, runes, dots, tash and mana buffs. You also probably get to dip into spell empowerment AA's in the endgame. Paladin is an incredible anchor class - one of the best imho. I hold a unique attachment to pal since i picked it at 3 y.o when little me was playing eq for the first time ages ago hehe.

replies.author: 👻🏳️‍🌈Spooky🦇Bird🏳️‍🌈🎃
replies.text: I've seen pal pair relatively well with wizard, because pal provides a strong face and robust heal ability, esp with loh. I think pal rng with ambidex and slay undead will be sufficient, though. May I hear about the RP reason? I also love rping my pally.

replies.author: Dalor Darden🔮
replies.text: Arawn will begin as an Enchanter/Ranger (with Druid then Wizard to mid 20s) before becoming a Paladin. He is invested in his connection to the Greater Faydark and that is why he is a hunter and explorer (ranger) as well as being magically inclined. Drawing closely to the Wood Elves and their conflict with the Crushbone Clan will pull him deeper into the wilds (as a Druid); but eventually he begins to desire more raw power to fight the horde (by becoming a wizard); before finally succumbing to his desire to be a leader and be able to stand fully in the line of battle while doing so (becoming a Paladin). That is the line I have envisioned at any rate.

replies.author: 👻🏳️‍🌈Spooky🦇Bird🏳️‍🌈🎃

replies.author: Shinra Kuonji (Twice Punished)
replies.text: To clarify: Ranger attack buffs (and attack buffs in general, including increases from Strength) don't impact accuracy. That is purely a function of your Offense and appropriate weapon skill compared to the target's Evasion AC. But they do shift the bell curve on your damage rolls to the right, so you see more max hits and less minimum hits.

replies.author: Jokon
replies.text: I don't have the *current* code but what's been sussed out over the years is that charm breaks are triggered for two reasons; first, there's a basic chance to break charms that is flat. Second, every tick (six seconds) the charm makes another magic resist check just like when you first cast. If that core system has changed then my info is out of date. When you level a charm spell, both checks are easier. The flat break chance is reduced to zero at +10. The second is easier because the innate MR you're checking against is lower and lower per spell level.

1529725911300313128.report:
I am more into roleplaying than mechanics in this game.

However, having said that, I feel that a Ranger should know how to quickly dispatch a foe...and that translates into doing as much damage as quickly as possible.

Would those who know the ins and outs of the mechanics mind explaining the best way to achieve DPS with a Ranger?

I'll rationalize it via my own stories/roleplaying while in the game.

replies.author: TaurenMoo
replies.text: Depends on your build. Generally depends on the situation and classes. I'm personally going for a mixed spell blade but other classes are gonna do more white damage, just depends.

replies.text: Aye...I'm primarily talking purely about Ranger AAs, weapons, and etc. Personally I'll be eventually going to Enchanter/Paladin/Ranger after leveling Druid and Wizard...but I'm trying to decipher the individual classes and then I can make a more informed decision on how to integrate them.

replies.author: TaurenMoo
replies.text: most of the ranger AA's don't actually cost anything, all the basic attack buffs they get through AA's. But if you're more melee focused likely the basic crit node. IF you wanna go bows the focus should be the bow AA's and getting a good bow (theres a number of options faydark, trueshot, etc.) and a good arrow (Fletching or farming)

replies.author: TaurenMoo
replies.text: I have been testing a more spell focused build that weaves spells inbetween attacks at any range (spell blade + fire arrow line <ranger spell> + big nuke class <magician in my build>) but there are lots of good combos that can easily mix in spell casting.

replies.author: TaurenMoo
replies.text: Generally lean towards a 2 hander in most cases. I'm not sure ambi does enough for dual wielding to be really valuable until you get higher end weapons and even then may not be worth it based on old information about how bad ambidextrous is without the later AA points. hopefully that helps

replies.author: Dalor Darden🔮
replies.text: It really does help, thank you so much!

replies.author: Jokon
replies.text: Ranger physical DPS differs from other individual class picks in that you innately gain attack power and strike through capacity through enemy defenses. This means that your *average* damage is higher, more consistent. You won't have big sexy back stabs or smites or what have you, but you will miss less and make more of potential. Spell wise, you also have a new Arrow line of damage that is respectable. You just hammer it on cool down, it's a bit brainless tbh. Finally, archery. It is highly gear dependent, and doesn't really get amazing until the end game bow Windstriker. It also suffers from roulette syndrome; unlike your melee which has a minimum damage buffer archery can hit for 1 damage. Repeatedly. It can also triple strike for 1000 per hit. Over long fights that averages out but short fights it's going to be literally hit or miss.

replies.author: Cyanide Bunnyslayer
replies.text: BST/MAG/NEC is a spellblade build with a strong pet. The right way to play this build is to co-tank with the pet, run in and Auto attack, and fire off dots/nukes/debuffs. Proper positioning is key, you always want to turn mobs such that you surround them with your pet. Either you are attacking from the rear or your pet is, no need for both of you to eat cleaves and ripostes. Any pet in this trio works well, but for pure tanking the earth pet wins slightly in the defenses. Water pet is THE premier DPS pet and should be used when you don't need maximum defenses. Air pet was meh when dungeon crawling, but 1-on-1 it should be fine. Fire pet was LOL on beta. BST pet didn't keep up with mage pets after level 20ish (and requires HEAVY mote investment) but Necro skelly boy was excellent in my testing. Sometimes I preferred it over Earth pet, especially soloing high yellows and reds. Always run Arcane Mastery invocation. Unlike many other builds, this build also has Evasive Stance. Alternate between Offensive Stance and Evasive Stance as the situation dictates. When your pet dies, ALWAYS pop Evasive and Inversion to get the pet back out asap. Then switch back to Arcane once the pet is alive and has aggro again.

replies.author: Cyanide Bunnyslayer

replies.author: Cactot
replies.text: Nukes aren't particularly under tuned, they just require more intention to build around. Nukes get absolutely silly with upgrades and doubly so with the AM invocation. Lava bolt X does 1307 damage before spell focuses or crits or invocations, and it's actually *more* mana efficient than the best end game dots similarly upgraded. With spell focuses and crits (not including wizard or druid bonuses) you are looking at like 1850ish damage on average every 5 seconds for a respectable 370 or so DPS, but even with AM2 that bumps up to over 530 DPS, and with AM3 it's over 600 DPS. Then add your pet and damage shields and you are looking at one of the highest DPS outputs possible in the game right now. It's also much better than dots in non-raid situations because the damage is front loaded and comes online instantly.

replies.author: Cactot
replies.text: The best mage DD and the best wizard DD are very similar in output, the mage is just slightly less mana efficient. The big game changer for wizards is that their rains are amazing, and the mage ones are awful

replies.author: Juff
replies.text: You basically just restated what I already said. also all DD's scale the same way, so the amount of damage the nukes scale to is irrelevant. The issue is pretty straight forward: even the best "nuke" (frost storm) is less efficient than most of the good dots, and its less damage per unit of cast time than the first 8 dots. And frost storm is wildly better than any other nuke in the game. This mostly leads the role of nukes to being "Cast these on things that are going to die faster than your dots will run their course, or when you have no dots to cast and mana isn't an issue". This is not exactly inspiring. And then mage nukes are even worse than the wizard spells, their pets are not particularly stronger than other pets, and summons are limited in usefulness. The only things they get that are unique to them that are good across the board are: frenzied companion (~25% more pet melee dps. this is pretty good!), and the 6% pet crit aa (this is very minor). If you are just trying to play the game for fun, mage is perfectly fine, it's not going to stop you from doing content. If you want to maximize a characters power, there's just not a lot of reason to select a mage.

replies.author: Cactot
replies.text: Frost storm is not less efficient than dots though? It's 5.6 dpm against single targets without upgrades, compared to E bolt at 5.1 dpm. The gap gets bigger with upgrades because nukes scale more aggressively on both damage and cost. Fully upgraded lava bolt has an incredible 13.7 dpm with no AA or focuses, because nuke cost scaling is absolutely ridiculous (-6% per level) Yes, nukes are more damage per cast, but they actually end up less efficient than top tier nukes because they don't have the same type of outrageous cost reduction from upgrades.

replies.author: Juff
replies.text: There are other dots than ebolt. Its less efficient than plague, malaria, gasping embrace. Also dots get the same mana cost reduction as nukes 2% per rank. They get less damage per rank because they also gain extra duration, which is just another damage scaling vector

replies.author: Juff
replies.text: Dots actually scale better than nukes. Dots get 3% damage per rank vs 6%, but 5% duration. At rank ten a dot gets 50% more duration (which is effectively just 50% more damage if the enemy lives long enough) and 30% more damage. 1.5 * 1.3 is 95% more damage, vs 60% from nukes.

replies.text: Aoe mez lets you freeze what would otherwise be a wipe pull of 9+ mobs into a "one at a time" encounter. Dots break mez. You cannot hurt them or aoe them down. It's effectively just forcing yourself to have a really good pull. It's great at what it does. It's *INCREDIBLY* clutch, and it's right up there with ice comet X crits, and a 2% hp LoH clutch in terms of satisfaction per cast / dopamine per spell. But it does literally nothing for dragonslaying. It does precisely what it needs to. It's perfectly balanced, and strong. It's one of my favorite spells in the game.

replies.author: 👻🏳️‍🌈Spooky🦇Bird🏳️‍🌈🎃

replies.author: malkavon
replies.text: It's this. If you want to talk about "OP", Whirl Till You Hurl lets you kill literally anything susceptible to it (which is most things that aren't giants/dragons, CT/Inny, and a few of the Planes minis) provided you're willing to put in the time. AOE Mez just ensures you're only ever fighting one thing, but if you can't actually kill that one thing, it does literally nothing to advance the situation. Whirl Till You Hurl lets you actually kill things that would otherwise turn you into paste - I was killing D4 ghoul lord in LGuk at like 36, so 11 levels below him, without being at meaningful risk thanks to Whirl

replies.author: malkavon
replies.text: That isn't to say AOE Mez isn't strong, it absolutely is, because ensuring every fight is a 1 v 1 is already a *massive* advantage, it's just not autowinning every fight on its own. You need *something* else to actually close each mob out

replies.author: Rahz
replies.text: Enc is the class you play for doing d4 dungeons since it has everything you need to succeed. It's almost like the higher dungeon difficulties were designed having an enc in group, kind of like original EQ. If you're simply facerolling in d0, any combo works. As far an individual abilities, AE mez is obviously very strong on d4. But for d0 it is simply a convenience, and also allows you to take on higher con camps for more regular xp, at the cost of less AAxp. Definitely helpful for levelling quickly. Whirl till You Hurl--my memory might be off, but pretty sure in original EQ the stun had a high chance to wear off from damage, so it could not be used to perma stun lock while attacking the target, unlike EQL. It gives the option to run non-standard trios like no-healer, which I think is neat. In any event, it has no bearing on the raid game since it doesn't land on raid bosses. If WTYH is adjusted it wont be a big deal as far as spell casting since enc has other ways to interrupt spells. Charm--this one has always been a balancing act in nearly every version of EQ. For the levelling game it seems irrelevant, since again, who cares. But if it gets a significant nerf, it will effect the raid game. Worse case scenario enc becomes worthless for raid bosses and instead your default slower is mostly shaman, with some bards, and the occasional beastlord. Why have an enc to slow with minimal dps when you can run shaman that can also heal and dps?

replies.text: As a long time monk/melee type, I "heard" about things like stun lock over the years, and I understood the concept, but never rolled a class that could employ it. That is, until Eql. I did the whole whirl till you hurl stun lock strategy. And, It works. But, it's a one trick pony. If you do it, then it's "all" you do. There's no time to do anything else. Cast/melee/cooldown/recast/melee/rinse/repeat/.. And what I found, (based on the mob respawn timers of the camp I was in when I tested), was that it was just over a 2:1 tradeoff. For the same mana/hp's, I could kill two mobs and be engaged with the third, in the same amount of time that it took me to kill just the one with stun lock. Note that I had only upgraded the whirl spell to "next to highest level". Maybe being fully upgraded, having that final level, is an absolute game changer, game breaker, that I'm simply not aware of.

replies.author: Nate
replies.text: Race: Dwarf Class: Pally/Necro/Monk Pally for the self-healing, plate armor, stun, aggro control, LoH, slay undead, Hp and Ac buffs Necro for the life tap, life tap over time, darkness ranged snares, mana regen, and the PET! Monk for the avoidance, sustained meleee dps, mobility, Feign death, dual wield, run speed, split pulling, mend, shuriken of death I still remember buying the disk for EQ from blockbuster, taking the game home and installing it. I remember every hair on my body standing up when I realized I was to actually talking to other people in a video game. Then the second day I was playing when I asked someone next to me how to do something and he told me to type /duel so I did, it was at that exact moment, the moment my lifeless body hit the grass that I both fell in love with and hated online gamming at the exact same time. I was completely hooked! This was back in February of 2000. Here it is twenty six years later and I still remember that day like it was yesterday. I started printing hundreds of pages of maps and mob locations punched them and put them in binders. Im telling you the money that I spent on printer ink alone almost caused a divorce.

replies.author: steelbeamz
replies.text: How EQL macros work (quick primer) EverQuest Legends includes a macro system for batches of up to 5 /commands set to a hotkey — but they're simple scripting, not code: no loops, no conditionals. You build them via the Actions window (EQL button → Actions > Actions, default keybind "L"), under the Macros tab. Same pause rules as classic: /pause goes at the beginning of a line followed by a comma (e.g. /pause 10, /assist), the number is tenths of a second, and the pause executes after the matching command. One important gotcha for combat macros: while a macro with pauses is running, no other macros can be activated — so keep your emergency buttons pause-free. If a macro is stuck mid-sequence, /stopsocial cancels it. eqlwiki + 3 Two nice EQL features: /cast accepts either a gem slot number or the name of a memorized spell, with partial names accepted — so /cast Charm keeps working even if you rearrange gems — and you can slap /timer XXX on a button for a visual cooldown, though the timer is purely visual and activates whether the command succeeds or fails. eqlwiki eqlwiki Recharm / initial charm (one button) /pet leave /attack off /cast Charm (or your gem slot #) /timer 600 Same dual-purpose logic as before — /pet leave is a valid EQL pet command, so this releases-and-recharms if you have a pet and just charms if you don't. The /timer line is a Legends-specific trick: set it near your charm's expected duration and the button itself becomes a rough "charm might break soon" gauge. Just remember it's cosmetic — actual charm duration varies with resists.

replies.author: steelbeamz
replies.text: Charm break panic button (no pauses!) /attack off /cast Stun (or your mez) Keep this one pause-free so it can never be blocked by another running macro. Stun/mez first, then hit the recharm button. Pet attack /pet attack Pet back off for OOC healing EQL's syntax is /pet back, not /pet back off: "back" makes the pet clear its hatelist. The full parking macro: eqlwiki /pet back /pet hold /pet guard here Legends has the full pet discipline suite baseline — and actually something better for charm pets: "ghold" (greater hold) means the pet will only attack something new if ordered and will not build a hate list of other mobs. Regular "hold" won't start attacks until ordered, but once attacking it builds a hate list and attacks other mobs as usual. For a charmed pet in a multi-mob camp, ghold is the safer default — it stops your pet from wandering onto your mezzed mobs. Consider setting /pet ghold right after every successful charm. Also worth adding /pet no taunt once per charm if you don't want it ripping aggr

replies.author: steelbeamz
replies.text: Autoattack safety — one Legends-specific gotcha Beyond keeping /attack off at the top of your mez macro, check this: /assist can toggle auto-attack on assist with [on|off]. Type /assist off once — otherwise every time you assist your tank onto a target, autoattack can flip on automatically, which is exactly how enchanters faceplant into mezzed mobs. This is the single most important safety setting for you. eqlwiki Your mez macro: /attack off /cast Mez /g Mezzing %T << DO NOT BREAK >> Note the variables are capitalized in EQL: %T is your current target by name, and %M is your pet's name. So a charm announce looks like /g Attempting to charm %T! — the wiki literally uses charming as its example, so the devs know their audience'

replies.author: steelbeamz
replies.text: A few more Legends-specific tips /pet target targets your pet, or F1 toggles between you and your pet — handy for checking charm status fast. /pet regroup makes the pet return to you whether its target is alive or not, without clearing its hatelist — useful mid-fight repositioning, but for true OOC healing you want back since the hate list is what matters. And /xtarget (extended target window) is worth setting up to watch your mezzed mobs' status at a glance. eqlwiki eqlwiki One thing I couldn't verify yet: whether charm mechanics themselves (break behavior, pet damage tables, weapon handoffs) work like classic EQ — the game is literally a day old and the wiki is still in beta, so test carefully before trusting your pet in a dungeon. Also keep in mind EQL's multiclass system means your "enchanter" is one of up to three classes — if one of your other classes has any stun or root, that's extra charm-break insurance worth hotkeying right next to your recharm button.
